# SP3 Sessions Engine Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Give every agent its own real terminal inside Agent OS. A person picks an agent and a folder, and the agent's own TUI runs exactly as it does in Terminal.app. The terminal keeps running when the window closes, is recorded (output only), and can be stopped, resumed and reattached. Quitting asks first when sessions are live.

**Architecture:** A new server module `server/runtime/sessions/` spawns each agent in a PTY (`node-pty`), with the user's login-shell environment (H2) and only additive launch options (H3). A headless xterm mirror keeps every session's screen, so any window can reattach through a WebSocket (`/api/sessions/:id/attach`, its own upgrade security). An asciicast recorder keeps the output. The Sessions page shows the terminals with `@xterm/xterm` 6.1 in tabs, with a side panel. On macOS the desktop shell hides the window instead of quitting; ⌘Q and the Quit item ask the UI before a quit, and every quit stops the server gracefully through its stdin.

**Tech Stack:** Node 24 + Express 4 (server), `node-pty` 1.2.0-beta.14, `@xterm/headless` 6.1.0-beta.303 + `@xterm/addon-serialize` 0.15.0-beta.301 + `@xterm/addon-unicode11` 0.10.0-beta.301 (server mirror), `ws` 8.22.0, React 18 + Vite + TypeScript (UI), `@xterm/xterm` 6.1.0-beta.304 and the add-ons built from the same xterm.js commit (decision Q42), Tauri 2 (desktop shell, Rust) with `tauri-plugin-dialog` 2.8.3 and `@tauri-apps/api` 2.12.1, `node --test` (tests, under the new no-real-agents watcher and the fake login shell), the Playwright-core audit harness (`.superpowers/ui-audit/`).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-cobalt-redesign-and-real-terminals-design.md`, section "SP3 Sessions engine and page", with the harness rules H1-H9, "Testing and verification", "Dependencies and packaging" and "Risks". The spec is binding; this plan argues from it.

**Prototype (owner-approved, the visual target):** `~/MediaStudio/runs/2026-10-10-agent-os-redesign/prototype/` (`sessions.html`, `index.html` for the New session dialog, `runs.html`, `agents.html`, `how-it-works.html`, `shared/cobalt.css`, `shots/*.png`). Build to match it with real data, never its sample data. To view it live: `cd ~/MediaStudio/runs/2026-10-10-agent-os-redesign/prototype && python3 -m http.server 4610 --bind 127.0.0.1`.

**Builds on:** SP1 (shell and tokens) and SP2 (core pages), both done and pushed through `8264b2b`. The SP2 ledger, with its rulings and parked minors, is at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-12-sp2-core-pages/progress.md`.

## Global Constraints

- **Harness fidelity (spec H1-H4), for every session:**
  - run the user's installed binary (path from `server/runtime/agents/detect.js`) with the user's real HOME and config; never set or change `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `HERMES_HOME` or any OpenClaw state or profile variable;
  - the environment is the login-shell environment minus `AGENT_OS_*`, `HERMES_AGENT_OS_*` and the nested-session markers (`CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` until spikes S3 and S6), plus `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`, `TERM_PROGRAM=AgentOS`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION`, `AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID`, and `PWD` set to the session's folder (decision Q7a); `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1` only with the fullscreen opt-in; never `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB`, never `TERM_PROGRAM=vscode`, no hook variables in SP3;
  - values Agent OS added itself never reach a session: the desktop shell passes `AGENT_OS_PORT`, never `PORT`, and the keys of Agent OS's own env file, and what npm added when an npm script started Agent OS, are kept out of what goes into the login shell (decision Q11a, Task S2);
  - argv only, never a shell; only the H3 additions; never `--bare`, `--disable-slash-commands`, `--strict-mcp-config`, a replacing `--mcp-config`, `--accept-hooks`, `--yolo`, `--trust`, `--no-alt-screen`, a forced `--tui`, or any permission-bypass, dangerous or full-access flag;
  - never a write to an agent's own config files.
- **The only bytes ever written into a PTY:** the writer's input (keys, paste and its terminal's automatic query replies) and the mirror's replies to the standard terminal queries while no writer is attached. Stop never types into a PTY. (SP4 adds the hand-off text under its own rules.)
- **Folders:** a session folder passes the folder policy (D12, `folders.js`); sessions never use `resolveRunCwd`. Runs stay sandboxed as today.
- **Files on disk:** `AGENT_OS_HOME`, `sessions/` and `worktrees/` are 0700 (chmod when they exist); recordings, `meta.json`, `config/sessions.json` and the per-session Claude settings file are 0600. Recordings hold output only, never input.
- **Local mode only:** every sessions and recordings route answers 404 `not_available`, and every sessions WebSocket upgrade is refused with 403 like any other failed upgrade (spec Security 1), unless Agent OS runs in local mode (not demo-public, not `HERMES_AGENT_OS_REQUIRE_AUTH=1`, not `HERMES_AGENT_OS_PUBLIC_MODE=1`).
- **Packages (the list the owner approved on 2026-10-14, with the `@xterm/headless` and add-on numbers corrected by decision Q42; exact pins only, all in `dependencies`):**
  - Task W0: `node-pty@1.2.0-beta.14` (a normal dependency, decision Q43), `ws@8.22.0`, `@xterm/xterm@6.1.0-beta.304`, `@xterm/headless@6.1.0-beta.303`, `@xterm/addon-serialize@0.15.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-fit@0.12.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-unicode11@0.10.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-search@0.17.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-web-links@0.13.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-clipboard@0.3.0-beta.303`, `@xterm/addon-webgl@0.20.0-beta.300`. These xterm numbers are the set built from one xterm.js commit (decision Q42); the orchestrator records the owner's yes to them in the ledger before W0 runs, and W0 stops if that line is missing.
  - Task D1, in one step: `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog@2.8.3` and `@tauri-apps/api@2.12.1` (the version already in `package-lock.json`, decision Q6), with the crate `tauri-plugin-dialog = "2"` (Cargo.lock resolves 2.8.3). U1 only checks they are present.
  - Nothing else is installed. `tauri-plugin-notification` waits for SP4.
- **Copy:**
  - plain English, sentence case; no em dash in visible text;
  - "—" means unknown and "…" means loading;
  - every sentence must be true in SP3: no alerts, waiting, held, split, hand-off, replay player or worktree offer promises (those are SP4);
  - the strings in "Planning decisions" below are verbatim;
  - D11: no UI text may say that Hold to stop all (or the palette's "Stop all agent work") stops the Hermes background service or the OpenClaw Gateway.
- **SP2 lessons (P26), in every UI task:** stale data sits under a warn note; every request has a time limit (`withTimeout` in `src/ui/homeShared.ts`); unmount guards, and never `navigateTo` after unmount; never throw away typed text; the main action is on screen at 1280×720; long text wraps or ends in "…"; focus moves into a dialog and back to its opener.
- **Design (unchanged from SP2):** only the tokens in `src/ui/tokens.css`, no new colour literals; one cobalt accent for the primary action, the live state and the focus ring; status is an icon plus a word; motion 120–200 ms with `var(--os-ease-out)`, off under `prefers-reduced-motion`; Archivo for the UI, JetBrains Mono for data and the terminal (13 px); breakpoints: off-canvas menu ≤ 900 px, 64 px icon rail 901–1366 px, full sidebar ≥ 1367 px; window minimum 1024×640; no sideways scroll.
- **Inventory behaviours that must keep working:** everything listed in the SP2 plan's Global Constraints (palette focus trap, Escape closes the menu, `aria-current`, rail tooltips, `#os-get-started`, `data-density`, 5 s polling through `useInterval`, modal title ids, the `test/release-config.test.js` window minimums and pinned capabilities).
- **Tests:**
  - the full suite is `env -u HERMES_HOME npm test`, which from Task W1 runs under the no-real-agents watcher and must end with zero violations;
  - the `grep -E '^# (tests|pass|fail|skipped)'` checks need the TAP reporter. Run them with the worktree's `node` (`node --version` prints v22 here). On Node 23 or newer, add `--test-reporter=tap` to `node --test` (for `npm test`, pass `npm test -- --test-reporter=tap`);
  - fakes only (`test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs` through `test/helpers/fake-agents.js`, and the existing fakes); temp `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`/`AGENT_OS_HOME` in tests only (real paths);
  - the fake login shell (decision Q1c): `test/fakes/login-shell.sh`, exported as `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL`, is the only `SHELL` any test uses. `scripts/run-tests.mjs` sets it and removes `ZDOTDIR`, `ENV` and `BASH_ENV` for the whole run, and every test that starts `server/index.js` also sets `SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` itself. Never `SHELL=/bin/sh` (a real login `sh` runs macOS's `path_helper`, which puts the folders where real agents live ahead of the fakes). Only the tests whose subject is a slow, noisy or failing login shell (S2, S8) pass their own fake shell, and S3's profile tests use a wrapper that only exports variables and prepends a PATH folder before it execs `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` (plus a missing shell for its fallback test);
  - `PATH` in any test that can start a session is the fake bin folder plus `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` only, and that fake bin holds all six names (`claude`, `codex`, `agent`, `cursor-agent`, `hermes`, `openclaw`);
  - UI tasks also pass `npx tsc -b`, `npm run build` and their audit probes.
- **Audit harness:** `node .superpowers/ui-audit/audit.mjs <mode>` or `node .superpowers/ui-audit/audit.mjs probe .superpowers/ui-audit/probes/<name>.mjs` from the worktree root (pass the probe path as its own argument). It starts a throwaway server on :8791 with a real-path temp HOME, the fake login shell, and the six TUI-like fake agent shims in `.superpowers/ui-audit/fake-bin/` (Task U1 sets these up with the first session probe; decision Q2). Run one at a time; make sure nothing is left on :8791 afterwards.
- **Workers:**
  - never commit, push, tag or set `CI=true`;
  - never start a real agent;
  - never read `.env` files or the `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.cursor`, `~/.openclaw` or `~/.hermes` credential files;
  - never install anything beyond the approved list above (Task W0 and Task D1 install those);
  - retry until the listed checks are green; report anything that could not be done.

## Review Focus

The five situations a person will meet that the spec implies but no task's main tests exercise, most likely first. Each one has a test in the task named after it.

1. **The person's login shell is slow, noisy or asks a question at start** (an oh-my-zsh "update now? [Y/n]" prompt, a banner, an rc file that hangs). Sessions must still start: the resolver gives the shell no input, ignores everything outside its markers, gives up at 10 s and uses the fallback with the quiet notice. (Task S2: fake shells that print junk, wait for input, and hang.)
2. **A big paste** (a log or a file over 64 KB) into a session. Nothing is lost: the client splits input into frames of at most 64 KB without breaking a character, and the server still refuses a single frame over 64 KB. (Tasks U1 and S9.)
3. **The same session open in two windows** (the desktop window and a browser tab), one of them slow or asleep. Only the focused one types and sets the size; the other's keys are dropped; a window that falls 4 MB behind is closed with a reason and reattaches with a fresh screen; the PTY never pauses because of a window that is gone, and a window that stops reading while the PTY is paused is closed after 10 s so the agent keeps going (decision Q41). (Tasks S6 and S9.)
4. **Agent OS is killed hard while sessions are live, or the folder is gone later.** On the next start each session shows as ended ("Ended when Agent OS quit.") with Resume, and Resume refuses with the folder-policy message when the folder was deleted or moved. Recent folders drop it. (Tasks S6 and S2.)
5. **Safety is switched to Look only while sessions are open.** Open sessions keep running and can be stopped; New session and Resume are refused with the Look only sentence and a way to Safety; the Safety page's level words say this truthfully. (Tasks S6, U3 and U4.)

## Planning decisions (the owner can overturn any of these)

The spec is binding. These decisions fill gaps the code maps found (`map-*.md`, "Mismatches with the spec") or settle wording the spec leaves to the plan. Each line: decision, why, cost if wrong. Tasks use them verbatim; a decision marked **(owner)** is listed for Harsha's review at hand-off, and the plan already follows it.

### Tests and the watcher

- **Q1 One watcher for the whole run.** `npm test` becomes `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`. It records a baseline of running processes, starts `node --test --test-timeout=180000` on the explicit file list `test/*.test.js` (so helpers and fakes under `test/helpers/` and `test/fakes/` are never run as tests), polls `ps -A -ww -o pid=,ppid=,command=` every 200 ms, and fails the run (exit 1, after the runner ends) when it saw a violation. Extra arguments are passed through: those starting with `-` go to `node --test` (in the `--flag=value` form), the others replace the file list (`npm test -- test/sessions-profiles.test.js`). Why: `--import` would start one poller per test file, and `node --test` with no file list also runs helper `.js` files as tests (map-tests-harness 1). Cost if wrong: a slower runner script; easy to swap. Known limit: a real agent that starts and exits in under 200 ms can be missed; every session the tests start lives far longer.
- **Q1a What counts as a real agent.** A process is a violation when (a) it was not in the baseline, (b) it is a descendant of the runner (ppid chain at the time it was first seen; pids once seen as descendants stay remembered after their parent dies, unless the pid now runs a different command under a parent that is not a descendant, which is a reused pid and ignored), and (c) the basename of its first or second command token is one of `claude`, `codex`, `agent`, `cursor-agent`, `hermes`, `openclaw` while that token's real path is outside the allowed fake roots: `os.tmpdir()` (realpath), the repo's `test/` folder and `.superpowers/ui-audit/fake-bin/`. A bare command word with no folder is a violation (it cannot be proved to be a fake). Whatever the roots say, a new descendant that runs from a real agent's own install folder (`REAL_AGENT_PATHS`: `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/`, `node_modules/@openai/codex/`, `node_modules/openclaw/`, `/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes`, `.local/share/claude/versions/`, `.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/`) is a violation, because the temp folder also holds every temp HOME. The owner's own always-running `claude` processes are not descendants, so they never trip it (map-tests-harness 2). On a violation it prints the pid, the binary path and the test file whose runner process is the ancestor, sends SIGTERM to the offender, and exits 1. Windows: prints "no-real-agents watcher: not available on Windows" and runs the tests unwatched.
- **Q1b Pure core for unit tests.** `test/helpers/no-real-agents.js` exports `parsePsRows(text)`, `findViolations(rows, { baseline, rootPid, seenDescendants, allowedRoots, names })` and `startWatcher({ rootPid, intervalMs = 200, onViolation })` (plus the names in "Shared names and shapes"). `test/no-real-agents.test.js` tests the pure functions with synthetic rows (no real agents ever started).
- **Q1c The tests never read the owner's shell setup.** `test/fakes/login-shell.sh` (exported from `test/helpers/fake-agents.js` as `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL`) is the only `SHELL` any test uses: started as `<it> -i -l -c <command>`, it runs the command with `/bin/sh -c`, reads no startup file and keeps PATH exactly as given. `scripts/run-tests.mjs` sets `SHELL` to it and removes `ZDOTDIR`, `ENV` and `BASH_ENV` for the whole run, and every test that starts `server/index.js` also sets `SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` itself, so a single file run with `node --test` is safe too. Never `SHELL=/bin/sh`: on macOS a real login `sh` runs `path_helper`, which puts `/usr/local/bin` and `/opt/homebrew/bin` ahead of the test's fake folder, so the Q8 fallback could start a real agent. The only exceptions are the tests whose subject is a slow, noisy or failing login shell (S2, S8); they pass their own fake shell. In a test that can start a session, `PATH` is the fake bin folder plus `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` only, and the fake bin holds all six names (`claude`, `codex`, `agent`, `cursor-agent`, `hermes`, `openclaw`), so detection's fixed fallback folders never find a real agent first. Applies to S1, S2, S8, S9, S10, E1, the UI audit harness, and the existing server-spawning test files (S8 updates those). Why: from S8 on, every local-mode server reads its login shell (Q23), and about 12 existing server test files pass `...process.env`, so they would run the owner's zsh and its startup files. Cost if wrong: one env object in the runner and one line per server test.
- **Q2 TUI fakes.** One script `test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs` (Node, no shell), started through per-name shims that `makeFakeAgentBin(dir, { names, mode })` in `test/helpers/fake-agents.js` writes into a temp bin folder. Behaviour is chosen by the `FAKE_AGENT_MODE` environment variable and by typed commands, never by real agent flags: it answers the detection probes (`--version`, `--help`, `auth status` and the like) at once without a terminal; otherwise it prints its argv and selected environment variables as one JSON line (`FAKE_ARGV {...}`), prints a prompt `> `, echoes typed lines, turns on bracketed paste (`ESC[?2004h`) and the alternate screen on request, sends BEL and OSC 9/99/777, asks DA1 (`ESC[c`) and DSR (`ESC[6n`) at once or with `ask after <ms>` (S9 closes the writer's window in between), prints the replies it receives (`REPLY`), a bracketed paste (`PASTE <json>`) and other keys (`KEY`), exits with a typed exit code (`exit 3`), and in mode `setsid-grandchild` starts a grandchild with `spawn(process.execPath, [...], { detached: true })` (libuv calls `setsid()`; macOS has no `setsid` command) that writes its pid to `FAKE_AGENT_PIDFILE` and sleeps. The `claude` shim also answers `agents --json` (mode `agents-hang` never answers) and `stop <id>`. Mode `updater` asks `Update now? [y/N] ` and prints `ANSWER <text>`. `FAKE_AGENT_LOG` gets one JSON line per event; on SIGTERM the fake logs the text of the file named by `FAKE_AGENT_SNAPSHOT_ON_TERM`, after replacing the literal `{AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID}` in that name with its own `AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID` (the quit test's proof that meta.json was written before any kill). The UI audit harness's `.superpowers/ui-audit/fake-bin/` gets the same six shims, so sessions in probes behave like TUIs (U1, which adds the first session probe, does this; later UI tasks reuse it).

### Process tree, shutdown, quit

- **Q3 Descendant walk.** `listDescendants(pid)` runs `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=` once (2 s limit, argv only) and walks the ppid map from `pid`; on Linux without `ps` (the Docker image has no `procps`) it reads `/proc/<n>/stat` instead. `killProcessTree` lists descendants first, then SIGTERMs the group (`-pid`) and each descendant, waits `graceMs`, then SIGKILLs every survivor (checked with `process.kill(p, 0)`) and the group. `killAllTrackedSync` (hard exit) uses `spawnSync("ps", …, { timeout: 500 })` (or the same `/proc` read) and SIGKILL. Windows keeps `taskkill /T /F`. Cost if wrong: a pid reused within the grace period could be signalled; the 3 s window makes that very unlikely.
- **Q4 Graceful quit on every OS through stdin.** The desktop shell starts the server with `AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN=1` and a piped stdin that stays open for the app's whole life. On quit it writes `AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN\n`, waits up to `QUIT_GRACE` (10 s) for the exit, then forces the server at once (SIGKILL on unix, `taskkill /T /F` on Windows); if the line cannot be written, unix sends SIGTERM at once. The server reads stdin only when that variable is `1`; the exact line (spaces and a trailing carriage return ignored) runs the same `shutdown()` as SIGTERM, and end-of-file on stdin (the shell crashed) also runs it. Why: on Windows the server has no console and `kill_server` is `taskkill /F` at once, so there is no other graceful path (map-desktop-packaging 6); forcing at once after the grace keeps the worst case at 10 s instead of 20. Cost if wrong: one extra code path in the server.
- **Q5 Custom Quit item.** `PredefinedMenuItem::quit` is replaced by `MenuItem::with_id("agentos-quit", "Quit Agent OS", true, accel)` where `accel` is `Some("CmdOrCtrl+Q")` on macOS and `None` elsewhere (on Windows and Linux, Ctrl+Q stays with the terminal, and closing the window is how you quit). Why: ⌘Q through the predefined item reaches only `RunEvent::Exit`, which cannot be prevented (map-desktop-packaging 5).
- **Q5a A termination signal to the app does not ask (owner).** SIGTERM or SIGINT to the desktop app runs the server's quit steps 3 and 4 (the stdin line, then the grace) and exits, without the question. Why: a signal must not hang on a dialog; the spec's own "if no window is loaded to ask, the quit continues from step 3" is the same idea. This differs from spec L521, which lists a termination signal among the routes that ask. Cost if wrong: one branch in `install_signal_handler` to change.
- **Q5b Quit routes that cannot ask (owner).** The Dock's Quit, the app switcher's Quit, logging out and the updater's restart reach only `RunEvent::Exit` (tao 0.37.1, Tauri 2.12.1; `prevent_exit()` ignores `RESTART_EXIT_CODE`) and cannot be prevented: they run the graceful stdin stop (Q4) without the question. The in-app "Install & restart" (`src/ui/components/UpdateBanner.tsx`) runs the quit check itself first and shows the same quit question when sessions are live (U1). Spike S7 records what the Dock's Quit and the app switcher's Quit really do. Why: the spec (L521) lists these routes among the ones that ask, but nothing in the shell can stop them; the page can ask only on the path it starts itself. Cost if wrong: a person who quits from the Dock loses live sessions without a question (each still ends as "Ended when Agent OS quit." with Resume).
- **Q6 Quit plumbing.** Shell → UI event `agentos://quit-requested`; the shell shows and focuses the window first, so the question is visible even when the window was hidden. The UI answers `agentos://quit-shown` as soon as anything is on screen (the checking sentence included), or `agentos://quit-answer` `{ quit: true }` at once when no session is live, then `agentos://quit-answer` `{ quit }`. No `quit-shown` within 2 s means no window can ask: quit. After `quit-shown`, the shell waits for the answer with no time limit; a second ⌘Q while the question is open does nothing; a page reload drops an open question, so the next quit asks again. `RunEvent::ExitRequested` (last window destroyed, `app.exit()`) and `WindowEvent::CloseRequested` on Windows/Linux go through the same flow. `listen`/`emit` are in `core:default`; no custom `invoke` command is added (a remote window would need an AppManifest, map-desktop-packaging 9). The UI imports `@tauri-apps/api/event`; Task D1 adds `@tauri-apps/api` to `package.json` dependencies at the exact version already in `package-lock.json` (2.12.1, installed today as a dependency of the plugins, so nothing new is downloaded), in the same step as `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog@2.8.3`; U1 only checks both are there **(owner)**.
- **Q6a Hide and show (macOS).** `CloseRequested` → `prevent_close()` + `hide()`; `RunEvent::Reopen` → `show()` + `set_focus()`; a "Show Agent OS" item (`agentos-show`) in the app menu does the same.
- **Q6b Accelerators on Windows and Linux.** The View menu's Reload loses its accelerator, and the predefined Edit, Window and Hide items are left out on Windows and Linux (their Ctrl accelerators are fixed in muda 0.20 and cannot be removed), so Ctrl+R, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+M and Ctrl+H reach the agent (map-desktop-packaging 4). Copy and paste in text fields rely on WebView2 and WebKitGTK handling the keys themselves (not checked at run time here; a later Windows spike). macOS keeps them on ⌘.
- **Q6c Notifications wait for SP4.** `tauri-plugin-notification` and the `AGENT_OS_ALERT:` stdout lines are added in SP4, when alerts exist (owner decision on 2026-10-14). SP3 adds only `tauri-plugin-dialog`.

### Environment, profiles, folders

- **Q7 Managed-Node CLIs keep their own Node.** For an agent whose detected binary is inside Agent OS's managed Node folder and whose first line is a node shebang, the session's `PATH` gets that binary's own folder first (the same rule as `withSiblingNodePath`, `server/runtime/safety.js`). Why: otherwise a managed-Node OpenClaw or Codex would run with whichever `node` is first on the login PATH (map-agents-profiles 4). Cost if wrong: one PATH entry.
- **Q7a PWD is the session's folder.** A session's environment sets `PWD` to the session's folder, as a shell does after `cd <folder>` in Terminal; the resolver shell's own `PWD`, `OLDPWD` and `_` are dropped (they named the short-lived resolver, not the person's settings). This is one variable beyond H2's "set" list, a deliberate fidelity choice; the S3 snapshot test pins it. Why: tools and prompts that read `PWD` would otherwise see HOME, which a Terminal session in that folder never shows. Cost if wrong: one line in `profiles.js` and its test assertions.
- **Q8 Finding the binary.** `profiles.js` uses the path from `server/runtime/agents/detect.js` (H1). When detect finds nothing, it looks once more on the login shell's `PATH` with a small private `findOnPath` (`which()` searches only the server's own PATH and fixed folders), in detection's name order (`agent` before `cursor-agent`); still nothing → 409 `agent_not_installed` with "<agent> isn't installed, or Agent OS can't find it. Install it in Setup, then try again." (`<agent>` is the short name). detect.js itself is not changed.
- **Q9 Claude settings for sessions.** `buildClaudeSettings(brain, helper, { forSession: true })` leaves out `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB` (headless keeps it; the test at `test/builder-brains.test.js` L751 stays as it is). The session file is written by `profiles.js` at `<root>/sessions/<id>/claude-settings.json` with mode 0600 (not `writeClaudeSettingsFile`, which picks random names), after `assertSafeClaudeSettings`. Sessions never add `--model` (H3 allows only `--session-id` and `--settings`; the model reaches Claude through the settings `env` block, map-agents-profiles 9). A plan brain with a model adds nothing.
- **Q10 Flags the repo has not seen.** The launch and resume argv are exactly the spec's tables, even where the repo has never seen a flag (map-agents-profiles 10). Spikes S2-S6 check them on the owner's Mac. If one is wrong, the agent prints its own usage error in the terminal and exits, the tab shows "Ended with exit code <n>.", and a follow-up task fixes the profile.
- **Q11 Session environment comes only from `shell-env.js`.** `profiles.js` never copies `plan.env` or argv from `buildRun` (Cursor `--trust`, Hermes `HERMES_HOME` and the permission flags must not leak in, map-agents-profiles 11-12). Every soft-stop CLI call (`claude agents --json`, `claude stop`) uses the session's own profile environment (built by `sessionEnv`) and folder, never the default `process.env`, which holds `AGENT_OS_TOKEN` (map-agents-profiles 3).
- **Q11a Values Agent OS added itself are not the person's environment.** The desktop shell passes `AGENT_OS_PORT=0` instead of `PORT=0`, and `server/index.js` reads `process.env.AGENT_OS_PORT ?? process.env.PORT` (`PORT` still works for `npm start`, Docker and the tests). The keys `loadLocalEnv` applied from Agent OS's own env file are registered with `excludeFromSessionEnv(envFile.applied)` in `server/index.js` before the login shell is read; they are left out of what goes into the login shell, the fallback and the Windows environment. The desktop shell also passes the PATH it was started with as `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH`, because the folders `server_path_env()` adds (Homebrew, `~/.local/bin`, the managed Node folder) are Agent OS's own additions. `shell-env.js` starts the login shell with that PATH when it is a non-empty string; the fallback keeps the server's PATH (H2). When an npm script started Agent OS (`npm start`, `npm run dev`, `npm run desktop:dev`), what npm added (its lower-case `npm_*` variables, `INIT_CWD`, `NODE`, `COLOR`, its `EDITOR` fill-in and its `node_modules/.bin` and `node-gyp-bin` PATH folders) is kept out of the same places (`serverEnv()` in Task S2); the known limit is that a person's own `EDITOR` equal to npm's fill-in, or their own lower-case `npm_config_*` variable, is dropped in the fallback and on Windows. Nothing is stripped from the login shell's own output beyond H2's list, so a value the person's own startup files set still passes. Why: otherwise a Hermes session would get Agent OS's `HERMES_HOME` (H1), and an agent's dev server would bind a random port, unlike Terminal (H2). Cost if wrong: one set in `shell-env.js`, one line in `server/index.js` and two variable names in `main.rs`.
- **Q12 Agent OS's folders.** The folder policy also refuses the managed Node folder (`managedNodeRoot()`, `~/.agent-os` by default), with the same message as AGENT_OS_HOME. Why: it is Agent OS's own folder too (map-agents-profiles 15).
- **Q13 Recovery order.** `sessionManager.recoverStaleSessions()` and `enforceRecordingCap()` run before `app.listen`, each in its own try/catch (a failure is logged and the server still starts), so no request sees a session still marked live from a previous run. The runs and rooms recovery stay where they are.
- **Q14 No folder-check route.** A typed folder (browser mode) and a picked folder (desktop) are both checked by `POST /api/sessions`, which answers 400 `{ error: "folder_refused", code, message }`; the dialog shows `message` under the field and keeps the typed text. A Look only refusal comes before a folder refusal (the Look only note replaces the form).
- **Q15 Look only.** Creating and resuming an `agent` session are refused at Look only with 409 `execution_gate_off`: "Safety is on Look only, so no session can start. Allow running agents in Safety, then try again." Open sessions keep running. Stop, dismiss, list and recordings always work. The `update` kind is not gated (spec).

### Engine

- **Q16 Hold to stop all.** Sessions (both kinds) and rooms start stopping together; runs follow the rooms and never wait for sessions (a session's Stop takes about 2 to 5 s). The result adds `sessions`, `sessionsStopped`, `sessionsFailed`, `sessionsTimedOut`, `sessionsAlreadyEnded`, `sessionsChecked` and `openClawStopped`, so the toast never says "Stopped" for a session that ended by itself and carries the OpenClaw note.
- **Q23 Login shell after READY, never blocking.** In local mode only, the login-shell environment starts resolving right after `AGENT_OS_READY` and never delays it; `POST /api/sessions` awaits it (at most the 10 s limit). In the public demo and public mode no session can exist, so the server never runs the login shell there.
- **Q24 List response.** `GET /api/sessions` → `{ sessions, environmentNotice, pty: { ok, reason }, maxLive: 8 }`, agent kind only unless `?kind=all` (the update service and Hold to stop all use `kind=all`).
- **Q25 Limits copy.** 9th live agent session: 409 `too_many_sessions`, "Agent OS runs at most 8 sessions at once. Stop one, then try again." node-pty missing: 503 `pty_unavailable`, "Agent OS could not load its terminal module on this computer, so sessions can't start." Unknown id: 404 `unknown_session`, "That session doesn't exist anymore."
- **Q26 Recording route.** `GET /api/sessions/:id/recording` streams `application/x-asciicast` from the recorder's `openRecording(id)`: one header line (the older segment's when it exists), the events of `screen.prev.cast`, then the events of `screen.cast` without its header and its leading "[earlier output removed]" marker, so that marker appears only at the start and only when output really was removed; a last line still being written is left out. `DELETE` refuses a live session (409 `recording_live`) and a missing recording (404 `recording_missing`, "That recording doesn't exist anymore.").
- **Q27 Quit check covers both kinds.** `quitCheck()` lists every live session of both kinds as `{ id, title, kind }` (an `update` session's title is "<agent> update"), so the quit question promises a resume only for agent sessions.
- **Q36 Resume rules.** Only an ended `agent` session resumes; same id and tab; new process; recording appended after "--- resumed ---" (the recorder writes the marker); status back to `starting`; `dismissed` back to false (the tab comes back). `resume.available` and `resume.reason` are computed on every list:
  - "Another <agent> session is open in this folder. Stop it first." (fallback agents, a live session of that agent in the folder);
  - "More than one ended <agent> session used this folder, so Agent OS can't tell which conversation to resume." (fallback agents);
  - "<agent> isn't installed anymore." (detect finds nothing).
  - `resume.fallback` is true for Hermes, Codex and Cursor until their spike.
- **Q37 Dismiss** only works on an ended session (409 `session_live` otherwise) and is stored in meta.json.
- **Q38 Recording cap.** `enforceRecordingCap()` runs at server start and after each session ends (with the manager's `isLive`, so a recording still being written is never removed). It removes only the cast files; meta.json stays, so the ended tab and Resume stay. A removed recording's row disappears from Runs; `GET /api/recordings` answers `{ recordings, removedByCap }`, and the note "Older recordings were removed to stay under 1 GB." shows on the Session recordings tab while `removedByCap` is above 0. An ended session whose recording is gone reads "… Its recording was removed." instead of "… The recording is in Runs.".
- **Q39 Ids.** Session ids are `crypto.randomUUID()`. Every route and the WebSocket check the id with `SESSION_ID_RE` (from `server/runtime/sessions/errors.js`) before any file path is built (no path traversal). Claude's `--session-id` uuid is a second, separate `crypto.randomUUID()` kept in meta.json as `agentSessionId`.
- **Q40 WebSocket refusals and reconnects.** An upgrade URL with any query string is refused. An unknown session id, an ended session and any other upgrade address are refused with 403 like every other failure (Security 1: "on any failure: write 403 and destroy the socket"). The 64 KB limit applies to the whole raw `in` frame. Close codes are `too_far_behind` 4000, `session_ended` 4001, `attach_failed` 4004, with the same word as the reason; clients decide by the word. The client never reattaches to an ended session; after a refused upgrade or a 1006 close it reattaches only while the latest session list still says the session is live, after 0.5, 1, 2, 5 and 5 s (5 attempts), then shows "Lost the connection to this session." with a "Reconnect" button.
- **Q41 A paused PTY never waits for a window that is not reading.** On top of the spec's back-pressure rule, a PTY paused for more than `PAUSED_DROP_MS = 10000` closes every attachment still more than 512 KB behind with `too_far_behind`, so the PTY resumes; the timer is not cleared just because one attachment closes, and it stops when the PTY resumes or the process exits. Why: once every window lags past 512 KB the PTY pauses and no more output is sent, so no window can ever reach the 4 MB close, and a hidden, throttled or asleep window would keep the agent blocked on its own output, which breaks "the window hides and sessions keep running" (D5). The closed window reattaches with a fresh snapshot when it reads again. Cost if wrong: a slow window is reattached more often than needed.

### Packaging and CI

- **Q20 CI desktop job.** `ci.yml` gains a `desktop` job, matrix `ubuntu-22.04`, `macos-14`, `windows-latest`, with the apt list from `release.yml` on Linux. It runs `node scripts/prepare-desktop.mjs --skip-node` (so the node-pty copy runs on all three systems), creates an empty `desktop/src-tauri/resources/node` (tauri-build stops when a resource folder is missing), then `cargo build --locked` (debug, no bundle) and `cargo test --locked` (D1's quit-flow and stdin tests) in `desktop/src-tauri`. It follows the action-pinning style already used in `ci.yml`; the existing `test` job keeps `macos-latest`.
- **Q21 node-pty in bundles.** esbuild keeps `node-pty` external (and `bufferutil`, `utf-8-validate`). `scripts/build-server-bundle.mjs` copies `node_modules/node-pty/{lib,package.json,prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>}` (without `.map`, `.test.js` and `.pdb` files) into `build/server/node_modules/node-pty/` after it bundles, for the host by default or for `--platform`/`--arch` when given; it fails when that prebuild folder is missing, checks `spawn-helper`'s mode (0755) on macOS, and checks the CPU of every copied `.node`, `.dll`, `.exe` and `spawn-helper` by reading its Mach-O, ELF or PE header instead of running it (the same check as `file` / `lipo -archs`, and it works on the Windows runner). `bundle.json` records `target: "<platform>-<arch>"`. `scripts/prepare-desktop.mjs` gains `--platform`/`--arch`, passes them on, and does the copy before its `--skip-node` early return. `release.yml` passes `matrix.node_platform`/`matrix.node_arch`. `pty-host.js` imports node-pty lazily, so a server without it still boots (portable test, Docker).
- **Q22 Watcher in CI.** Linux and macOS runners use the watcher; Windows prints the "not available" line (Q1a).
- **Q42 The xterm package set (owner).** Pin the set built from the same xterm.js commit (`c58ea36`) as `@xterm/xterm@6.1.0-beta.304`, which is also the set VS Code pins: `@xterm/headless@6.1.0-beta.303`, `@xterm/addon-serialize@0.15.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-fit@0.12.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-unicode11@0.10.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-search@0.17.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-web-links@0.13.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-clipboard@0.3.0-beta.303`, `@xterm/addon-webgl@0.20.0-beta.300`. `@xterm/headless` and `@xterm/addon-serialize` are CommonJS: load them with a default import or `createRequire`, never a named ESM import. `@xterm/addon-unicode11` is used by both the mirror (S4) and the browser terminal (U2). Why: the add-ons numbered `-beta.304` come from later commits, need `@xterm/xterm` ≥ beta.305 to beta.310 and stop `npm install` with ERESOLVE (checked with `npm view`), and the serializer reads xterm internals, so it must match its terminal's build. The orchestrator records the owner's yes in the ledger before W0 runs; W0's worker does not ask, it stops if that line is missing. Cost if wrong: a re-pin of eight packages in one later task.
- **Q43 node-pty stays a normal dependency.** `node-pty` goes in `dependencies`, not `optionalDependencies`. Why: every CI, release and Docker target has a prebuilt binary, so `npm ci` never needs a compiler there, and `pty-host.js`'s lazy import already covers a missing module (the server boots and answers `pty_unavailable`). Cost if wrong: on a system with no prebuild and no compiler, `npm ci` fails instead of installing without terminals.
- **Q44 Docker.** Sessions inside the Docker image are out of scope for SP3: the image must still build and boot (the lazy node-pty import), and the Dockerfile is unchanged. Recorded as a known limit. Why: the image is the public demo and remote-host path, where sessions are refused (local mode only) anyway. Cost if wrong: a later task adds the session prerequisites to the image.

### UI

- **Q17 Terminal theme.** The `--os-term-*` and `--os-ansi-*` tokens already exist (`src/ui/tokens.css` L104-124). The terminal theme reads them with `getComputedStyle` at mount and when `<html>`'s theme changes. A test computes the contrast of all 16 ANSI colours on `--os-term-bg` in every CSS block of `tokens.css` that sets them (today only `:root`; a later light theme is tested without changing the test) and asserts ≥ 4.5:1.
- **Q18 Status words.** `starting` uses the kit's idle icon (dashed circle) with the word "Starting"; `exited` uses the stopped icon with the word "Ended". Both are new labels on the existing `StatusWord` states, not new colours. Why: the only icons that do not claim "working", "ready" or "failed".
- **Q30 One shared sessions poll.** `useSessionsList()` (`src/ui/useSessionsList.ts`, inside `SessionsListProvider`; 5 s, through `useInterval`, paused on a hidden tab, every call through a time limit) feeds the menu count, Home, Agents and the Sessions page.
- **Q31 SP2 lessons apply to every UI task (P26):** copy must be true; "—" means unknown, "…" means loading; stale data sits under a warn note; every request has a time limit (`withTimeout` in `src/ui/homeShared.ts`); unmount guards, and never `navigateTo` after unmount; never throw away typed text; the main action is on screen at 1280×720; long text wraps or ends in "…"; focus moves sensibly (into a dialog, back to its opener).
- **Q32 Pieces with no prototype picture (owner).** The ended tab, the Sessions empty state, the settings menu, "What works here", the quit question (with the update banner's "Install & restart" variant), the folder field states, the Safety level words and the Help page's changed sentences are built from the Cobalt kit or reworded for SP3. E1 shows Harsha screenshots of each for approval before SP3 is called done; changes go back to a worker.
- **Q45 Terminal defaults.** The DOM renderer is the default on macOS and in the Linux desktop app (both WebKit web views, where WebGL glyph corruption is reported); WebGL is the default in the Windows desktop app and in browser mode on Windows and Linux, with the fallback to DOM when the WebGL context is lost. In the desktop app, a terminal link whose address is outside the opener's allow list is copied, with the sentence "Link copied. Open it in your browser." (the opener scope stays as the owner approved). `mailto:` text is not made a link (the web-links add-on needs "//" after the scheme). No Ctrl+Shift+C/V in SP3: the spec's key list sends every other key to the agent, so on Windows and Linux paste works through the context menu. Why: the spec names DOM on macOS; Linux's desktop app uses the same engine; the opener scope is a security choice the owner already made. Cost if wrong: one default in `defaultTerminalPrefs` and one sentence.

The recording continues after a marker."; fallback warning (spec): "This resumes the most recent <agent> conversation in this folder, which may be one you started outside Agent OS."; buttons "Cancel" and "Resume conversation".

(the recording holds output only, but an agent's terminal shows the prompts and pasted text it echoes, so they are in the recording; Q32); cap note "Older recordings were removed to stay under 1 GB."

If you go ahead, it ends them." (Q5b); no "Review guide" button. A Claude Code background task moved with /bg may keep running if Agent OS can't find it, and OpenClaw may still finish its last step after the terminal closes. The Hermes background service and the OpenClaw Gateway keep running: each has its own Stop on Agents."

## Shared names and shapes

Every task uses these names, paths, signatures and shapes exactly. A task's Interfaces quote from this section; where a task's text and this section differ, this section is right and the task is fixed before it is dispatched. The spec section is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-cobalt-redesign-and-real-terminals-design.md` lines 333-607 plus H1-H9 (lines 58-128); decisions named Q<n> are in "Planning decisions" below.

| `@tauri-apps/api` | `2.12.1` (already in `package-lock.json`) | D1 | `QuitQuestion.tsx` (U1, `@tauri-apps/api/event`) |
