- The xterm set is the one built from xterm.js commit `c58ea36` (the commit of `@xterm/xterm@6.1.0-beta.304`), the set VS Code pins (Q42). The orchestrator records the owner's yes in the ledger before W0 runs; W0 stops if that line is missing.
- D1 installs both Tauri packages in one step (`npm install --save-exact @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog@2.8.3 @tauri-apps/api@2.12.1`); U1 only checks that both are present and stops if not.
- Loading: `@xterm/headless` and `@xterm/addon-serialize` are CommonJS; load them with `createRequire(import.meta.url)` or a default import, never a named ESM import. `ws` has named ESM exports (`import { WebSocketServer } from "ws"`; tests use `import WebSocket from "ws"`). `node-pty` is loaded only by `pty-host.js`, lazily (`await import("node-pty")` in a try/catch), so a server without it still boots (portable test, Docker); its `spawn` is a named export and also on `.default`.
- node-pty stays a normal dependency (Q43). Its prebuilds: `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/` for darwin, linux and win32 on x64 and arm64; macOS folders hold `pty.node` and `spawn-helper` (0755); Linux folders hold only `pty.node`; Windows folders hold `conpty.node`, `conpty_console_list.node` and `conpty/`.

### Files on disk

| Path | Mode | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `<AGENT_OS_HOME>` (`runtimePaths().root`) | 0700 | S2 `ensureRuntimeStore()` |
| `<root>/sessions/`, `<root>/worktrees/` | 0700 | S2 `ensureRuntimeStore()` |
| `<root>/sessions/<id>/` | 0700 | S3, S5, S6 through `ensurePrivateDir` |
| `<root>/sessions/<id>/meta.json` | 0600 | S6 (S7 writes the quit fields) |
| `<root>/sessions/<id>/screen.cast`, `screen.prev.cast` | 0600 | S5 |
| `<root>/sessions/<id>/claude-settings.json` | 0600 | S3 (Claude with an OpenRouter or Local brain only) |
| `<root>/config/sessions.json` | 0600 | S3 (`{ claudeFullscreen }`) |

- Folders are created with mode 0700 and chmodded to 0700 when they already exist (Windows: created only). A chmod of the root that fails with EPERM or EACCES logs `Agent OS could not make its folder private (0700): <root>` once per root and carries on; any other error on the root, and every chmod error on `sessions/` or `worktrees/`, throws.
- `meta.json` (version 1), read by S2 (`recentSessionFolders`) and S5 (`listRecordings`, the cap):
  `{ version: 1, id, kind: "agent" | "update", agentId, agentLabel, folder, folderName, folderShown, branch, status: "starting" | "exited", createdAt, startedAt, endedAt, exitCode, signal, endedBy: "stop" | "quit" | null, dismissed, brain, agentSessionId, resumeMode, resumes, lastUsedAt }`
  - `status` is `"starting"` while the process runs and `"exited"` after; activity states live only in memory. Without the manager's `isLive`, a session counts as live when `status !== "exited"` and `endedAt` is empty.
  - Times are ISO 8601 UTC strings (compared as text). `createdAt` is the first start (tab order); `startedAt` the latest start or resume ("Running for"); `lastUsedAt` the latest start, resume or end (recent folders sort by it).
  - `folder` is the profile's real `cwd`; OpenClaw's is HOME with `folderShown: false` while `OPENCLAW_FOLDER_HONOURED` is false. `agentLabel` is `SESSION_AGENT_LABEL[agentId]`. No pid is stored.

### Errors: `server/runtime/sessions/errors.js` (S3)

- The only home of:
  - `export const SESSION_ID_RE = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/`;
  - `export function isSessionId(value)` → boolean;
  - `export function sessionError(status, code, message, extra = {})` → an `Error` with `.status`, `.code`, `.message` and `.extra` (no `.body`, no `.folderCode`);
  - `export function errorBody(err)` → `{ error: err.code, message: err.message, ...err.extra }`.
- S5 and S6 import it and never create or overwrite it. `manager.js` re-exports `SESSION_ID_RE`, `isSessionId` and `sessionError` (`export { SESSION_ID_RE, isSessionId, sessionError } from "./errors.js";`), so S8, S9 and tests may import them from either file.
- The routes answer every `sessionError` with `res.status(err.status).json(errorBody(err))`. Brain errors (`brainError` from `server/runtime/builders/brain-launch.js`: `openrouter_key_missing`, `base_url_without_credential`; `.code` and `.message`, no `.status`) pass through `create` and `resume` unchanged and are answered with the existing `builderErrorResponse(error)` from `server/runtime/builders/resolve.js` (both 409).
- `<agent>` below is `SESSION_AGENT_LABEL[agentId]`, the short name.

| Status | Code | Message | Raised by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `unknown_agent` | "Agent OS can't start a session for that agent." | S3, S6 |
| 400 | `unknown_kind` | "Agent OS can't start that kind of session." | S3 |
| 400 | `update_not_available` | "Only Hermes is updated in a session." (also `createUpdateSession` for any agent but Hermes) | S3, S6 |
| 400 | `folder_refused` | the folder policy's message, with `extra: { code }` (the policy code); the answer is `{ error: "folder_refused", message, code }` (Q14) | S3, S6 |
| 400 | `invalid_settings` | "Only the Claude Code fullscreen setting (on or off) can be changed here." | S3 (S8 passes it through) |
| 404 | `unknown_session` | "That session doesn't exist anymore." (also any id that fails `SESSION_ID_RE`) | S3, S5, S6, S8 |
| 404 | `recording_missing` | "That recording doesn't exist anymore." | S5 |
| 409 | `execution_gate_off` | "Safety is on Look only, so no session can start. Allow running agents in Safety, then try again." | S6 |
| 409 | `too_many_sessions` | "Agent OS runs at most 8 sessions at once. Stop one, then try again." | S6 |
| 409 | `update_running` | "An update is already running. Wait for it to finish, then try again." | S6 |
| 409 | `agent_not_installed` | "<agent> isn't installed, or Agent OS can't find it. Install it in Setup, then try again." | S3 |
| 409 | `not_resumable` | the session's `resume.reason` (Q36); "This Claude Code conversation can't be resumed." (a Claude resume without a valid uuid); "An update session can't be resumed." | S3, S6 |
| 409 | `session_live` | resume: "That session is still running, so there is nothing to resume."; dismiss: "That session is still running. Stop it first, then dismiss it." | S6 |
| 409 | `session_ended` | "That session has ended. Its recording is in Runs." (attach to an ended session) | S6 |
| 409 | `recording_live` | "That session is still running. Stop it first, then delete its recording." | S5 |
| 500 | `unsafe_argv` | "Agent OS stopped <agent> from starting: its command line had an option Agent OS never adds." | S3 |
| 500 | `start_failed` | "Agent OS could not start <agent>. Check that it is installed, then try again." | S6 |
| 500 | `internal_error` | "Something went wrong with sessions. Try again." (never a file path) | S8 |
| 503 | `pty_unavailable` | "Agent OS could not load its terminal module on this computer, so sessions can't start." | S6 |

Outside local mode, `requireLocalMode` answers 404 `{ error: "not_available" }` (no message) for every sessions route and every recordings route. The sessions WebSocket checks `isLocalMode()` itself in `checkUpgradeRequest` (S9), and outside local mode it is refused like every other failed upgrade: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` and a destroyed socket (spec Security 1).

### Server modules

#### `server/runtime/process-tree.js` (S1)

- `trackPid(pid, onExit?)`: registers a process this module did not start; ignores anything that is not a positive integer. `onExit` is an optional subscribe function `(listener: () => void) => unknown` that trackPid calls once, so the pid untracks itself when the process ends. pty-host passes the handle's own `onExit`.
- `untrackPid(pid)`; `listTrackedPids()` → `number[]` (a copy).
- `listDescendants(pid)` → `Promise<number[]>`: one `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=` (argv only, 2 s limit), every pid below `pid` at any depth. On Linux without `ps` it reads `/proc/<n>/stat` for every numeric entry of `/proc`. `[]` on Windows, for a bad pid, or when neither can be read.
- `descendantsFromPsOutput(text, pid)` → `number[]` (the pure walk); `parseProcStat(text)` → `{ pid, ppid } | null` (fields counted from the last `)`).
- `killProcessTree(pid, { graceMs = 1500 } = {})` → `Promise<void>` (never rejects). POSIX: lists descendants first, sends SIGTERM to the group led by `pid` and to each descendant, polls every 50 ms, sends SIGKILL to every target still alive after `graceMs`, then waits at most 1 s more. Windows: `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F`.
- `killAllTracked({ graceMs = 1500 } = {})`: every tracked child and tracked pid in parallel, then forgets them. `killAllTrackedSync()`: one `ps` snapshot (500 ms limit; the `/proc` read on Linux when `ps` fails), then SIGKILL to every tracked group and descendant (Windows: `child.kill()` for children, `taskkill /T /F` for tracked pids). `spawnTracked` keeps its signature.

#### `server/runtime/shutdown.js` (S1)

- `HARD_EXIT_MS = 8000`, `SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS = 7000`, `STDIN_SHUTDOWN_LINE = "AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN"`.
- `registerShutdownTask(name, fn)` → an unregister function; a second registration under the same name replaces the first; an empty name or a non-function throws `TypeError`.
- `shutdown({ server, taskLimitMs = SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS } = {})`: stops the scheduler; runs the runs' `stopAll()` and every registered task in parallel, each task cut off at `taskLimitMs` (errors logged, never thrown); awaits them BEFORE `killAllTracked()`; then the live-chat children; then `server.close` (500 ms fallback).
- `installShutdownHandlers(server, { hardExitMs = HARD_EXIT_MS, taskLimitMs = SHUTDOWN_TASK_LIMIT_MS } = {})`: SIGTERM, SIGINT (and SIGBREAK on Windows) start the shutdown with the hard exit timer (exit code 0). When `process.env.AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN === "1"` it reads stdin lines; the line `AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN` (compared after trimming spaces and a trailing carriage return) or the end of stdin starts the same shutdown. Without that variable stdin is never read.
- Budget: sessions quit ≤ 7 s (`SHUTDOWN_GUARD_MS`, S7) < server hard exit 8 s < desktop `QUIT_GRACE` 10 s (D1).

#### `server/runtime/store.js` (S2)

- `runtimePaths()` gains `sessions: <root>/sessions` and `worktrees: <root>/worktrees`.
- `ensureRuntimeStore()` makes `root`, `sessions` and `worktrees` 0700 as under "Files on disk".
- `export async function ensurePrivateDir(dir)` → `dir` (mkdir -p with 0700, then chmod 0700; Windows only makes it).

#### `shell-env.js` (S2)

- `LOGIN_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000`; `NESTED_MARKERS = ["CLAUDECODE", "CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT"]` (spikes S3 and S6 add the Codex and Cursor markers); `FALLBACK_NOTICE = "Agent OS could not read your login shell's settings, so sessions use a basic environment."`.
- `resolveLoginShellEnv({ shell, timeoutMs = 10000, nodePath = process.execPath, platform = process.platform } = {})` → `{ env, source: "login-shell" | "fallback" | "process", notice: string | null }`; never throws.
  - `shell` defaults to `process.env.SHELL`, else `os.userInfo().shell`. Runs `<shell> -i -l -c '<node> -e <script>'` (`-ic` for csh and tcsh), detached, stdin ignored, `cwd` HOME. The script prints `process.env` as JSON between two random markers; only the text between them is read.
  - The shell's environment is the server's minus `AGENT_OS_*`, `HERMES_AGENT_OS_*` and every excluded name, plus `AGENT_OS_RESOLVING_ENVIRONMENT=1`. Its `PATH` is `process.env.AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` when that is a non-empty string (the `PATH` the desktop app was started with, before `server_path_env()` adds its folders; Task D1). Otherwise it is the server's own `PATH` (`npm start`, the tests). `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` is an `AGENT_OS_*` name, so it never reaches the shell or a session. The fallback and the Windows environment keep the server's own `PATH` (H2). The parsed result leaves out `PWD`, `OLDPWD`, `_` and that flag; a result without `PATH` is a failure.
  - Timeout or failure: `source: "fallback"`, the server's environment without the excluded names, plus `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `~/.local/bin` appended to PATH when missing, and `notice: FALLBACK_NOTICE`. Windows: `source: "process"`, the process environment without the excluded names, `notice: null`.
- `excludeFromSessionEnv(keys)`: adds each string to the module's set of excluded names (Q11a; compared without letter case on Windows). `resetExcludedForTests()` empties it. Excluded names are left out of what goes INTO the login shell, the fallback and the Windows environment, never out of what the login shell gives back.
- `getLoginShellEnv()` → the same promise on every call (resolved once per server); `resetLoginShellEnvForTests()`.
- `sessionEnv(baseEnv, { sessionId, agentOsVersion = RUNTIME_VERSION, claudeFullscreen = false, agentId, platform = process.platform } = {})` → a new object:
  - without every `AGENT_OS_*`, `HERMES_AGENT_OS_*` and `NESTED_MARKERS` key (names compared without case on Windows);
  - with `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`, `TERM_PROGRAM=AgentOS`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION=<agentOsVersion>`, `AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID=<sessionId>`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1` only when `agentId === "claude" && claudeFullscreen === true`;
  - never setting or changing `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `HERMES_HOME`, any `OPENCLAW_*` variable or `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB`, and never `TERM_PROGRAM=vscode`.

#### `folders.js` (S2)

- `checkSessionFolder(input, { home = os.homedir(), agentOsHome = runtimePaths().root, managedRoot = managedNodeRoot(), platform = process.platform } = {})` → `{ ok: true, path, name }` or `{ ok: false, code, message }`.
  - Input is trimmed. `path` is `fs.realpath.native` of the input; `home`, `agentOsHome` and `managedRoot` are compared as real paths too, ignoring letter case on `darwin` and `win32`.
  - `<agentOsHome>/worktrees` and below pass the Agent OS rule but must still be inside HOME. The managed Node folder is refused like AGENT_OS_HOME (Q12).

  | code | message |
  |---|---|
  | `not_absolute` | "Type the full path, starting with / (or a drive letter on Windows)." |
  | `missing` | "That folder doesn't exist." (exists but can't be opened: "Agent OS can't open that folder.") |
  | `not_a_directory` | "That is a file, not a folder." |
  | `is_home` | "Your home folder itself can't be used. Pick a folder inside it." |
  | `inside_agent_os` | "Agent OS's own folder can't be used." |
  | `outside_home` | "Pick a folder inside your home folder." |

- `recentSessionFolders({ limit = 8 } = {})` → `[{ path, name, lastUsedAt }]`, newest first, one row per real folder, from meta.json `kind`, `folder`, `folderShown`, `startedAt`, `endedAt` and `lastUsedAt` (a row's `lastUsedAt` is the latest of `startedAt`, `endedAt` and `lastUsedAt`, so an older meta.json without `lastUsedAt` still sorts). Rows with `kind: "update"` or `folderShown: false` are left out; each folder is re-checked with `checkSessionFolder` and dropped when it fails.

#### `settings.js` (S3)

- `readSessionSettings()` → `{ claudeFullscreen: boolean }` (false when the file is missing, broken, or holds anything but `true`).
- `writeSessionSettings(patch)` → the new settings. Only `{ claudeFullscreen: boolean }` is accepted; anything else throws `invalid_settings` and writes nothing.

#### `profiles.js` (S3), plus two exports elsewhere

- `server/runtime/builders/brain-launch.js`: `buildClaudeSettings(brain, helper, { forSession = false } = {})`; with `forSession: true` the settings `env` has no `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB`. Headless callers (two arguments) are unchanged.
- `server/runtime/runs/run-manager.js`: `export function hasCursorForceFlag(plan)` (body unchanged).
- `SESSION_AGENTS = ["claude", "codex", "cursor", "hermes", "openclaw"]`.
- `OPENCLAW_FOLDER_HONOURED = false` (until spike S5).
- `SESSION_AGENT_LABEL = { claude: "Claude Code", codex: "Codex", cursor: "Cursor", hermes: "Hermes", openclaw: "OpenClaw" }`: the short names every session message, tab and dialog uses. `manager.js` imports it and re-exports it; nothing defines a second map.
- `buildSessionProfile({ agentId, folder, sessionId, kind = "agent", resume = null, settings, detected, brain = null, agentOsVersion = RUNTIME_VERSION } = {})` → `{ command, args, cwd, env, agentSessionId, settingsFile, softStop, resumeMode, folderShown, notes }`:
  - `resume` is `null` (a fresh start) or `{ agentSessionId: string | null }` (the value in meta.json). `settings` undefined reads `readSessionSettings()`; `detected` undefined calls `getAdapter(agentId).detect()`.
  - `command`: `detected.path`; when detection found nothing, the first match on the login shell's `PATH` through a private `findOnPath` (`agent` before `cursor-agent`; Q8). argv only, never a shell.
  - `args`:

    | Agent | Start | Resume |
    |---|---|---|
    | claude | `--session-id <new uuid>` (+ `--settings <file>` with an OpenRouter or Local brain) | `--resume <agentSessionId>` (+ the same `--settings` rule) |
    | codex | `-C <folder> -c tui.notification_method=osc9 -c tui.notifications=["agent-turn-complete","approval-requested"] -c tui.notification_condition=always` (+ `codexBrainArgs` with an OpenRouter or Local brain) | `resume --last` + the same `-c` options and brain options, in the same folder |
    | cursor | `--workspace <folder>` | `--resume --workspace <folder>` |
    | hermes | `--in <folder>` (kind `update`: exactly `update`) | `--resume latest --in <folder>` |
    | openclaw | `tui --session agentos-<sessionId>` | the same |

  - `cwd`: the real path from `checkSessionFolder(folder)`; OpenClaw uses `os.homedir()` while `OPENCLAW_FOLDER_HONOURED` is false, with `folderShown: false`.
  - `env`: `sessionEnv((await getLoginShellEnv()).env, { sessionId, agentOsVersion, claudeFullscreen, agentId })`; for a node-shebang CLI inside the managed Node folder, `withSiblingNodePath` puts its own folder first on `PATH` (Q7); then `PWD` is set to `cwd` (Q7a).
  - `agentSessionId`: Claude a new `crypto.randomUUID()` (or the resumed one); OpenClaw `agentos-<sessionId>`; Codex, Cursor, Hermes and the update kind `null`.
  - `settingsFile`: `<root>/sessions/<sessionId>/claude-settings.json` (0600) for Claude with an OpenRouter or Local brain, written from `buildClaudeSettings(brain, helper, { forSession: true })` after `assertSafeClaudeSettings`; otherwise `null` and no `--settings`. Sessions never add `--model` (Q9).
  - `softStop`: `"claude-bg"` (Claude), `"openclaw-abort"` (OpenClaw), otherwise `null`. `resumeMode`: `"id"` (Claude, OpenClaw), `"fallback"` (Codex, Cursor, Hermes), `null` (update). `notes`: `[FALLBACK_NOTICE]` when the login shell could not be read, else `[]`.
- `assertSessionArgvSafe(agentId, args)`: throws `unsafe_argv` unless `args` is exactly one of the shapes above and no option name is on the blocked list (`containsBlockedFlag`), `--bare`, `--disable-slash-commands`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--mcp-config`, `--accept-hooks`, `--yolo`, `--trust`, `--no-alt-screen`, a token containing `dangerously`, `bypass`, `full-access` or `skip-permission`, `--tui` for Hermes, or Cursor's `-f` / `--force` (`hasCursorForceFlag({ command: "agent", args })`). Codex `-c` values must be the exact notification options or `codexBrainArgs` keys. Values (folders, ids, models) are checked by shape. Every per-agent lookup uses `Object.hasOwn` or a `Map`, so `"constructor"` and other prototype names are refused.

#### `pty-host.js` (S4)

- `PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON = "Agent OS could not load its terminal module on this computer."`
- `ptyAvailable()` → `Promise<{ ok: true, reason: null } | { ok: false, reason: string }>`. Loads node-pty once and runs `node -e "process.exit(0)"` in a PTY once; a missing module is final, a failed probe is retried after 30 s.
- `spawnPty({ command, args = [], cwd, env, cols = 120, rows = 32, tracker })` → `PtyHandle` `{ pid, write(data), resize(cols, rows), kill(signal = "SIGTERM"), pause(), resume(), onData(cb) → unsubscribe, onExit(cb) → unsubscribe }`.
  - `command` and `cwd` absolute, `args` a string array, `env` an explicit object; otherwise `TypeError`. Errors carry `code: "pty_unavailable"` (S6 answers 503) or `code: "spawn_failed"`.
  - `onExit` delivers `{ exitCode: number | null, signal: string | null }`: the signal as a name (`"SIGTERM"`), and `exitCode: null` when a signal ended it. A listener added after the end is still called once.
  - Output before the first `onData` listener is kept (up to 1 MB) and handed to it.
  - `trackPid(pid, handle.onExit)` right after the spawn; `untrackPid(pid)` on exit. `tracker` and `setPtyLoaderForTests(fn | null)` are for tests only.

#### `mirror.js` (S4)

- `createMirror({ cols, rows, onQueryReply, onAlert, now = Date.now })` → `Mirror`:
  - `write(chunk)`; `resize(cols, rows)` (cols 2-500, rows 1-200, else ignored); `dispose()`;
  - `snapshot()` → `Promise<{ data, cols, rows, modes }>`, covering exactly the chunks written before the call. `modes = { altScreen: boolean, bracketedPaste: boolean, mouseTracking: "none" | "x10" | "vt200" | "drag" | "any", mouseEncoding: "default" | "sgr" | "sgr-pixels", focusReporting: boolean, cursorKeysApp: boolean, kittyFlags: number }`. `data` already restores the alternate screen, bracketed paste, focus reporting, cursor keys and mouse tracking; the client applies only `mouseEncoding` and `kittyFlags` after writing it;
  - `setWriterAttached(boolean)`: while false, DA1 (`ESC[?1;2c`), cursor position (`ESC[<row>;<col>R`) and kitty (`ESC[?<flags>u`) replies go to `onQueryReply(reply)`; every other reply is dropped, and nothing is sent while a writer is attached;
  - `onCountedOutput(cb)` → unsubscribe: at most every 250 ms, when the text above the bottom 6 rows changed or the screen scrolled.
  - `onAlert(raw)`: `"bel"` or `"<osc number>;<payload>"` (for example `"9;Approval requested"`, `"777;notify;Codex;Waiting"`), capped at 4096 characters.
  - Uses `@xterm/addon-unicode11` with `allowProposedApi: true`, so wide characters measure as in the browser terminal.
- `isUserInput(data)` → `false` for a frame made only of terminal replies (DA, cursor position, status, kitty flags, mode reports, XTVERSION, DECRQSS, OSC colour replies), focus reports (`ESC[I`, `ESC[O`) or mouse-motion reports; `true` for keys, paste, clicks and the wheel; `false` for an empty frame.
- `COUNTED_BOTTOM_ROWS = 6`, `COUNTED_CHECK_MS = 250`, `MIRROR_SCROLLBACK = 1000`, `ALERT_RAW_LIMIT = 4096`.

#### `recorder.js` (S5)

- `CAST_FILE = "screen.cast"`, `PREV_CAST_FILE = "screen.prev.cast"`, `SEGMENT_BYTES = 26214400`, `RECORDING_CAP_BYTES = 1073741824`, `ROTATION_MARKER = "[earlier output removed]"`, `RESUME_MARKER = "--- resumed ---"`.
- `createRecorder({ dir, cols, rows, segmentBytes = 26214400, append = false, now = Date.now, onError })` → `{ output(chunk), marker(text), resize(cols, rows), close() }`.
  - asciicast v2, output events only, never input; writes in order in the background; event times never go backwards.
  - `marker(text)` writes an `"m"` event; `resize(cols, rows)` an `"r"` event `"<cols>x<rows>"`; `close()` returns the same Promise every time and resolves when everything is on disk.
  - Rotation at `segmentBytes`: `screen.cast` becomes `screen.prev.cast`, and the new segment starts with the rotation marker.
  - `append: true` (resume) writes the `"m"` event `"--- resumed ---"` and an `"r"` event itself (a new header when no recording is left); the manager never writes this marker.
  - A recording that cannot be written calls `onError(error)` once (default one `console.warn`) and ignores further output; it never throws into the session.
- `listRecordings({ isLive } = {})` → `[{ sessionId, kind, agentId, agentLabel, folder, folderName, folderShown, startedAt, endedAt, bytes, live }]`, newest `startedAt` first; only sessions with a valid id folder, a readable meta.json and at least one cast file.
- `enforceRecordingCap({ capBytes = 1073741824, isLive } = {})` → `Promise<{ deleted: string[] }>`: while over the cap, deletes the cast files of the ended recording with the oldest `endedAt` (else `startedAt`); never a live one; keeps meta.json (the ended tab and Resume stay); one run at a time.
- `recordingsRemovedByCap()` → how many recordings the cap removed since the server started.
- `deleteRecording(sessionId, { isLive } = {})` → `{ ok: true }`; removes only the two cast files; throws `unknown_session`, `recording_live` or `recording_missing`.
- `openRecording(sessionId)` → `{ lines: AsyncGenerator<string> }`: one header line (the older segment's when it exists), the older segment's events, then the newer segment's events without its header and leading rotation marker; each line ends with `"\n"`; a last line still being written is left out; throws `unknown_session` or `recording_missing` before anything is streamed.
- `isLive(id)` lets the caller say which sessions run right now: the manager passes `(id) => live.has(id)` (a session still flushing its recording counts as live); the routes pass the manager's own `isLive` (`(id) => manager.isLive(id)`, ruling R8). Without it, meta.json decides.

#### `manager.js` (S6, S7)

- Constants: `IDLE_AFTER_MS = 20000`, `PAUSE_LAG_BYTES = 524288`, `PAUSED_DROP_MS = 10000`, `CLOSE_LAG_BYTES = 4194304`, `MAX_INPUT_BYTES = 65536` (S6); `STOP_GRACE_MS = 3000`, `SHUTDOWN_GUARD_MS = 7000` (S7).
- Re-exports: `SESSION_ID_RE`, `isSessionId`, `sessionError` (from `errors.js`) and `SESSION_AGENT_LABEL` (from `profiles.js`). Also `readGitBranch(folder)` → `string | null`.
- `createSessionManager({ now, spawn = spawnPty, buildProfile = buildSessionProfile, recorderFactory = createRecorder, mirrorFactory = createMirror, maxLive = 8, isExecutionAllowed = isExecutionEnabled, checkFolder = checkSessionFolder, ptyCheck = ptyAvailable, detect, resolveBrain, readSettings = readSessionSettings, enforceCap = enforceRecordingCap, killTree = killProcessTree, softStop = runSoftStop } = {})` (all optional; `detect` defaults to `(agentId) => getAdapter(agentId).detect()`, `resolveBrain` to `(agentId) => resolveBrainForRun(agentId, undefined, { prepare: true })`). `getSessionManager()` returns one manager per server and registers `registerShutdownTask("sessions", () => manager.shutdownAll({ reason: "quit" }))`. Session ids are `crypto.randomUUID()` (Q39).
- `SessionSummary` (every item of `GET /api/sessions`, and the answer of `create`, `get`, `resume`, `dismiss`):
  `{ id, kind: "agent" | "update", agentId, agentLabel, folder, folderName, folderShown: boolean, branch: string | null, status: SessionStatus, stateSince: string, startedAt: string, endedAt: string | null, exitCode: number | null, signal: string | null, endedBy: "stop" | "quit" | null, dismissed: boolean, brain: { kind: "plan" | "openrouter" | "local", label: string } | null, resume: { available: boolean, reason: string | null, fallback: boolean }, alerts: "basic", recordingBytes: number }`
  - `SessionStatus = "starting" | "live" | "waiting" | "idle" | "held" | "exited"`; `waiting` and `held` are never produced in SP3 (SP4).
  - `stateSince` is when the current status began (ISO). `exitCode` is `null` when a signal ended the process; `signal` is a name. `recordingBytes` is 0 when the recording was removed.
- Methods:

  | Method | Answer |
  |---|---|
  | `create({ agentId, folder })` | `Promise<SessionSummary>`; `folder` is `null` for OpenClaw while `OPENCLAW_FOLDER_HONOURED` is false. Checks the agent, Look only, the terminal module and the folder policy in that order (a Look only refusal comes before a folder refusal), and the live limit |
  | `createUpdateSession({ agentId, folder })` | `Promise<SessionSummary>`; Hermes only (400 `update_not_available` otherwise; an agent outside `SESSION_AGENTS` is `unknown_agent`); the folder passes the folder policy; not gated by Safety; not counted toward 8; at most one at a time (`update_running`); `brain: null` |
  | `list({ includeUpdate = false } = {})` | `Promise<SessionSummary[]>`, sorted by `createdAt`, dismissed sessions included (the UI filters) |
  | `get(id)` | `Promise<SessionSummary>`; `unknown_session` |
  | `resume(id)` | `Promise<SessionSummary>`; only an ended `agent` session; same id and tab, new process, `status` back to `starting`, `dismissed: false`, the recorder in `append: true` |
  | `dismiss(id)` | `Promise<SessionSummary>`; only an ended session (`session_live` otherwise); stored in meta.json |
  | `attach(id, { id, send(frame), close(reason) })` | `Promise<{ snapshot, detach() }>`; see the WebSocket protocol; throws `session_ended` for an ended session |
  | `focus(id, attachmentId)`, `write(id, attachmentId, data)`, `resize(id, attachmentId, cols, rows)`, `ack(id, attachmentId, seq)` | `boolean`, synchronous (false = dropped: not the writer, out of bounds, `data` over 64 KB in UTF-8 bytes, unknown session or window) |
  | `stop(id, { by = "stop" } = {})` | `Promise<SessionSummary & { note: string \| null }>`; stopping an ended session answers its unchanged summary; two Stops of one session share one sequence |
  | `quitCheck()` | `Promise<{ live: [{ id, title, kind }] }>`, every live session of both kinds; an update's title is "<agent> update" |
  | `isLive(id)` | `boolean`, synchronous: `live.has(id)`, true from the spawn until the session's recording is closed and its meta.json written (a session still closing its recording counts as live, ruling R8); S8 hands it to `listRecordings` and `deleteRecording` |
  | `shutdownAll({ reason = "quit" } = {})` | `Promise<{ stopped: number }>` |
  | `recoverStaleSessions()` | `Promise<{ recovered: number }>`: every meta.json still `"starting"` becomes `"exited"` with `endedBy: "quit"` ("Ended when Agent OS quit."), Resume available |

- Activity (every SP3 session is "basic"): `starting` → `live` on the first output of any kind or user input (`isUserInput`); `live` → `idle` after 20 s without counted output; `idle` → `live` on counted output or user input; any → `exited` when the process ends. Counted output in the 1 s after an applied resize is not activity.
- After each exit the manager closes the recording, writes meta.json, then calls `enforceCap({ isLive: (id) => live.has(id) })`; a session leaves the `live` map only after its recording is closed. An applied writer resize also calls `recorder.resize(cols, rows)`.

#### Stop and quit (S7): `soft-stop.js` and `manager.js`

- `soft-stop.js`: `SOFT_STOP_LIMIT_MS = 2000`; `OPENCLAW_STOP_NOTE = "Stopped the terminal. OpenClaw may still be finishing its last step."`; `findBackgroundAgent(text, { agentSessionId, pid })` → `string | null` (accepts an array, `{ agents }` or `{ sessions }`, entries with `kind` or `type` `"background"`, matched by `id` / `sessionId` / `session_id` or `pid`; never an id starting with `-`); `runCli(command, args, { env, cwd, signal, onSpawn })` → `Promise<{ ok, code, aborted, stdout }>` (never rejects); `runSoftStop({ softStop, command, env, cwd, agentSessionId, pid, limitMs = 2000, run = runCli, onSpawn })` → `{ outcome: "none" | "terminal-only" | "stopped-background" | "failed" | "timeout", note: string | null }`.
- Stop sequence (never writes into the PTY): the soft stop with a hard 2 s limit for the whole step (Claude: `claude agents --json`, then `claude stop <id>` when this session is a background session; OpenClaw: no CLI call until spike S5, `note: OPENCLAW_STOP_NOTE`; others and `update` sessions: none), then `killTree(pid, { graceMs: STOP_GRACE_MS })`. Soft-stop CLI calls use the session's own `profile.env` and `profile.cwd` (Q11) and are `spawnTracked` children.
- `shutdownAll({ reason: "quit" })` writes `endedBy: "quit"` and `status: "exited"` into every live session's meta.json BEFORE any kill, then stops all sessions in parallel, capped at `SHUTDOWN_GUARD_MS`.

#### `routes.js`, `local-session.js`, `server/index.js` (S8)

- `server/runtime/local-session.js`: `export function isLocalMode()` (not the public demo, not `HERMES_AGENT_OS_REQUIRE_AUTH=1`, not `HERMES_AGENT_OS_PUBLIC_MODE=1`) and `export function requireLocalMode(req, res, next)` → 404 `{ error: "not_available" }` outside local mode. Every sessions route and recordings route use it; the WebSocket (S9) cannot use Express middleware, so it calls `isLocalMode()` in its own upgrade check and answers 403.
- `createSessionsRouter({ manager = getSessionManager() } = {})` at `/api/sessions` and `createRecordingsRouter({ manager = getSessionManager() } = {})` at `/api/recordings`; fixed paths before `/:id`. Any `:id` failing `SESSION_ID_RE` is 404 `unknown_session` before anything else runs.

  | Method and path | Answer |
  |---|---|
  | `GET /api/sessions[?kind=all]` | 200 `{ sessions: SessionSummary[], environmentNotice: string \| null, pty: { ok: boolean, reason: string \| null }, maxLive: 8 }`; agent kind only unless `kind=all` (Q24); `environmentNotice` is `(await getLoginShellEnv()).notice`, `null` until the login shell has been read |
  | `POST /api/sessions` `{ agentId, folder }` | 201 `SessionSummary`; the manager's refusals with their own status |
  | `GET /api/sessions/folders` | 200 `{ folders: [{ path, name, lastUsedAt }] }` |
  | `GET /api/sessions/settings` | 200 `{ claudeFullscreen }` |
  | `PUT /api/sessions/settings` `{ claudeFullscreen: boolean }` | 200 the new settings; 400 `invalid_settings` |
  | `POST /api/sessions/quit-check` | 200 `{ live: [{ id, title, kind }] }` |
  | `GET /api/sessions/:id` | 200 `SessionSummary`; 404 `unknown_session` |
  | `POST /api/sessions/:id/stop` | 200 `SessionSummary & { note: string \| null }`, bare (no wrapper object); an ended session answers its unchanged summary |
  | `POST /api/sessions/:id/resume` | 200 `SessionSummary`; 409 `not_resumable`, `session_live`, `execution_gate_off` |
  | `POST /api/sessions/:id/dismiss` | 200 `SessionSummary`; 409 `session_live` |
  | `GET /api/sessions/:id/recording` | 200 `Content-Type: application/x-asciicast`, the lines of `openRecording(id)` (Q26); 404 `unknown_session`, `recording_missing` |
  | `DELETE /api/sessions/:id/recording` | 200 `{ ok: true }`; 409 `recording_live`; 404 `unknown_session`, `recording_missing` |
  | `GET /api/recordings` | 200 `{ recordings: RecordingSummary[], removedByCap: number }` |

  An unexpected error is 500 `internal_error`. The recordings routes pass the manager's `isLive` (`(id) => manager.isLive(id)`, ruling R8) to the recorder.
- `server/index.js`: a module-scope `const sessionManager = getSessionManager();`; the port is `parsePort(process.env.AGENT_OS_PORT ?? process.env.PORT)` (Q11a); right after `const envFile = loadLocalEnv({ root });` it calls `excludeFromSessionEnv(envFile.applied)`. Before `app.listen`: `sessionManager.recoverStaleSessions()` and `enforceRecordingCap()`, each in its own try/catch (a failure is logged, the server still starts; Q13). After `AGENT_OS_READY`, in local mode only, `getLoginShellEnv()` starts resolving and never delays READY (Q23).

#### `ws.js` and the WebSocket protocol (S9)

- `MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1048576`, `MAX_CLIENT_FRAME_BYTES = 65536`.
- `CLOSE_CODES = { too_far_behind: 4000, session_ended: 4001, attach_failed: 4004 }`; the close reason text is the same word, and clients decide by the reason word, never the number (U1's `sessionCloseAdvice`). ws itself closes with 1009 when a message is over 1 MB.
- `allowedOrigins(port, env = process.env)`; `checkUpgradeRequest(req, { port })` → `{ ok: true, sessionId } | { ok: false, reason }` (pure; `reason` is for tests only, never sent or logged); `parseClientFrame(data, isBinary)` → `{ t: "focus" } | { t: "in", d } | { t: "resize", cols, rows } | { t: "ack", seq } | null`; `attachSessionsUpgrade(server, { getPort, manager })` installs the one `upgrade` listener.
- `scripts/dev-server.mjs` sets `process.env.AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN = "1"` and imports `server/index.js`; `npm run dev` = `concurrently "node --watch scripts/dev-server.mjs" "vite --host 127.0.0.1"`. `vite.config.ts`: the `/api` proxy gains `ws: true`.
- Upgrade (Security 1): path `/api/sessions/<id>/attach` checked lower-cased, no query string, Host allowlisted with the real bound port, Origin exactly `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` or `http://localhost:<port>` (the Vite dev origin on 5173 only with `AGENT_OS_DEV_ORIGIN=1`, ignored when `NODE_ENV=production` or `AGENT_OS_PACKAGED=1`; `AGENT_OS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` never widens the Origin list), the session cookie compared with `timingSafeEqual`, local mode. An unknown id, an ended session (`manager.get(id)` says `exited`) and any other upgrade address are refused the same way: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`, socket destroyed.
- Frames (JSON text, one message per frame). Client → server: `{t:"focus"}` (makes this attachment the writer; the client sends `{t:"resize"}` right after), `{t:"in", d}` (writer only; the whole raw frame at most 64 KB), `{t:"resize", cols, rows}` (writer only, debounced 50 ms, cols 2-500, rows 1-200), `{t:"ack", seq}` (at least every 64 KB received and processed). A frame over 64 KB, a binary frame, non-JSON or an unknown frame is dropped without an answer; the socket stays open.
- Server → client, in this order on attach (the manager sends them; `ws.js` never sends a snapshot): `{t:"snapshot", data, cols, rows, modes}`, then `{t:"state", status, exitCode, signal, endedBy, resetAt}` (`exitCode`, `signal`, `endedBy` only with `exited`, `resetAt` only with `held` in SP4; the client reads a missing field as `null`), then the output and alerts that arrived while the snapshot was taken, then live `{t:"out", seq, d}` and `{t:"alert", raw}`. `seq` is the cumulative UTF-8 byte count of all `d` sent to this attachment, from 0 after its snapshot.
- Terminal queries: while a writer is attached only its browser terminal answers (viewers' replies are dropped); while none is attached the mirror answers DA1, DSR cursor position and kitty `CSI ? u`.
- Back-pressure, per attachment `lag = bytes sent - last acked seq`: pause the PTY only when every open attachment lags more than `PAUSE_LAG_BYTES`; resume when any one catches up; never pause with zero attachments; a closed attachment leaves the count at once; an attachment more than `CLOSE_LAG_BYTES` behind is closed with `too_far_behind`; a PTY paused for more than `PAUSED_DROP_MS` closes every attachment still over 512 KB behind with `too_far_behind`, so the PTY resumes. That timer is not cleared just because one attachment closes; it stops when the PTY resumes or the process exits.
- When `attach` fails after the upgrade, the socket closes with 4001 `session_ended` for a `session_ended` error and 4004 `attach_failed` otherwise. Stopping a session closes its attachments with `session_ended`. No shutdown task closes sockets.

#### Hold to stop all (S10, `src/ui/stopAllShared.ts` and `src/ui/stopAll.ts`)

- `interface StoppableSession { id: string; status: string; kind?: string; agentId?: string; agentLabel?: string; folderName?: string; folderShown?: boolean }` (a `SessionSummary` fits it).
- `StopAllDeps` gains `listSessions(): Promise<{ sessions: StoppableSession[] }>` (`GET /api/sessions?kind=all`) and `stopSession(id): Promise<unknown>` (`POST /api/sessions/:id/stop`), both kinds of session. `StopLook` gains `sessions` and `sessionsChecked`. `StopAllResult` gains `sessions`, `sessionsStopped`, `sessionsFailed`, `sessionsTimedOut`, `sessionsAlreadyEnded`, `sessionsChecked: boolean` and `openClawStopped`.
- `SESSION_ALREADY_ENDED = "session_already_ended"`; `withSessionAnswers(deps)` (a `not_available` list is empty; `unknown_session`, or a stop answer `{ status: "exited" }` with `endedBy !== "stop"`, is `SESSION_ALREADY_ENDED`); `thingsWord(runs, rooms, sessions = 0)`; `sessionStopTitle(session)` (the same words as `sessionTitle`).
- Sessions and rooms start together; runs follow the rooms and never wait for sessions. Never calls a service control (`adapter.service`, `POST /api/agents/:id/service/:action`).
- The palette item `stop-all` reads "Stop all agent work" and its dialog "Stop all agent work?"; the hold control keeps "Hold to stop all".

### Desktop shell (D1, `desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`)

- Events: shell → page `"agentos://quit-requested"` (payload `null`); page → shell `"agentos://quit-shown"` (any payload) and `"agentos://quit-answer"` with `{ "quit": true | false }` (anything else ignored). `listen` and `emit` are in `core:default`; no custom command.
- The shell shows, unminimizes and focuses the main window before it emits `quit-requested`. No `quit-shown` within 2 s (`QUIT_SHOWN_WAIT`) means no window can ask: it quits. After `quit-shown` it waits for the answer with no time limit; another quit request while the question is open does nothing; a page load (`Builder::on_page_load`) drops an open question, so the next quit request asks again.
- Routes that ask: the "Quit Agent OS" item and ⌘Q, `RunEvent::ExitRequested` (last window destroyed, `app.exit()`), and closing the window on Windows and Linux. Routes that cannot ask (Q5a, Q5b): a termination signal to the app, the Dock's Quit, the app switcher's Quit, logout and the updater's restart; they run the graceful stdin stop without the question.
- macOS: `CloseRequested` → `prevent_close()` + `hide()`; `RunEvent::Reopen` → show + focus; the app menu item "Show Agent OS" (`agentos-show`, no accelerator) does the same.
- Menu ids: `"agentos-quit"` ("Quit Agent OS"; accelerator `CmdOrCtrl+Q` on macOS only), `"agentos-show"`; `"reload"` stays. Windows and Linux: Reload has no accelerator, and the predefined Edit, Window and Hide items are left out (their Ctrl accelerators cannot be removed).
- Server: `spawn_server` sets `AGENT_OS_PORT=0` (never `PORT`), `AGENT_OS_STDIN_SHUTDOWN=1` and `AGENT_OS_LAUNCH_PATH` (the app's own `PATH`, `env::var_os("PATH").unwrap_or_default()`, empty when it had none; S2's login-shell read starts the shell with it, H2, Q11a). The server's own `PATH` stays `server_path_env()`. Its stdin is piped and kept open for the app's whole life. On quit it writes `AGENT_OS_SHUTDOWN\n`, waits up to `QUIT_GRACE` (10 s), then forces the server at once (SIGKILL on unix, `taskkill /T /F` on Windows); if the line cannot be written, unix sends SIGTERM at once.
- `tauri_plugin_dialog::init()` is registered; `"dialog:allow-open"` is last in the pinned permissions of `capabilities/default.json` and `test/release-config.test.js`; the capability description names quit and the folder picker. The opener scope stays as the owner approved (commit `8264b2b`).
- Rust unit tests: `cargo test --locked` in `desktop/src-tauri` (18 tests; 15 on Windows).

- `scripts/node-pty-bundle.mjs`: `parseTargetArgs(argv, { platform = process.platform, arch = process.arch } = {})` → `{ platform, arch }`; `binaryArches(buffer)` → `("x64" | "arm64")[]` (reads the Mach-O, ELF or PE header); `copyNodePty({ from, to, platform, arch })` → `{ prebuild: "<platform>-<arch>", files: string[], bytes: number }`.
- The copy: `lib/` (without `.map` and `.test.js`), `package.json` and `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/` (without `.pdb`) into `build/server/node_modules/node-pty/`; it fails when that prebuild is missing, checks every copied `.node`, `.dll`, `.exe` and `spawn-helper` by its header, and checks `spawn-helper`'s mode 0755 (darwin).
- `node scripts/build-server-bundle.mjs [--platform p] [--arch a]`: esbuild keeps `node-pty`, `bufferutil` and `utf-8-validate` external; `bundle.json` gains `target: "<platform>-<arch>"`. `node scripts/prepare-desktop.mjs [--skip-node] [--platform p] [--arch a]` passes them on and copies node-pty before its `--skip-node` return; `release.yml` passes `matrix.node_platform` and `matrix.node_arch`.

`SessionKind`, `SessionStatus`, `SessionEndedBy`, `SessionSummary` (the server shape above), `SessionListResponse`, `StopSessionResult` (`SessionSummary & { note: string | null }`), `SessionSettings`, `SessionFolder`, `SessionFolderList`, `QuitCheckItem` (`{ id, title, kind: SessionKind }`), `QuitCheckResponse`, `RecordingSummary` (the recorder's list item, `kind` and `folderShown` required), `RecordingListResponse` (`{ recordings, removedByCap: number }`), `MouseTrackingMode`, `MouseEncodingMode`, `SessionModes`, `SessionSnapshot`, `SessionStateFrame` (`{ status, exitCode, signal, endedBy, resetAt }`, each `null` when absent), `SessionServerFrame`, `SessionClientFrame`.

#### `src/sessionsApi.ts` (U1)

- `SESSION_LIMITS_MS` (every call has its own time limit; a time limit rejects with `new Error("Agent OS did not answer in time.")`). Refusals are the existing `ApiError` (`message` = the server's code, `detail` = its sentence).
- `listSessions(): Promise<SessionListResponse>`, `createSession({ agentId, folder }: { agentId: string; folder: string | null }): Promise<SessionSummary>` (no `confirm`), `stopSession(id): Promise<StopSessionResult>`, `resumeSession(id)`, `dismissSession(id): Promise<SessionSummary>`, `getSessionSettings()`, `putSessionSettings(patch: Partial<SessionSettings>): Promise<SessionSettings>`, `listSessionFolders(): Promise<SessionFolderList>`, `quitCheck(): Promise<QuitCheckResponse>`, `listRecordings(): Promise<RecordingListResponse>`, `deleteRecording(id): Promise<{ ok: true }>`; `sessionProblem(error)`, `sessionGotNoAnswer(error)`, `sessionSocketUrl(id)`.
- `openSessionSocket(id, { onSnapshot, onOut, onState, onAlert, onClose })` → `{ focus(), input(data), resize(cols, rows), close() }`. A promise returned by `onSnapshot` holds later frames; a promise returned by `onOut` counts its bytes as processed when it settles; `input` splits data into frames of at most 64 KB (JSON and all) without breaking a character; `ack` at least every 64 KB processed. `onClose({ code, reason, hadSnapshot, advice })`, `advice: "reattach" | "ended" | "wait"` (`too_far_behind` → reattach; `session_ended` → ended; `attach_failed` or 1009 → wait; anything else → reattach).

### Task W0: Install the approved packages (exact pins) and prove node-pty loads

SP3 runs each agent in a real terminal on the server (node-pty), mirrors that terminal on the server for reattach (`@xterm/headless` with the serialize and unicode11 addons), carries it to the page over a WebSocket (`ws`), and draws it in the page (`@xterm/xterm` and its addons). None of these packages is installed today (map-tests-harness 9, map-desktop-packaging 11). This task installs them, each at one exact version, and adds a small permanent test that proves, on every computer that runs `npm test` (the three CI systems included), that node-pty loads its prebuilt binary and runs a real program in a real terminal, and that the server-side pieces work in Node. Nothing in the app uses the packages yet; later tasks import them. The two Tauri page packages (`@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog`, `@tauri-apps/api`) are Task D1's (ruling R3), so this diff holds only the terminal packages.

**Why the xterm numbers are not "-beta.304" for every package (ruling R1).** xterm.js publishes all its packages from one commit, but each package counts its own betas. The set that belongs with `@xterm/xterm@6.1.0-beta.304` (git commit `c58ea36`, published 2026-08-30; the registry's `gitHead` is `c58ea3637f3968e0e6e79cd92cf9aace7ef89ee2` for every package below) is: headless `6.1.0-beta.303`, serialize `0.15.0-beta.301`, fit `0.12.0-beta.301`, unicode11 `0.10.0-beta.301`, search `0.17.0-beta.301`, web-links `0.13.0-beta.301`, clipboard `0.3.0-beta.303`, webgl `0.20.0-beta.300`. Each addon declares the peer `@xterm/xterm ^6.1.0-beta.304`. VS Code's main branch lists the same versions for the packages it uses (`microsoft/vscode` `package.json`: `@xterm/xterm ^6.1.0-beta.304`, `@xterm/headless ^6.1.0-beta.303`, `@xterm/addon-serialize ^0.15.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-unicode11 ^0.10.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-search ^0.17.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-clipboard ^0.3.0-beta.303`, `@xterm/addon-webgl ^0.20.0-beta.300`; checked 2026-10-15), which is what the spec asks for ("an exact build that VS Code uses", "the matching beta addons", "`@xterm/headless` matching"). The headless and addon builds numbered `-beta.304` come from later commits published on 2026-10-12; the addons need `@xterm/xterm` `^6.1.0-beta.305` (clipboard), `^6.1.0-beta.308` (fit, unicode11, search, web-links, serialize) or `^6.1.0-beta.310` (webgl) as a peer, and make `npm install` stop with `ERESOLVE`.

- Modify: `package-lock.json` (written by npm: 12 new `node_modules/…` entries, the 11 packages plus `node-addon-api@7.1.1`, which node-pty lists as its one dependency).
- Create: `test/session-deps.test.js`.
- Test: `test/session-deps.test.js`.

- Facts the later tasks rely on, each checked by `test/session-deps.test.js`:
  - `await import("node-pty")` gives `spawn` as a named export and on `.default`, and `createRequire(import.meta.url)("node-pty")` (the form W1 and S1 use) gives the same object (node-pty is CommonJS: `exports.spawn = spawn;` in `lib/index.js`). From `typings/node-pty.d.ts`: `spawn(file: string, args: string[] | string, options: IPtyForkOptions | IWindowsPtyForkOptions): IPty`; `IPty` has `readonly pid: number`, `onData: IEvent<string>`, `onExit: IEvent<{ exitCode: number, signal?: number }>`, `write(data: string | Buffer)`, `resize(columns, rows)`, `kill(signal?: string)` (default SIGHUP; "Will throw when signal is used on Windows"), `pause()`, `resume()`; `IEvent<T>` is `(listener: (e: T) => any) => IDisposable`.
  - `@xterm/headless`, `@xterm/addon-serialize` and `@xterm/addon-unicode11` are CommonJS/UMD builds whose names ESM cannot see (ruling R1): load them with a default import (`import xtermHeadless from "@xterm/headless"; const { Terminal } = xtermHeadless;`, the form S4's `mirror.js` uses) or with `createRequire` (`require("@xterm/headless").Terminal`), never `import { Terminal } from "@xterm/headless"`. Both forms give the same class.
  - On a headless terminal created with `allowProposedApi: true`, `loadAddon(new Unicode11Addon())` registers the version `"11"`, and `term.unicode.activeVersion = "11"` makes an emoji such as U+1F642 take two columns, as in the browser terminal (without it the headless terminal measures with Unicode 6 and gives it one).
  - `ws` has an ESM wrapper with named exports and a default export: `import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from "ws"`, and `(await import("ws")).default === WebSocket` (S9's Step 0 checks both).
  - node-pty ships prebuilt binaries in `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/` for darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64, win32-arm64 and win32-x64. macOS folders hold `pty.node` and `spawn-helper` (mode 0755 inside the package); Linux folders hold only `pty.node`; Windows folders hold `conpty.node`, `conpty_console_list.node`, their `.pdb` files and `conpty/` (`conpty.dll`, `OpenConsole.exe`). Its install script (`node scripts/prebuild.js || node-gyp rebuild`) compiles only when that folder is missing, so no compiler is needed on these systems (the Dockerfile's `node:20-bookworm-slim` included). At run time `loadNativeModule` (`lib/utils.js`) tries `build/Release`, then `build/Debug`, then `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>`. On Windows the post-install script (`scripts/post-install.js`) creates `build/Release/conpty/` with copies of `conpty.dll` and `OpenConsole.exe`; it compiles nothing, so "nothing was compiled" means no `.node` file under `build/`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the failing test.** Create `test/session-deps.test.js`:

```js
// The SP3 terminal packages (spec "Dependencies and packaging"; Task W0):
// each one is pinned to one exact version and installed; node-pty loads its
// prebuilt binary and runs a real program in a real terminal (a PTY); the
// server-side pieces (@xterm/headless with its serialize and unicode11
// addons, and ws) load and work in Node. Nothing here starts an agent.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { once } from "node:events";
import { existsSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";

// One xterm.js release (git commit c58ea36, 2026-08-30), the set VS Code's
// main branch lists. Each xterm package numbers its own betas.
const EXACT_PINS = {
  "node-pty": "1.2.0-beta.14",
  ws: "8.22.0",
  "@xterm/xterm": "6.1.0-beta.304",
  "@xterm/headless": "6.1.0-beta.303",
  "@xterm/addon-serialize": "0.15.0-beta.301",
  "@xterm/addon-fit": "0.12.0-beta.301",
  "@xterm/addon-unicode11": "0.10.0-beta.301",
  "@xterm/addon-search": "0.17.0-beta.301",
  "@xterm/addon-web-links": "0.13.0-beta.301",
  "@xterm/addon-clipboard": "0.3.0-beta.303",
  "@xterm/addon-webgl": "0.20.0-beta.300"
};

function readJson(file) {
  return JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, "utf8"));
}

// The xterm packages are CommonJS bundles whose names ESM cannot see, so they
// are loaded the way the mirror (Task S4) loads them: the default import holds
// the classes. A named import (`import { Terminal } from "@xterm/headless"`)
// does not work.
async function loadXterm() {
  const { Terminal } = (await import("@xterm/headless")).default;
  const { SerializeAddon } = (await import("@xterm/addon-serialize")).default;
  const { Unicode11Addon } = (await import("@xterm/addon-unicode11")).default;
  return { Terminal, SerializeAddon, Unicode11Addon };
}

// Resolves once the terminal has parsed the data (xterm parses asynchronously).
function writeAll(term, data) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => term.write(data, resolve));
}

// Runs one program in a real terminal and collects everything it printed.
async function runInPty(file, args, options) {
  const pty = require("node-pty");
  const term = pty.spawn(file, args, options);
  let output = "";
  term.onData((data) => {
    output += data;
  });
  const exit = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      try {
        term.kill();
      } catch {
        // already gone
      }
      reject(new Error(`no exit within 15 s; output so far: ${JSON.stringify(output)}`));
    }, 15000);
    term.onExit((info) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve(info);
    });
  });
  // The last bytes can arrive just after the exit event.
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 200));
  return { output, exit };
}

test("package.json pins every SP3 terminal package to one exact version, and that version is installed", () => {
  const pkg = readJson(path.join(root, "package.json"));
  for (const [name, version] of Object.entries(EXACT_PINS)) {
    assert.equal(pkg.dependencies?.[name], version, `package.json must pin ${name} to exactly ${version}`);
    const installed = path.join(root, "node_modules", ...name.split("/"), "package.json");
    assert.ok(existsSync(installed), `${name} is not installed; run npm ci`);
    assert.equal(readJson(installed).version, version, `installed version of ${name}`);
  }
});

test("node-pty loads as a named ESM export, as the default export and through require", async () => {
  const mod = await import("node-pty");
  assert.equal(typeof mod.default.spawn, "function");
  assert.equal(typeof mod.spawn, "function", "named export (pty-host.js may use either form)");
  assert.equal(require("node-pty").spawn, mod.default.spawn, "require and import give the same module");
});

test("node-pty uses its prebuilt binary for this computer (nothing was compiled)", () => {
  const pkgDir = path.join(root, "node_modules", "node-pty");
  const dir = path.join(pkgDir, "prebuilds", `${process.platform}-${process.arch}`);
  assert.ok(existsSync(dir), `node-pty has no prebuilt binary for ${process.platform}-${process.arch}`);
  assert.ok(existsSync(path.join(dir, isWindows ? "conpty.node" : "pty.node")));
  if (process.platform === "darwin") {
    const helper = path.join(dir, "spawn-helper");
    assert.ok(existsSync(helper), "macOS needs spawn-helper beside pty.node");
    assert.notEqual(statSync(helper).mode & 0o111, 0, "spawn-helper must be executable, or every spawn fails");
  }
  // node-pty loads build/Release before prebuilds/, so a compiled copy would win.
  // (On Windows its post-install step copies conpty.dll into build/Release/conpty/;
  // that folder is expected and is not a compiled binary.)
  for (const folder of ["Release", "Debug"]) {
    for (const name of ["pty.node", "conpty.node", "conpty_console_list.node"]) {
      const compiled = path.join(pkgDir, "build", folder, name);
      assert.equal(existsSync(compiled), false, `node-pty was compiled from source (${compiled}) instead of using its prebuilt binary`);
    }
  }
});

test("node-pty runs a program in a real terminal and reports its exit code", async () => {
  const { output, exit } = isWindows
    ? await runInPty(process.env.ComSpec || "cmd.exe", ["/d", "/c", "echo pty-ok"], {
        cols: 80,
        rows: 24,
        cwd: os.tmpdir(),
        env: process.env
      })
    : await runInPty("/bin/echo", ["pty-ok"], {
        name: "xterm-256color",
        cols: 80,
        rows: 24,
        cwd: os.tmpdir(),
        env: { PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin", TERM: "xterm-256color" }
      });
  assert.match(output, /pty-ok/);
  assert.equal(exit.exitCode, 0);
});

test(
  "the program sees a terminal of the size we asked for, not a pipe",
  { skip: isWindows ? "test -t and stty are POSIX tools" : false },
  async () => {
    const { output, exit } = await runInPty(
      "/bin/sh",
      ["-c", "if test -t 0 && test -t 1; then echo is-a-tty; fi; stty size"],
      { name: "xterm-256color", cols: 100, rows: 30, cwd: os.tmpdir(), env: { PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin", TERM: "xterm-256color" } }
    );
    assert.match(output, /is-a-tty/);
    assert.match(output, /30 100/);
    assert.equal(exit.exitCode, 0);
  }
);

test("@xterm/headless and its serialize addon load in Node and copy a screen exactly", async () => {
  const { Terminal, SerializeAddon } = await loadXterm();
  assert.equal(require("@xterm/headless").Terminal, Terminal, "createRequire gives the same class");
  const term = new Terminal({ cols: 40, rows: 5, allowProposedApi: true });
  const serializer = new SerializeAddon();
  term.loadAddon(serializer);
  await writeAll(term, "hello\r\n\x1b[1mbold\x1b[22m");
  const data = serializer.serialize();
  assert.match(data, /hello/);
  assert.match(data, /bold/);

  const copy = new Terminal({ cols: 40, rows: 5, allowProposedApi: true });
  await writeAll(copy, data);
  assert.equal(copy.buffer.active.getLine(0).translateToString(true), "hello");
  assert.equal(copy.buffer.active.getLine(1).translateToString(true), "bold");
  term.dispose();
  copy.dispose();
});

test("the unicode11 addon works on the headless terminal: an emoji takes two columns, as in the browser terminal", async () => {
  const { Terminal, Unicode11Addon } = await loadXterm();
  // Without the addon the headless terminal measures with Unicode 6, where this emoji is one column.
  const plain = new Terminal({ cols: 20, rows: 2, allowProposedApi: true });
  await writeAll(plain, "\u{1F642}x");
  assert.equal(plain.buffer.active.cursorX, 2);
  plain.dispose();

  const term = new Terminal({ cols: 20, rows: 2, allowProposedApi: true });
  term.loadAddon(new Unicode11Addon());
  assert.ok(term.unicode.versions.includes("11"), `versions: ${term.unicode.versions.join(", ")}`);
  term.unicode.activeVersion = "11";
  await writeAll(term, "\u{1F642}x");
  assert.equal(term.buffer.active.cursorX, 3, "with Unicode 11 the emoji takes two columns, then x one");
  term.dispose();
});

test("ws loads with named and default ESM exports and echoes a message over a local WebSocket", async () => {
  const wsModule = await import("ws");
  const { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } = wsModule;
  assert.equal(wsModule.default, WebSocket, "the default export is the WebSocket class");
  const server = new WebSocketServer({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: 0 });
  await once(server, "listening");
  server.on("connection", (socket) => socket.on("message", (data) => socket.send(`echo:${data}`)));
  const client = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`);
  try {
    await once(client, "open");
    client.send("hi");
    const [reply] = await once(client, "message");
    assert.equal(String(reply), "echo:hi");
  } finally {
    client.terminate();
    for (const socket of server.clients) socket.terminate();
    await new Promise((resolve) => server.close(() => resolve()));
  }
});
```

(API notes: `Terminal.write(data: string | Uint8Array, callback?: () => void)`, `buffer.active.getLine(y): IBufferLine | undefined` with `translateToString(trimRight?)`, `buffer.active.cursorX`, `unicode: IUnicodeHandling` (`versions`, `activeVersion`; a proposed API, hence `allowProposedApi: true`) and `allowProposedApi?: boolean` are from `@xterm/headless/typings/xterm-headless.d.ts`; `SerializeAddon.serialize(options?: ISerializeOptions): string` from `@xterm/addon-serialize/typings/addon-serialize.d.ts`; `Unicode11Addon` from `@xterm/addon-unicode11/typings/addon-unicode11.d.ts`. U+1F642 is one column in xterm's Unicode 6 table (above U+FFFF only U+20000 to U+3FFFD are wide) and two in the addon's Unicode 11 table (wide range U+1F5FB to U+1F64F). `ws`'s `WebSocketServer.close(cb)` waits for open connections, hence the `terminate()` calls first.)

### Task W1: Test runner with the no-real-agents watcher; TUI-like fake agents

The spec's first SP3 rule is that no test may ever start a real agent: "build `test/helpers/no-real-agents.js`. It polls `ps` during the test run and fails the test if a real `claude`, `codex`, `agent`, `hermes` or `openclaw` binary from outside the fakes folder starts. Every SP3 to SP5 test runs under it." Today `npm test` is a bare `node --test`, which also runs every `.js` file under `test/` as a test (helpers and fakes included), and an `--import` hook would start one watcher per test file (map-tests-harness 1 and 12). So, per planning decisions Q1, Q1a and Q1b, this task:
- adds `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, which takes one baseline of running processes, runs `node --test` on the explicit list `test/*.test.js`, polls `ps` every 200 ms, and fails the run when a real agent CLI started below it;
- puts the watcher's logic in pure, tested functions in `test/helpers/no-real-agents.js`;
- adds the TUI-like fake agent every later SP3 task uses (`test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs`, reached through shims written by `test/helpers/fake-agents.js`), so tests can drive echo, a prompt, bracketed paste, the alternate screen, BEL, OSC 9/99/777, terminal queries (at once or after a delay), exit codes, a setsid grandchild, the Claude Stop CLI calls and an updater question, inside a real terminal (and a headless run that keeps running until it is stopped, outside one);
- gives the tests a stand-in login shell (`test/fakes/login-shell.sh`, planning decision Q1c): from Task S8 on, every server a test starts in local mode reads its login shell (`$SHELL -i -l -c`). The runner sets `SHELL` to this file for the whole run, so that read never runs the owner's startup files, and a real login `sh` never runs macOS's `path_helper`, which would put `/usr/local/bin` and `/opt/homebrew/bin` ahead of a test's fake folder. It is the only `SHELL` any test uses;
- switches `npm test` to the runner.

The owner's Mac always runs real `claude` processes (the Claude desktop app and its plugins), so the watcher counts only processes that descend from the runner and were not running when it started (map-tests-harness 8). A pid it once saw below the runner stays watched after its parent exits, unless the system reused that pid for a different command (so the owner's own `claude` is never flagged or stopped). Besides names, the watcher knows where the real agents install themselves (an npm package folder, Claude's and Cursor's `versions` folders, Hermes's venv): a process run from one of those places counts even inside the temp folder, because a real agent can be installed under a temp HOME. Nothing in this task starts a real agent: the planted "claude" in the tests is a shell script that only sleeps.

**Files:**
- Create: `scripts/run-tests.mjs`.
- Create: `test/helpers/no-real-agents.js`.
- Create: `test/helpers/fake-agents.js`.
- Create: `test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs`.
- Create: `test/fakes/login-shell.sh` (mode 0755).
- Modify: `package.json` line 20 (the `"test"` script).
- Test: `test/no-real-agents.test.js` (new), `test/fake-agents.test.js` (new).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: W0's `node-pty@1.2.0-beta.14`, loaded with `createRequire(import.meta.url)("node-pty")`; its `spawn(file, args, options)` returns an `IPty` with `pid`, `onData(listener)`, `onExit(listener)` giving `{ exitCode, signal? }`, `write(data)` and `kill(signal?)` (`typings/node-pty.d.ts`).
- Produces:
  - `npm test` = `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`. With no arguments it runs `test/*.test.js` (never `test/helpers/` or `test/fakes/`). Arguments are passed on: anything starting with `-` is a `node --test` flag (use the `--flag=value` form), anything else is a test file and replaces the default list (`npm test -- test/portable.test.js`). A clean run ends with `no-real-agents watcher: no real agent started (<n> checks)`. On a violation it prints `no-real-agents watcher: a real "<name>" started during the tests (pid <pid>, <binary>, from <test file>). Sent it SIGTERM.`, sends SIGTERM to that process, and exits 1 after the tests end, even if every test passed. On Windows it prints `no-real-agents watcher: not available on Windows` and runs the tests unwatched. The tests run with `ZDOTDIR`, `ENV`, `BASH_ENV` and `HERMES_AGENT_OS_EXECUTABLE_PATHS` removed (the last is detection's extra folders, which `server/runtime/safety.js` `executableSearchDirs()` searches before `PATH`, so a real agent there would be found ahead of a test's fakes) and, except on Windows, `SHELL` set to `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL`. Every later test that starts `server/index.js` also sets `SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` in that server's environment itself, so a single file run with `node --test` is safe too; no test sets `SHELL=/bin/sh`.
  - From this task on: full suite `env -u HERMES_HOME npm test`; one file `env -u HERMES_HOME node --test test/<file>.test.js` (unwatched; the full suite is the gate), or `env -u HERMES_HOME npm test -- test/<file>.test.js` for one file under the watcher and the stand-in shell. Summary filter: `2>&1 | grep -E '^# (tests|pass|fail|skipped)|^not ok|no-real-agents'`.
  - `test/helpers/no-real-agents.js`:
    - `AGENT_NAMES` = `["claude", "codex", "agent", "cursor-agent", "hermes", "openclaw"]`;
    - `REAL_AGENT_PATHS` = `[{ name, pattern }]`, where the real agents install themselves: `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/` and `.local/share/claude/versions/` (claude), `node_modules/@openai/codex/` (codex), `node_modules/openclaw/` (openclaw), `/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes` (hermes), `.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/` (cursor-agent);
    - `defaultAllowedRoots()` → `[os.tmpdir(), <repo>/test, <repo>/.superpowers/ui-audit/fake-bin]`;
    - `parsePsRows(text)` → `[{ pid, ppid, command }]`;
    - `readPsRows()` → `Promise<rows | null>` (one `ps -A -ww -o pid=,ppid=,command=`);
    - `isAllowedBinary(token, allowedRoots = defaultAllowedRoots())` → boolean (judges the real path, through symlinks; a bare name with no folder is never allowed);
    - `findViolations(rows, { baseline, rootPid, seenDescendants, allowedRoots, names })` → `[{ pid, ppid, name, binary, command, testFile }]`, where `baseline` is a `Map<pid, command>` (a `Set` of pids also works) and `seenDescendants` is a `Map<pid, { ppid, command }>` the function updates in place. A new descendant is flagged when its first or second word is named like an agent and lives outside `allowedRoots`, or, whatever `allowedRoots` says, when any word of its command (or the real path of its first or second word) matches a `REAL_AGENT_PATHS` pattern whose `name` is in `names`;
    - `startWatcher({ rootPid = process.pid, intervalMs = 200, onViolation, allowedRoots, names, kill = true })` → `Promise<{ stop(): Promise<{ checks, violations }> }>` (resolves after the baseline is taken; throws on Windows or when `ps` cannot run; `stop()` may be called more than once).
  - `test/helpers/fake-agents.js`:
    - `FAKE_AGENT_NAMES` (the same six names), `FAKE_AGENT_MODES` = `["tui", "setsid-grandchild", "ignore-term", "agents-hang", "updater"]`, `FAKE_AGENT_SCRIPT` (absolute path of `test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs`);
    - `makeFakeAgentBin(dir, { names = FAKE_AGENT_NAMES, mode = "tui" } = {})` → `Promise<{ dir, script, paths: { [name]: string } }>`. Each shim is `#!/bin/sh`, sets `FAKE_AGENT_NAME=<name>`, uses `FAKE_AGENT_MODE` from the environment when set and `mode` otherwise, and execs this Node on `tui-agent.mjs` (node need not be on PATH). A file or link already at a shim's path is removed first, never written through (the UI audit harness's `.superpowers/ui-audit/fake-bin/` holds links that all point at one `fake-agent` file; Task U1 replaces them with these shims). It throws on Windows (POSIX shims, like every fake CLI in this suite) and on an unknown mode.
    - `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL` (absolute path of `test/fakes/login-shell.sh`): the stand-in login shell and the only `SHELL` any test uses. Started as `<it> -i -l -c <command>` (shell-env.js's form, Task S2), it runs the last argument with `/bin/sh -c`, reads no startup file and keeps the environment exactly as given, `PATH` and the `FAKE_AGENT_*` variables included. POSIX only.
  - `test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs` behaviour (the full list is in its header comment):
    - one-shot answers (print and exit 0, no terminal needed): `--version` or `-v` → `<name> 9.9.9-fake`; `--help`, `-h` or any argv containing `--help` → `Usage: <name> [options]…`; `auth status` → `{"loggedIn":true}`; `login status`; `status …`; `doctor …`; `config get approvals.mode` → `manual` (Hermes's approvals read as on, as the UI audit harness's earlier `fake-agent` answered); any other `config get …` → an empty line; `gateway status` (with `--json` → `{"running":false}`); `gateway start|stop|restart` → logged as `{ event: "gateway", args }`; `claude agents …` → `FAKE_CLAUDE_AGENTS_JSON` or `[]` (mode `agents-hang`: never answers); `claude stop <id>` → `stopped <id>`, logged as `{ event: "stop", id }`;
    - a headless run (`-p`, `--print` or `exec` anywhere in argv, as the Runs page starts one; no session argv has these) prints nothing, is logged as `{ event: "run", args }`, keeps running until it is stopped (SIGTERM ends it at once) and ends by itself after 5 minutes, like the audit harness's earlier fake, whose probes stop live runs;
    - any other argv starts the terminal program: first the line `FAKE_ARGV <json>` with `{ name, mode, argv, cwd, isTTY, env, agentOsKeys, secretKeys }` (`env` holds only `TERM`, `COLORTERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION`, `AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB`, `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `SHELL`, `EDITOR`, `VISUAL`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `HERMES_HOME`, `FAKE_AGENT_MODE`, each only when set; `agentOsKeys` lists every `AGENT_OS_*` and `HERMES_AGENT_OS_*` name; `secretKeys` lists names matching `TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|_KEY$`; secret values are never printed), then the prompt `> `;
    - typed commands: `alt on|off`, `paste on|off`, `mouse on|off`, `focus on|off`, `keys app|normal`, `kitty on|off`, `bell`, `osc9 <text>`, `osc9st <text>`, `osc99 <text>`, `osc777 <text>`, `title <text>`, `ask` (DA1 `ESC[c` and DSR `ESC[6n`), `ask after <ms>` (the same two questions, sent <ms> milliseconds later, 10 to 60000; S9 closes the writer's window in between), `ask kitty` (`ESC[?u`), `ask color` (`ESC]11;?BEL`), `lines <n>`, `flood <KiB>`, `bottom <text>` (redraws only the last row, no new prompt), `ticker <ms> <count>` (redraws only the last row on a timer), `exit <code>`; anything else prints `you said: <text>`; replies and focus reports print `REPLY <json>`, a bracketed paste prints `PASTE <json>`, other escape sequences print `KEY <json>`; Ctrl+C exits 130;
    - modes: `setsid-grandchild` prints `GRANDCHILD:<pid>` and writes the pid to `FAKE_AGENT_PIDFILE` (the grandchild ignores SIGTERM when `FAKE_AGENT_GRANDCHILD_IGNORE_TERM=1`); `ignore-term` survives SIGTERM; `updater` asks `Update now? [y/N] `, prints `ANSWER <text>`, and exits 0 for y and 1 otherwise;
    - on SIGTERM it appends `{ event: "sigterm", snapshot }` to `FAKE_AGENT_LOG` and then dies from SIGTERM itself. `snapshot` is the text of the file named by `FAKE_AGENT_SNAPSHOT_ON_TERM`, in which a literal `{AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID}` is replaced by the fake's own `AGENT_OS_SESSION_ID` (Task S8's end-to-end quit test only learns the session id after the session starts; it reads the session's meta.json at the moment SIGTERM arrives to prove `endedBy: "quit"` was written before any kill). A file that cannot be read gives `snapshotError` (its error code, for example `"ENOENT"`) instead. Every log line also carries `name`, `pid` and `at` (milliseconds since 1970), so a test can put events in order; the log events are `start` (with the `FAKE_ARGV` record), `line`, `paste`, `reply`, `key`, `grandchild`, `agents`, `stop`, `gateway`, `run` and `sigterm`;
    - the terminal program leaves when its terminal closes: it never handles or ignores SIGHUP (Task S8's recovery test kills the server with SIGKILL and relies on this);
    - its output lines end in `\r\n`; a terminal adds its own carriage return, so tests match with `\r+\n` or a plain substring.

```js
// The no-real-agents watcher that `npm test` runs around the whole suite
// (spec SP3; planning decisions Q1, Q1a, Q1b). The pure functions are tested
// with made-up `ps` rows. The planted-process tests start a shell script
// named "claude" that only sleeps, from a temp folder the test declares "not
// a fake folder". No real agent is ever started.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { chmod, mkdir, mkdtemp, rm, symlink, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import {
  AGENT_NAMES,
  REAL_AGENT_PATHS,
  defaultAllowedRoots,
  findViolations,
  isAllowedBinary,
  parsePsRows,
  readPsRows,
  startWatcher
} from "./helpers/no-real-agents.js";

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";
const POSIX_ONLY = { skip: isWindows ? "the watcher is not available on Windows (no ps)" : false };
const delay = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

// Made-up rows: the runner is pid 100; "/fake-root-agent-os/bin" plays the
// fake folder; "/home/agent-os-test-user/..." plays a real install.
const RUNNER = 100;
const FAKE_ROOT = "/fake-root-agent-os/bin";
const REAL_HOME = "/home/agent-os-test-user";
const runnerRows = [
  { pid: RUNNER, ppid: 1, command: "node scripts/run-tests.mjs" },
  { pid: 101, ppid: RUNNER, command: "node --test --test-timeout=180000 /repo/test/a.test.js /repo/test/b.test.js" },
  { pid: 102, ppid: 101, command: "node --test-timeout=180000 /repo/test/b.test.js" }
];

function check(rows, options = {}) {
  return findViolations(rows, {
    baseline: new Map(),
    rootPid: RUNNER,
    seenDescendants: new Map(),
    allowedRoots: [FAKE_ROOT],
    ...options
  });
}

async function waitUntil(probe, label, ms = 5000) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + ms;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    const value = await probe();
    if (value) return value;
    await delay(25);
  }
  throw new Error(`timed out waiting for ${label}`);
}

// A stand-in "claude": a shell script that only sleeps. Started directly, ps
// shows it as "/bin/sh <dir>/claude ...", so its second word is named claude.
async function plantFakeClaude(dir) {
  const script = path.join(dir, "claude");
  await writeFile(script, "#!/bin/sh\n/bin/sleep 30\nexit 0\n");
  await chmod(script, 0o755);
  return script;
}

function killGroup(child) {
  if (!child?.pid) return;
  try {
    process.kill(-child.pid, "SIGKILL");
  } catch {
    // already gone
  }
}

test("a descendant is remembered after its parent exits, but a reused pid is not", POSIX_ONLY, () => {
  const seenDescendants = new Map();
  const first = [
    ...runnerRows,
    { pid: 300, ppid: 102, command: `/bin/sh ${FAKE_ROOT}/codex` },
    { pid: 301, ppid: 300, command: `${REAL_HOME}/.local/bin/codex resume --last` },
    { pid: 400, ppid: 102, command: "node -e setInterval" }
  ];
  assert.deepEqual(check(first, { seenDescendants }).map((v) => v.pid), [301]);

  // The parent is gone and 301 was handed to pid 1; pid 400 exited and the
  // system reused its number for the owner's own claude.
  const second = [
    ...runnerRows,
    { pid: 301, ppid: 1, command: `${REAL_HOME}/.local/bin/codex resume --last` },
    { pid: 400, ppid: 1, command: `${REAL_HOME}/.local/bin/claude --input-format stream-json` }
  ];
  const again = check(second, { seenDescendants });
  assert.deepEqual(again.map((v) => [v.pid, v.testFile]), [[301, "/repo/test/b.test.js"]]);
});

test("isAllowedBinary judges where the file really is, through symlinks", POSIX_ONLY, async () => {
  const dir = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-watch-paths-"));
  const fakes = path.join(dir, "fakes");

    await mkdir(fakes);
    await mkdir(elsewhere);
    await writeFile(path.join(elsewhere, "real-claude"), "#!/bin/sh\n");
    await writeFile(path.join(fakes, "fake-claude"), "#!/bin/sh\n");
    await symlink(path.join(elsewhere, "real-claude"), path.join(fakes, "claude"));
    await symlink(path.join(fakes, "fake-claude"), path.join(elsewhere, "claude"));

    assert.equal(isAllowedBinary(path.join(fakes, "claude"), [fakes]), false, "a link in a fake folder to a real file");
    assert.equal(isAllowedBinary(path.join(elsewhere, "claude"), [fakes]), true, "a link elsewhere to a fake file");
    assert.equal(isAllowedBinary(path.join(fakes, "gone", "claude"), [fakes]), true, "a path that no longer exists, as written");
    assert.equal(isAllowedBinary(path.join(elsewhere, "gone", "claude"), [fakes]), false);
    assert.equal(isAllowedBinary("claude", [fakes]), false, "a bare name can never be proved to be a fake");
    assert.equal(isAllowedBinary(path.join(fakes, "fake-claude"), [os.tmpdir()]), true, "the temp folder under either of its names");

  }
});

    assert.equal(notAllowed[0].name, "claude");

    assert.equal(allowed.some((v) => v.pid === planted.pid), false, "the temp folder is a fake folder by default");
```
