### Task S4: pty-host and mirror (headless xterm, serialize, modes, query answers, alerts, counted output)

This task builds the two engine pieces that sit right next to an agent's terminal program. `pty-host.js` runs the program in a real pseudo-terminal (PTY, the kind of "fake keyboard and screen" Terminal.app gives a program) through node-pty: argv only, never a shell, with exactly the environment and folder it is given, never the server's own environment (which holds `AGENT_OS_TOKEN`). It loads node-pty lazily, so a server without it still starts, and it registers each PTY's pid with `trackPid` so quit and Hold to stop all reach sessions. `mirror.js` keeps the server's own copy of each session's screen with xterm.js's headless terminal. That copy gives a window that attaches later the exact screen and the modes the serializer leaves out, answers the three standard terminal questions only while no window is the writer, forwards alerts (BEL, OSC 9/99/777) raw, and reports "counted output" for the 20 s activity rule. Nothing here knows about sessions, routes or sockets; S6 wires the pieces together.

Two facts about the real packages shape this task:
- `term.write()` in xterm.js is asynchronous, so a snapshot taken synchronously can miss output that the mirror has received but not yet read. That output would be lost for the window that attaches. `snapshot()` therefore returns a Promise that is built inside a write callback, so it covers exactly the output written before the call, never more and never less. The manager (S6) registers a new window as "waiting", takes the snapshot, then sends the snapshot and the output that arrived meanwhile, so nothing is lost or sent twice.
- `@xterm/addon-serialize` reads xterm.js internals (`terminal._core`), so the headless terminal and the serialize addon must come from the same xterm.js build. W0 pins the set built from the same commit as `@xterm/xterm@6.1.0-beta.304`: `@xterm/headless@6.1.0-beta.303`, `@xterm/addon-serialize@0.15.0-beta.301` and `@xterm/addon-unicode11@0.10.0-beta.301` (the browser terminal, U2, loads the same unicode11 build). All three are CommonJS bundles, so `mirror.js` loads them with a default import, never a named ESM import.

**Files:**
- Create: `server/runtime/sessions/pty-host.js`
- Create: `server/runtime/sessions/mirror.js`
- Test: `test/sessions-pty.test.js` (new; 12 tests in Step 2, 14 after Step 10)
- Test: `test/sessions-mirror.test.js` (new; 12 tests)
- No existing file changes. (`server/runtime/process-tree.js` is S1's; this task only imports from it.)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - S1, `server/runtime/process-tree.js`: `trackPid(pid, onExit?)`, where `onExit` is a subscribe function `(listener) => unsubscribe` that trackPid calls once so the pid untracks itself when the process ends; `untrackPid(pid)`; and `killAllTracked({ graceMs })`, which stops every tracked child and every tracked pid with its whole tree. pty-host passes the PTY handle's own `onExit` as that subscribe function, and still calls `untrackPid(pid)` itself on exit (harmless twice).
  - W0, in `dependencies` at exact versions: `node-pty@1.2.0-beta.14`, `@xterm/headless@6.1.0-beta.303`, `@xterm/addon-serialize@0.15.0-beta.301`, `@xterm/addon-unicode11@0.10.0-beta.301`.
  - W1, `test/helpers/fake-agents.js`:
    - `makeFakeAgentBin(dir, { names = all six agent names, mode = "tui" })` writes an executable shim `<dir>/<name>` for each name. In mode `tui` (no `FAKE_AGENT_MODE` in the environment) the fake prints one line `FAKE_ARGV <json>` whose `argv` holds its arguments as JSON strings, then the prompt `> `; it echoes typed text (`you said: <text>`), and `exit <n>` typed at the prompt makes it exit with code n (planning decision Q2).

Each `IEvent` returns an `IDisposable`.

Provide a callback to know when the data was processed"), `onData`, `onBell`, `onWriteParsed`, `parser.registerCsiHandler(id, cb)` / `registerEscHandler` / `registerOscHandler(ident, cb)` ("Return true if the sequence was handled; false if we should try a previous handler ... The most recently added handler is tried first"), `modes: IModes` (`bracketedPasteMode`, `mouseTrackingMode: 'none'|'x10'|'vt200'|'drag'|'any'`, `sendFocusMode`, `applicationCursorKeysMode`; no mouse encoding and no kitty flags), `buffer.active` (`type`, `baseY`, `getLine(y).translateToString(true)`), `unicode.activeVersion` ("(EXPERIMENTAL)", needs `allowProposedApi: true`), `vtExtensions.kittyKeyboard`.
  - @xterm/addon-serialize typings: `new SerializeAddon()`, `serialize(options?)` (includes the alternate screen and the modes in `IModes`, but not mouse encoding or kitty flags).
- Produces (`server/runtime/sessions/pty-host.js`):
  - `export const PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON = "Agent OS could not load its terminal module on this computer."`
  - `export function ptyAvailable()` → `Promise<{ ok: true, reason: null } | { ok: false, reason: string }>`. It loads node-pty once and runs `node -e "process.exit(0)"` in a PTY once (a probe). A missing module is final; a failed probe is retried after 30 s.
  - `export async function spawnPty({ command, args = [], cwd, env, cols = 120, rows = 32, tracker })` → `PtyHandle`:
    `{ pid, write(data), resize(cols, rows), kill(signal = "SIGTERM"), pause(), resume(), onData(cb) → unsubscribe, onExit(cb) → unsubscribe }`.
    - `command` and `cwd` must be absolute, `args` a string array, and `env` an explicit object (never `process.env` by default): otherwise `TypeError`.
    - Errors: plain `Error`s with `code: "pty_unavailable"` (message `PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON`) or `code: "spawn_failed"`. The manager (S6) checks `ptyAvailable()` before it spawns and answers 503 `pty_unavailable` itself, and turns any spawn error into its own 500 `start_failed`.
    - `onExit` delivers `{ exitCode: number | null, signal: string | null }`: the signal as a NAME (`"SIGTERM"`, `"SIGKILL"`), and `exitCode: null` when a signal ended it. A listener added after the end is still called once.
    - Output that arrives before the first `onData` listener is kept (up to 1 MB) and handed to that first listener.
    - `trackPid(pid, handle.onExit)` right after the spawn; `untrackPid(pid)` on exit.
    - `tracker` (`{ trackPid, untrackPid }`) is for tests only; it defaults to process-tree's.
  - `export function setPtyLoaderForTests(fn | null)`: tests only.
- Produces (`server/runtime/sessions/mirror.js`):
  - `export function createMirror({ cols, rows, onQueryReply, onAlert, now = Date.now })` → `Mirror`:
    - `write(chunk: string)`;
    - `resize(cols, rows)` (cols 2-500, rows 1-200; anything else ignored);
    - `snapshot()` → **`Promise<{ data, cols, rows, modes }>`**, where `modes = { altScreen: boolean, bracketedPaste: boolean, mouseTracking: "none"|"x10"|"vt200"|"drag"|"any", mouseEncoding: "default"|"sgr"|"sgr-pixels", focusReporting: boolean, cursorKeysApp: boolean, kittyFlags: number }`. It covers exactly the chunks written before the call;
    - `setWriterAttached(boolean)`: while false, DA1 (`ESC[?1;2c`), cursor position (`ESC[<row>;<col>R`, and the `ESC[?…R` form) and kitty (`ESC[?<flags>u`) replies go to `onQueryReply(reply)`. Every other reply xterm.js would make is dropped, and nothing is sent while a writer is attached;
    - `onCountedOutput(cb)` → unsubscribe: fires at most every 250 ms when the text above the bottom 6 rows changed or the screen scrolled since the last check;
    - `dispose()`.
    - `onAlert(raw)`: `"bel"`, or `"<osc number>;<payload>"`, for example `"9;Approval requested"` or `"777;notify;Codex;Waiting"`, capped at 4096 characters.
  - `export function isUserInput(data)` → `false` for a frame made only of terminal replies (DA1/DA2/DA3, cursor position, status, kitty flags, mode reports, XTVERSION, DECRQSS, OSC colour replies), focus reports (`ESC[I`, `ESC[O`) or mouse-motion reports (SGR and default encoding). Otherwise `true`: keys, paste, clicks, the wheel. An empty frame is `false`.
  - `export const COUNTED_BOTTOM_ROWS = 6, COUNTED_CHECK_MS = 250, MIRROR_SCROLLBACK = 1000, ALERT_RAW_LIMIT = 4096`.

```js
async function waitFor(predicate, { timeoutMs = 10000, intervalMs = 20, what = "the condition" } = {}) {

  while (Date.now() < deadline) {

    if (value) return value;
    await sleep(intervalMs);
  }
  throw new Error(`timed out waiting for ${what}`);
}

function collect(handle) {
  const out = { text: "" };
  handle.onData((chunk) => {
    out.text += chunk;
  });
  return out;
}

// Resolves with the exit info, or null when the program has not ended in time.
function exitOf(handle, timeoutMs = 10000) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(null), timeoutMs);
    timer.unref?.();
    handle.onExit((info) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve(info);
    });
  });
}

function isAlive(pid) {
  try {
    process.kill(pid, 0);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

test("kill reports the signal by name, and a listener added after the end still hears about it", SKIP_POSIX, async () => {
  await withTempDir(async (dir) => {

    const second = await spawnPty({ command: process.execPath, args: [script], cwd: dir, env: ptyEnv(dir) });
    try {

      first.kill(); // SIGTERM by default
      assert.deepEqual(await firstExit, { exitCode: null, signal: "SIGTERM" });

      const secondExit = exitOf(second);
      second.kill("SIGKILL");
      assert.deepEqual(await secondExit, { exitCode: null, signal: "SIGKILL" });
      assert.deepEqual(await exitOf(second), { exitCode: null, signal: "SIGKILL" }, "a listener added after the end");

      // Everything is a quiet no-op after the end.
      second.write("ignored");
      second.resize(80, 24);
      second.pause();
      second.resume();
      second.kill("SIGKILL");
    } finally {
      first.kill("SIGKILL");
      second.kill("SIGKILL");
    }
  });
});

test("pause stops the program's output until resume", SKIP_POSIX, async () => {

        chunks += 1;
      });
      await waitFor(() => chunks > 0, { what: "the first tick" });
      handle.pause();
      await sleep(200); // let anything already on its way arrive
      const frozen = chunks;
      await sleep(400);
      assert.equal(chunks, frozen, "no output arrives while paused");
      handle.resume();
      await waitFor(() => chunks > frozen, { what: "output after resume" });
    } finally {
      handle.kill("SIGKILL");
    }
  });
});

test("the pid is tracked at the start (with an onExit subscription) and untracked at the end", SKIP_POSIX, async () => {
  await withTempDir(async (dir) => {
    const script = await writeScript(dir, "sleeper.mjs", SLEEPER);
    const calls = [];
    let trackedOnExit = null;
    const tracker = {
      trackPid: (pid, onExit) => {
        trackedOnExit = onExit;
        calls.push(["track", pid]);
      },
      untrackPid: (pid) => calls.push(["untrack", pid])
    };
    const handle = await spawnPty({ command: process.execPath, args: [script], cwd: dir, env: ptyEnv(dir), tracker });
    try {
      assert.deepEqual(calls, [["track", handle.pid]]);
      assert.equal(typeof trackedOnExit, "function");
      const heard = [];
      trackedOnExit((info) => heard.push(info));
      const exit = exitOf(handle);
      handle.kill("SIGKILL");
      assert.deepEqual(await exit, { exitCode: null, signal: "SIGKILL" });
      assert.deepEqual(calls, [["track", handle.pid], ["untrack", handle.pid]]);
      assert.deepEqual(heard, [{ exitCode: null, signal: "SIGKILL" }]);
    } finally {
      handle.kill("SIGKILL");
    }
  });
});

test("killAllTracked (quit and Hold to stop all) reaches a PTY program too", SKIP_POSIX, async () => {
  await withTempDir(async (dir) => {
    const script = await writeScript(dir, "sleeper.mjs", SLEEPER);
    const handle = await spawnPty({ command: process.execPath, args: [script], cwd: dir, env: ptyEnv(dir) });
    try {
      const exit = exitOf(handle);
      await killAllTracked({ graceMs: 500 });
      const info = await exit;
      assert.ok(info, "the program ended");
      assert.ok(["SIGTERM", "SIGKILL"].includes(info.signal), `ended by ${info.signal}`);
      assert.equal(isAlive(handle.pid), false);
    } finally {
      handle.kill("SIGKILL");
    }
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the PTY host.** Create `server/runtime/sessions/pty-host.js` with exactly this content:

```js
// Runs an agent's own terminal program inside a real pseudo-terminal (PTY)
// with node-pty, the way Terminal.app does: argv only (never a shell), the
// environment it is given (never the server's own, which holds
// AGENT_OS_TOKEN) and the folder it is given.
//
// node-pty is a native module, so it is loaded only when a session needs it.
// A server without it (the portable test, Docker) still starts and simply
// reports that sessions can't start.
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { trackPid, untrackPid } from "../process-tree.js";

export const PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON = "Agent OS could not load its terminal module on this computer.";

const DEFAULT_TRACKER = Object.freeze({ trackPid, untrackPid });
const EARLY_OUTPUT_LIMIT = 1024 * 1024; // characters kept until the first listener
const PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000;
const PROBE_RETRY_MS = 30000;
const realLoader = () => import("node-pty");

let loader = realLoader;
let loading = null;
let availability = null;
let probeFailedAt = 0;

function loadNodePty() {
  if (!loading) {
    loading = Promise.resolve()
      .then(() => loader())
      .then((mod) => {
        // node-pty is CommonJS: spawn sits on the namespace or on `default`.
        const pty = typeof mod?.spawn === "function" ? mod : mod?.default;
        if (typeof pty?.spawn !== "function") throw new Error("node-pty has no spawn()");
        return { ok: true, pty };
      })
      .catch((error) => ({ ok: false, error }));
  }
  return loading;
}

// Tests only: replace how node-pty is loaded. null puts the real import back.
export function setPtyLoaderForTests(fn) {
  loader = typeof fn === "function" ? fn : realLoader;
  loading = null;
  availability = null;
  probeFailedAt = 0;
}

// The probe gets only what a program needs to start, never the server's
// secrets.
function probeEnv() {
  const env = {};
  for (const key of ["PATH", "SystemRoot", "SYSTEMROOT", "TEMP", "TMP"]) {
    const value = process.env[key];
    if (typeof value === "string" && value) env[key] = value;
  }
  return env;
}

// Runs `node -e "process.exit(0)"` in a PTY, which proves the whole chain
// works (on macOS that includes node-pty's spawn-helper being executable).
function probe(pty) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    let child;
    try {
      child = pty.spawn(process.execPath, ["-e", "process.exit(0)"], {
        name: "xterm-256color",
        cols: 80,
        rows: 24,
        cwd: os.tmpdir(),
        env: probeEnv(),
        encoding: "utf8"
      });
    } catch (error) {
      reject(error);
      return;
    }
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      try {
        child.kill();
      } catch {
        // already gone
      }
      reject(new Error("the terminal module did not answer in time"));
    }, PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS);
    child.onData(() => {}); // keep the output flowing so the exit is reported
    child.onExit(({ exitCode }) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve(exitCode);
    });
  });
}

async function checkAvailability() {
  const loaded = await loadNodePty();
  if (!loaded.ok) return { ok: false, reason: PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON };
  try {
    if ((await probe(loaded.pty)) === 0) return { ok: true, reason: null };
  } catch {
    // reported below
  }
  probeFailedAt = Date.now();
  return { ok: false, reason: PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON };
}

// { ok: true, reason: null } or { ok: false, reason }. A module that does not
// load stays unavailable; a failed probe is tried again after 30 s, because
// it may have been a passing problem (for example too many processes).
export function ptyAvailable() {
  if (availability && probeFailedAt && Date.now() - probeFailedAt > PROBE_RETRY_MS) {
    availability = null;
    probeFailedAt = 0;
  }
  if (!availability) availability = checkAvailability();
  return availability;
}

function ptyUnavailableError() {
  const error = new Error(PTY_UNAVAILABLE_REASON);
  error.code = "pty_unavailable";
  return error;
}

function toSize(value, fallback, max) {
  const number = Number(value);
  return Number.isInteger(number) && number >= 1 && number <= max ? number : fallback;
}

function stringEnv(env) {
  const clean = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(env)) {
    if (typeof value === "string") clean[key] = value;
  }
  return clean;
}

// node-pty reports the signal as a number (0 when there was none).
function signalName(signal) {
  if (typeof signal === "string" && signal) return signal;
  if (!Number.isInteger(signal) || signal <= 0) return null;
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(os.constants.signals)) {
    if (value === signal) return name;
  }
  return String(signal);
}

function safeCall(listener, value) {
  try {
    listener(value);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Agent OS: a terminal listener failed:", error);
  }
}

export async function spawnPty({ command, args = [], cwd, env, cols = 120, rows = 32, tracker = DEFAULT_TRACKER } = {}) {
  if (typeof command !== "string" || !path.isAbsolute(command)) {
    throw new TypeError("spawnPty needs the full path of the program to run.");
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(args) || args.some((arg) => typeof arg !== "string")) {
    throw new TypeError("spawnPty needs its arguments as a list of strings.");
  }
  if (typeof cwd !== "string" || !path.isAbsolute(cwd)) {
    throw new TypeError("spawnPty needs the full path of the folder to start in.");
  }
  if (!env || typeof env !== "object" || Array.isArray(env)) {
    // Without an env, node-pty would pass on process.env, which holds AGENT_OS_TOKEN.
    throw new TypeError("spawnPty needs an explicit environment; it never passes on the server's own.");
  }
  const loaded = await loadNodePty();
  if (!loaded.ok) throw ptyUnavailableError();

  const childEnv = stringEnv(env);
  let child;
  try {
    child = loaded.pty.spawn(command, [...args], {
      name: childEnv.TERM || "xterm-256color",
      cols: toSize(cols, 120, 500),
      rows: toSize(rows, 32, 200),
      cwd,
      env: childEnv,
      encoding: "utf8"
    });
  } catch (error) {
    const failure = new Error(`Could not start ${path.basename(command)}: ${error?.message || error}`);
    failure.code = "spawn_failed";
    throw failure;
  }

  const pid = child.pid;
  const dataListeners = new Set();
  const exitListeners = new Set();
  let early = [];
  let earlyChars = 0;
  let exitInfo = null;

  child.onData((chunk) => {
    if (dataListeners.size > 0) {
      for (const listener of [...dataListeners]) safeCall(listener, chunk);
      return;
    }
    if (early && earlyChars + chunk.length <= EARLY_OUTPUT_LIMIT) {
      early.push(chunk);
      earlyChars += chunk.length;
    }
  });

  // The first listener also receives what arrived before it (in order, just
  // after this call returns). Later listeners get only new output.
  function onData(listener) {
    if (typeof listener !== "function") return () => {};
    dataListeners.add(listener);
    if (early) {
      const kept = early;
      early = null;
      if (kept.length) {
        queueMicrotask(() => {
          for (const chunk of kept) safeCall(listener, chunk);
        });
      }
    }
    return () => {
      dataListeners.delete(listener);
    };
  }

  // A listener added after the end is still told, once.
  function onExit(listener) {
    if (typeof listener !== "function") return () => {};
    if (exitInfo) {
      const info = exitInfo;
      queueMicrotask(() => safeCall(listener, info));
      return () => {};
    }
    exitListeners.add(listener);
    return () => {
      exitListeners.delete(listener);
    };
  }

  child.onExit(({ exitCode, signal }) => {
    const name = signalName(signal);
    exitInfo = Object.freeze({
      exitCode: name ? null : Number.isInteger(exitCode) ? exitCode : null,
      signal: name
    });
    try {
      tracker.untrackPid(pid);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error("Agent OS: could not untrack a terminal program:", error);
    }
    const listeners = [...exitListeners];
    exitListeners.clear();
    for (const listener of listeners) safeCall(listener, exitInfo);
  });

  const handle = Object.freeze({
    pid,
    write(data) {
      if (exitInfo || typeof data !== "string" || data.length === 0) return;
      try {
        child.write(data);
      } catch {
        // the program is ending
      }
    },
    resize(nextCols, nextRows) {
      const width = toSize(nextCols, 0, 500);
      const height = toSize(nextRows, 0, 200);
      if (exitInfo || !width || !height) return;
      try {
        child.resize(width, height);
      } catch {
        // the program is ending
      }
    },
    kill(signal = "SIGTERM") {
      if (exitInfo) return;
      try {
        // node-pty throws when a signal is named on Windows.
        if (process.platform === "win32") child.kill();
        else child.kill(signal);
      } catch {
        // already gone
      }
    },
    pause() {
      if (exitInfo) return;
      try {
        child.pause();
      } catch {
        // the program is ending
      }
    },
    resume() {
      if (exitInfo) return;
      try {
        child.resume();
      } catch {
        // the program is ending
      }
    },
    onData,
    onExit
  });

  try {
    // Quit and Hold to stop all (killAllTracked) reach this program from now on.
    tracker.trackPid(pid, onExit);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Agent OS: could not track a terminal program:", error);
  }
  return handle;
}
```

```js
// The session mirror: the server's headless copy of a session's screen.
// Snapshot and modes for reattach, the three standard terminal questions
// answered only while no writer is attached, raw alerts, counted output for
// the 20 s activity rule, and what counts as user input. No process runs here:
// the tests write terminal output straight into the mirror.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import xtermHeadless from "@xterm/headless";
import { ALERT_RAW_LIMIT, COUNTED_CHECK_MS, createMirror, isUserInput } from "../server/runtime/sessions/mirror.js";

// @xterm/headless is a CommonJS bundle: its classes sit on the default export.
const { Terminal } = xtermHeadless;
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

const DEFAULT_MODES = {
  altScreen: false,
  bracketedPaste: false,
  mouseTracking: "none",
  mouseEncoding: "default",
  focusReporting: false,
  cursorKeysApp: false,
  kittyFlags: 0
};

// Waits until everything written so far is on the mirror's screen and a
// counted-output check has had time to run.
async function settle(mirror) {
  await mirror.snapshot();
  await sleep(COUNTED_CHECK_MS * 2 + 100);
}

// Writes a snapshot into a fresh terminal of the same size, the way a browser
// terminal restores one, and reads the screen back.
async function replay(snapshot) {
  const term = new Terminal({ cols: snapshot.cols, rows: snapshot.rows, logLevel: "off" });
  await new Promise((resolve) => term.write(snapshot.data, resolve));
  const buffer = term.buffer.active;
  const lines = [];
  for (let y = 0; y < term.rows; y += 1) lines.push(buffer.getLine(buffer.baseY + y)?.translateToString(true) ?? "");
  const result = { lines, cursor: [buffer.cursorX, buffer.cursorY], screen: buffer.type };
  term.dispose();
  return result;
}

test("a snapshot restores the screen, the cursor and the alternate screen in a fresh terminal", async () => {
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 10 });
  try {
    mirror.write("\x1b[1mbold\x1b[0m plain\r\nsecond line\r\n\x1b[32mgreen\x1b[0m");
    const normal = await mirror.snapshot();
    assert.equal(normal.cols, 40);
    assert.equal(normal.rows, 10);
    const restored = await replay(normal);
    assert.deepEqual(restored.lines.slice(0, 3), ["bold plain", "second line", "green"]);
    assert.deepEqual(restored.cursor, [5, 2]);
    assert.equal(restored.screen, "normal");

    mirror.write("\x1b[?1049h\x1b[Hin the alt screen");
    const alt = await mirror.snapshot();
    assert.equal(alt.modes.altScreen, true);
    const restoredAlt = await replay(alt);
    assert.equal(restoredAlt.screen, "alternate");
    assert.equal(restoredAlt.lines[0], "in the alt screen");
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

test("a snapshot covers exactly the output written before it was asked for, never later output", async () => {
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 10 });
  try {
    mirror.write("first");
    const pending = mirror.snapshot();
    mirror.write("\r\nsecond"); // written after the request: goes to the window as live output instead
    const early = await replay(await pending);
    assert.deepEqual(early.lines.slice(0, 2), ["first", ""]);
    const later = await replay(await mirror.snapshot());
    assert.deepEqual(later.lines.slice(0, 2), ["first", "second"]);
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

test("modes: bracketed paste, mouse tracking and encoding, focus reports, cursor keys and the alternate screen are tracked and cleared", async () => {
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 10 });
  try {
    assert.deepEqual((await mirror.snapshot()).modes, DEFAULT_MODES);

    mirror.write("\x1b[?2004h\x1b[?1002h\x1b[?1006h\x1b[?1004h\x1b[?1h\x1b[?1049h");
    const on = await mirror.snapshot();
    assert.deepEqual(on.modes, {
      altScreen: true,
      bracketedPaste: true,
      mouseTracking: "drag",
      mouseEncoding: "sgr",
      focusReporting: true,
      cursorKeysApp: true,
      kittyFlags: 0
    });
    assert.ok(on.data.includes("\x1b[?2004h"), "the serialized screen carries bracketed paste itself");

    mirror.write("\x1b[?1016h");
    assert.equal((await mirror.snapshot()).modes.mouseEncoding, "sgr-pixels");
    mirror.write("\x1b[?1006l"); // xterm.js turns off either encoding with either reset
    assert.equal((await mirror.snapshot()).modes.mouseEncoding, "default");

    mirror.write("\x1b[?1006h\x1b[?2004l\x1b[?1002l\x1b[?1006l\x1b[?1004l\x1b[?1l\x1b[?1049l");
    assert.deepEqual((await mirror.snapshot()).modes, DEFAULT_MODES);
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

test("a full reset (RIS) clears every tracked mode", async () => {
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 10 });
  try {
    mirror.write("\x1b[?1006h\x1b[?2004h\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1049h\x1b[>5u");
    const before = await mirror.snapshot();
    assert.equal(before.modes.kittyFlags, 5);
    assert.equal(before.modes.mouseEncoding, "sgr");
    mirror.write("\x1bc");
    assert.deepEqual((await mirror.snapshot()).modes, DEFAULT_MODES);
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

test("kitty keyboard flags follow push, pop and set, per screen, exactly as xterm.js itself answers them", async () => {
  const replies = [];
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 10, onQueryReply: (reply) => replies.push(reply) });
  // Asks xterm.js for its flags (CSI ? u) and compares with what the mirror tracked.
  async function kittyNow() {
    replies.length = 0;
    mirror.write("\x1b[?u");
    const { modes } = await mirror.snapshot();
    return { tracked: modes.kittyFlags, xterm: replies.at(-1) };
  }
  const steps = [
    ["\x1b[>1u", 1, "push 1"],
    ["\x1b[>3u", 3, "push 3"],
    ["\x1b[<u", 1, "pop one"],
    ["\x1b[=4;2u", 5, "set bits"],
    ["\x1b[=1;3u", 4, "clear bits"],
    ["\x1b[=2u", 2, "replace"],
    ["\x1b[?1049h", 0, "the alternate screen has its own flags"],
    ["\x1b[>8u", 8, "push on the alternate screen"],
    ["\x1b[?1049l", 2, "back to the main screen's flags"],
    ["\x1b[?1049h", 8, "the alternate screen's flags were kept"],
    ["\x1b[?1049l\x1b[<5u", 0, "popping past the bottom leaves 0"]
  ];
  try {
    for (const [sequence, expected, why] of steps) {
      mirror.write(sequence);
      assert.deepEqual(await kittyNow(), { tracked: expected, xterm: `\x1b[?${expected}u` }, why);
    }
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

test("the mirror answers DA1, cursor position and kitty flags only while no writer is attached, and nothing else", async () => {
  const replies = [];
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 10, onQueryReply: (reply) => replies.push(reply) });
  try {
    // DA1, cursor position, DA2 (dropped), status (dropped), a kitty push, a kitty query.
    mirror.write("abc\x1b[c\x1b[6n\x1b[>c\x1b[5n\x1b[>3u\x1b[?u");
    await mirror.snapshot();
    assert.deepEqual(replies, ["\x1b[?1;2c", "\x1b[1;4R", "\x1b[?3u"]);

    mirror.setWriterAttached(true); // the writer's own browser terminal answers now
    mirror.write("\x1b[c\x1b[6n\x1b[?u");
    await mirror.snapshot();
    assert.equal(replies.length, 3, "no answer while a writer is attached");

    mirror.setWriterAttached(false);
    mirror.write("\x1b[c");
    await mirror.snapshot();
    assert.deepEqual(replies.slice(3), ["\x1b[?1;2c"]);
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

test("alerts: BEL and OSC 9, 99 and 777 are forwarded raw; a title or a BEL that ends an OSC is not an alert", async () => {
  const alerts = [];
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 10, onAlert: (raw) => alerts.push(raw) });
  try {
    mirror.write("ding\x07");
    mirror.write("\x1b]9;Approval requested\x07");
    mirror.write("\x1b]9;Turn done\x1b\\");
    mirror.write("\x1b]777;notify;Codex;Waiting for you\x07");
    mirror.write("\x1b]99;i=1:d=0;Hello\x1b\\");
    mirror.write("\x1b]0;just a title\x07");
    mirror.write("\x1b]9;spl");
    mirror.write("it across writes\x07");
    mirror.write(`\x1b]9;${"x".repeat(10000)}\x07`);
    await mirror.snapshot();
    assert.deepEqual(alerts.slice(0, 6), [
      "bel",
      "9;Approval requested",
      "9;Turn done",
      "777;notify;Codex;Waiting for you",
      "99;i=1:d=0;Hello",
      "9;split across writes"
    ]);
    assert.equal(alerts.length, 7);
    assert.equal(alerts[6].length, ALERT_RAW_LIMIT, "a huge payload is cut to the limit");
    assert.ok(alerts[6].startsWith("9;xxx"));
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

test("counted output: new text above the bottom 6 rows and scrolling count; the bottom rows, colours, cursor, titles, modes and identical redraws do not", async () => {
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 12 }); // rows 7 to 12 are the bottom 6
  let counted = 0;
  let stopped = 0;
  mirror.onCountedOutput(() => {
    counted += 1;
  });
  const off = mirror.onCountedOutput(() => {
    stopped += 1;
  });
  off();
  try {
    mirror.write("\x1b[2;1Hworking on step 1");
    await settle(mirror);
    assert.equal(counted, 1, "new text above the bottom 6 rows");

    mirror.write("\x1b[7;1Hstatus: 12%\x1b[12;1H> ");
    await settle(mirror);
    assert.equal(counted, 1, "a status line and an input box in the bottom 6 rows");

    mirror.write("\x1b[2;1Hworking on step 1");
    mirror.write("\x1b[2;1H\x1b[31mworking on step 1\x1b[0m");
    mirror.write("\x1b[4;9H\x1b]0;a new title\x07\x1b[?2004h\x1b[?25l");
    await settle(mirror);
    assert.equal(counted, 1, "identical redraws, a colour, the cursor, a title and modes");

    mirror.write("\x1b[12;1H\r\n\r\n");
    await settle(mirror);
    assert.equal(counted, 2, "scrolling the screen");
    assert.equal(stopped, 0, "an unsubscribed listener hears nothing");
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

test("counted output is checked at most every 250 ms", async () => {
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 12 });
  let counted = 0;
  mirror.onCountedOutput(() => {
    counted += 1;
  });
  try {
    const started = Date.now();
    for (let step = 0; Date.now() - started < 1000; step += 1) {
      mirror.write(`\x1b[2;1Hstep ${step}   `);
      await sleep(10);
    }
    await settle(mirror);
    assert.ok(counted >= 2, `expected counted output, got ${counted}`);
    assert.ok(counted <= 6, `expected at most one count per 250 ms over about 1.3 s, got ${counted}`);
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

test("resize changes the mirror's size, ignores impossible sizes, and its reflow is not counted as output", async () => {
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 12 });
  let counted = 0;
  mirror.onCountedOutput(() => {
    counted += 1;
  });
  try {
    mirror.write("\x1b[2;1Ha line that is long enough to wrap when narrow");
    await settle(mirror);
    assert.equal(counted, 1);
    mirror.resize(20, 12);
    mirror.write("\x1b[12;1Hstatus");
    await settle(mirror);
    assert.equal(counted, 1, "the text moved by the resize is not output");
    mirror.resize(0, 12);
    mirror.resize(600, 12);
    mirror.resize(30.5, 12);
    mirror.resize(30, 0);
    const snap = await mirror.snapshot();
    assert.deepEqual([snap.cols, snap.rows], [20, 12]);
  } finally {
    mirror.dispose();
  }
});

test("dispose answers a snapshot still waiting, and later calls do nothing", async () => {
  const mirror = createMirror({ cols: 40, rows: 10 });
  mirror.write("bye");
  const pending = mirror.snapshot();
  mirror.dispose();
  const snap = await pending;
  assert.equal(typeof snap.data, "string");
  assert.deepEqual([snap.cols, snap.rows], [40, 10]);
  mirror.write("ignored");
  mirror.resize(80, 24);
  mirror.setWriterAttached(true);
  mirror.dispose();
  assert.equal((await mirror.snapshot()).data, "");
});

test("isUserInput: replies, focus reports and mouse motion are not user input; keys, paste, clicks and the wheel are", () => {
  const motion = (button) => "\x1b[M" + String.fromCharCode(32 + button, 32 + 10, 32 + 5);
  const notInput = [
    "",
    "\x1b[?1;2c", // DA1 reply
    "\x1b[>0;276;0c", // DA2 reply
    "\x1b[12;40R", // cursor position
    "\x1b[?12;40R", // cursor position, private form
    "\x1b[0n", // status report
    "\x1b[?997;1n", // colour scheme report
    "\x1b[?5u", // kitty keyboard flags
    "\x1b[?2004;1$y", // mode report
    "\x1b]11;rgb:1e1e/1e1e/1e1e\x1b\\", // background colour reply
    "\x1b]10;rgb:ffff/ffff/ffff\x07", // foreground colour reply
    "\x1b]4;1;rgb:cdcd/0000/0000\x07", // palette colour reply
    "\x1bP>|xterm.js(6.1.0)\x1b\\", // terminal name and version
    "\x1b[I", // focus in
    "\x1b[O", // focus out
    "\x1b[<35;10;5M", // mouse moved, no button
    "\x1b[<32;10;5M", // mouse moved with the left button held
    motion(35), // mouse moved, default encoding
    "\x1b[O\x1b[?1;2c\x1b[<35;1;1M\x1b[3;7R" // several in one frame
  ];
  const input = [
    "a",
    "hello\r",
    "\r",
    "\x03", // Ctrl+C
    "\x1b", // Escape
    "\x1b[A", // arrow up
    "\x1b[3~", // Delete
    "\x1b[13;2u", // Shift+Enter with the kitty keyboard
    "\x1b[97u", // "a" with the kitty keyboard
    "\x1b[200~pasted text\x1b[201~",
    "\x1b[<0;10;5M", // click
    "\x1b[<0;10;5m", // release
    "\x1b[<64;10;5M", // wheel up
    "\x1b[<65;10;5M", // wheel down
    motion(0), // click, default encoding
    "\x1b[Ix", // a focus report, then a key
    "\x1b[?1;2cq" // a reply, then a key
  ];
  for (const frame of notInput) assert.equal(isUserInput(frame), false, JSON.stringify(frame));
  for (const frame of input) assert.equal(isUserInput(frame), true, JSON.stringify(frame));
  assert.equal(isUserInput(undefined), false);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Write the mirror.** Create `server/runtime/sessions/mirror.js` with exactly this content:

```js
// The server's own copy of a session's screen (the "mirror"), kept with
// xterm.js's headless terminal at the same size as the PTY. It:
// - gives a window that attaches later the screen exactly as it is now
//   (snapshot: the serialized screen plus the modes the serializer leaves out);
// - answers the three standard terminal questions (DA1, cursor position,
//   kitty keyboard flags) while no window is the writer, so an agent never
//   waits forever for a reply after the window closes;
// - reports alerts raw (SP3): BEL, and OSC 9, 99 and 777 notifications;
// - tells the session manager when real work shows on screen ("counted
//   output"): text that changes above the bottom 6 rows, or a scroll, checked
//   at most every 250 ms. Status lines, input boxes and key hints live in the
//   bottom rows, so their redraws do not keep a session "live".
import xtermHeadless from "@xterm/headless";
import serializeAddon from "@xterm/addon-serialize";
import unicode11Addon from "@xterm/addon-unicode11";

// These packages are CommonJS bundles: their classes sit on the default export.
const { Terminal } = xtermHeadless;
const { SerializeAddon } = serializeAddon;
const { Unicode11Addon } = unicode11Addon;

export const COUNTED_BOTTOM_ROWS = 6;
export const COUNTED_CHECK_MS = 250;
export const MIRROR_SCROLLBACK = 1000;
export const ALERT_RAW_LIMIT = 4096;

const ALERT_OSC_IDS = [9, 99, 777];
const ALT_SCREEN_MODES = new Set([47, 1047, 1049]);
const KITTY_STACK_LIMIT = 16; // the same limit xterm.js uses
// Replies the mirror may send on the agent's behalf: DA1, the cursor position
// (plain and private form) and the kitty keyboard flags. xterm.js would also
// answer DA2, mode requests and more; those are dropped.
const STANDARD_REPLY = /^(?:\x1b\[\?[\d;]*c|\x1b\[\??\d+;\d+R|\x1b\[\?\d+u)$/;
const DEFAULT_MODES = Object.freeze({
  altScreen: false,
  bracketedPaste: false,
  mouseTracking: "none",
  mouseEncoding: "default",
  focusReporting: false,
  cursorKeysApp: false,
  kittyFlags: 0
});

function clampSize(value, fallback, min, max) {
  const number = Number(value);
  return Number.isInteger(number) && number >= min && number <= max ? number : fallback;
}

// One numeric parameter of a CSI sequence (sub-parameters arrive as arrays).
function param(params, index, fallback) {
  const value = params[index];
  const number = Array.isArray(value) ? value[0] : value;
  return Number.isInteger(number) ? number : fallback;
}

function freshKitty() {
  return { flags: 0, mainFlags: 0, altFlags: 0, mainStack: [], altStack: [] };
}

function safeCall(listener, value) {
  try {
    listener(value);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Agent OS: a screen listener failed:", error);
  }
}

export function createMirror({ cols, rows, onQueryReply, onAlert, now = Date.now } = {}) {
  const reply = typeof onQueryReply === "function" ? onQueryReply : () => {};
  const alert = typeof onAlert === "function" ? onAlert : () => {};
  const term = new Terminal({
    cols: clampSize(cols, 120, 2, 500),
    rows: clampSize(rows, 32, 1, 200),
    scrollback: MIRROR_SCROLLBACK,
    allowProposedApi: true, // term.unicode is a proposed API
    logLevel: "off",
    vtExtensions: { kittyKeyboard: true }
  });
  const serializer = new SerializeAddon();
  term.loadAddon(serializer);
  // Measure wide characters (emoji, CJK) the way the browser terminal does.
  term.loadAddon(new Unicode11Addon());
  term.unicode.activeVersion = "11";

  let disposed = false;
  let writerAttached = false;
  let warnedBehind = false;
  let mouseEncoding = "default";
  let kitty = freshKitty();
  let finalModes = null;
  let finalSize = null;
  let dirty = false;
  let checkTimer = null;
  let lastCheckAt = now() - COUNTED_CHECK_MS;
  const disposables = [];
  const countedListeners = new Set();
  const pendingSnapshots = new Set();

  function currentModes() {
    const modes = term.modes;
    return {
      altScreen: term.buffer.active.type === "alternate",
      bracketedPaste: modes.bracketedPasteMode,
      mouseTracking: modes.mouseTrackingMode,
      mouseEncoding,
      focusReporting: modes.sendFocusMode,
      cursorKeysApp: modes.applicationCursorKeysMode,
      kittyFlags: kitty.flags
    };
  }

  // What a snapshot holds once the mirror is gone: no screen, the last size
  // and modes.
  function emptySnapshot() {
    const size = finalSize || { cols: term.cols, rows: term.rows };
    return { data: "", cols: size.cols, rows: size.rows, modes: { ...(finalModes || DEFAULT_MODES) } };
  }

  // The text above the bottom 6 rows of the visible screen, and where that
  // screen starts in the buffer (it moves when lines scroll away).
  function readScreen() {
    const buffer = term.buffer.active;
    const above = Math.max(0, term.rows - COUNTED_BOTTOM_ROWS);
    const lines = [];
    for (let y = 0; y < above; y += 1) {
      lines.push(buffer.getLine(buffer.baseY + y)?.translateToString(true) ?? "");
    }
    return { screen: buffer.type, baseY: buffer.baseY, text: lines.join("\n") };
  }

  let baseline = readScreen();

  function checkCounted() {
    checkTimer = null;
    if (disposed || !dirty) return;
    dirty = false;
    lastCheckAt = now();
    const current = readScreen();
    const scrolled = current.screen === baseline.screen && current.baseY !== baseline.baseY;
    const changed = current.text !== baseline.text;
    baseline = current;
    if (scrolled || changed) {
      for (const listener of [...countedListeners]) safeCall(listener);
    }
  }

  function markDirty() {
    if (disposed) return;
    dirty = true;
    if (checkTimer) return;
    const wait = Math.max(0, lastCheckAt + COUNTED_CHECK_MS - now());
    checkTimer = setTimeout(checkCounted, wait);
    checkTimer.unref?.();
  }

  // Modes the serializer leaves out: the mouse encoding and the kitty keyboard
  // flags. Every handler returns false, so xterm.js still applies the
  // sequence itself; this copy follows xterm.js's own rules.
  function trackPrivateModes(params, on) {
    for (let index = 0; index < params.length; index += 1) {
      const mode = param(params, index, -1);
      if (mode === 1006) mouseEncoding = on ? "sgr" : "default";
      else if (mode === 1016) mouseEncoding = on ? "sgr-pixels" : "default";
      else if (ALT_SCREEN_MODES.has(mode)) {
        // Each screen keeps its own kitty flags.
        if (on) {
          kitty.mainFlags = kitty.flags;
          kitty.flags = kitty.altFlags;
        } else {
          kitty.altFlags = kitty.flags;
          kitty.flags = kitty.mainFlags;
        }
      }
    }
    return false;
  }

  function kittyStack() {
    return term.buffer.active.type === "alternate" ? kitty.altStack : kitty.mainStack;
  }

  disposables.push(
    term.parser.registerCsiHandler({ prefix: "?", final: "h" }, (params) => trackPrivateModes(params, true)),
    term.parser.registerCsiHandler({ prefix: "?", final: "l" }, (params) => trackPrivateModes(params, false)),
    // CSI = flags ; mode u: 1 replaces, 2 sets bits, 3 clears bits.
    term.parser.registerCsiHandler({ prefix: "=", final: "u" }, (params) => {
      const value = param(params, 0, 0);
      const how = params.length > 1 ? param(params, 1, 1) || 1 : 1;
      if (how === 1) kitty.flags = value;
      else if (how === 2) kitty.flags |= value;
      else if (how === 3) kitty.flags &= ~value;
      return false;
    }),
    // CSI > flags u: push the current flags, then use the new ones.
    term.parser.registerCsiHandler({ prefix: ">", final: "u" }, (params) => {
      const stack = kittyStack();
      if (stack.length >= KITTY_STACK_LIMIT) stack.shift();
      stack.push(kitty.flags);
      kitty.flags = param(params, 0, 0);
      return false;
    }),
    // CSI < count u: pop; an emptied stack means no flags.
    term.parser.registerCsiHandler({ prefix: "<", final: "u" }, (params) => {
      const count = Math.max(1, param(params, 0, 1) || 1);
      const stack = kittyStack();
      for (let index = 0; index < count && stack.length > 0; index += 1) kitty.flags = stack.pop();
      if (stack.length === 0) kitty.flags = 0;
      return false;
    }),
    // ESC c (RIS, full reset) clears every mode.
    term.parser.registerEscHandler({ final: "c" }, () => {
      mouseEncoding = "default";
      kitty = freshKitty();
      return false;
    }),
    // xterm.js's own replies to terminal questions arrive here.
    term.onData((data) => {
      if (disposed || writerAttached) return;
      if (STANDARD_REPLY.test(data)) safeCall(reply, data);
    }),
    term.onBell(() => {
      if (!disposed) safeCall(alert, "bel");
    }),
    ...ALERT_OSC_IDS.map((id) =>
      term.parser.registerOscHandler(id, (payload) => {
        // Raw in SP3 (SP4 turns these into alert kinds). OSC 9;4 progress
        // reports are forwarded too; SP4 decides what they mean.
        if (!disposed) safeCall(alert, `${id};${payload}`.slice(0, ALERT_RAW_LIMIT));
        return true;
      })
    ),
    term.onWriteParsed(() => markDirty())
  );

  function write(chunk) {
    if (disposed || typeof chunk !== "string" || chunk.length === 0) return;
    try {
      term.write(chunk);
    } catch (error) {
      // xterm.js refuses more than 50 MB waiting to be read. Keep the server
      // running; the screen catches up on the agent's next redraw.
      if (!warnedBehind) {
        warnedBehind = true;
        console.warn(`Agent OS: a session's screen copy fell behind (${error.message}).`);
      }
    }
  }

  function resize(nextCols, nextRows) {
    if (disposed) return;
    const width = clampSize(nextCols, 0, 2, 500);
    const height = clampSize(nextRows, 0, 1, 200);
    if (!width || !height || (width === term.cols && height === term.rows)) return;
    term.resize(width, height);
    // Text moved by the reflow is not output.
    baseline = readScreen();
  }

  // The screen as of every chunk written before this call. xterm.js reads
  // writes later, in order; the empty write's callback runs right after the
  // earlier chunks are read and before any later one, so the serialized
  // screen is an exact cut. Chunks written after this call are not in it:
  // the caller sends those to the window as live output.
  function snapshot() {
    if (disposed) return Promise.resolve(emptySnapshot());
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      const waiter = { resolve };
      pendingSnapshots.add(waiter);
      const finish = () => {
        if (!pendingSnapshots.delete(waiter)) return;
        resolve(
          disposed
            ? emptySnapshot()
            : { data: serializer.serialize(), cols: term.cols, rows: term.rows, modes: currentModes() }
        );
      };
      try {
        term.write("", finish);
      } catch {
        finish();
      }
    });
  }

  function setWriterAttached(value) {
    writerAttached = Boolean(value);
  }

  function onCountedOutput(listener) {
    if (typeof listener !== "function" || disposed) return () => {};
    countedListeners.add(listener);
    return () => {
      countedListeners.delete(listener);
    };
  }

  function dispose() {
    if (disposed) return;
    finalSize = { cols: term.cols, rows: term.rows };
    try {
      finalModes = currentModes();
    } catch {
      finalModes = { ...DEFAULT_MODES };
    }
    disposed = true;
    if (checkTimer) clearTimeout(checkTimer);
    checkTimer = null;
    countedListeners.clear();
    for (const waiter of pendingSnapshots) waiter.resolve(emptySnapshot());
    pendingSnapshots.clear();
    for (const disposable of disposables) {
      try {
        disposable.dispose();
      } catch {
        // already gone
      }
    }
    try {
      term.dispose();
    } catch {
      // already gone
    }
  }

  return Object.freeze({ write, resize, snapshot, setWriterAttached, onCountedOutput, dispose });
}

// Sequences a terminal sends by itself, never typed by a person. A frame
// made only of these (and of mouse-motion reports) is not user input.
const AUTOMATIC_REPLIES = [
  /\x1b\[\?[\d;]*c/y, // DA1 reply
  /\x1b\[>[\d;]*c/y, // DA2 reply
  /\x1bP!\|[0-9A-Fa-f]*\x1b\\/y, // DA3 reply
  // Cursor position report, plain and private form. The old keyboard
  // encoding also sends Ctrl or Shift+F3 as CSI 1;<n>R; with the kitty
  // keyboard on (the default) F3 is sent differently, so only that old key
  // is affected.
  /\x1b\[\??\d+;\d+R/y,
  /\x1b\[[03]n/y, // status report
  /\x1b\[\?\d+(?:;\d+)*n/y, // private status replies, such as the colour scheme
  /\x1b\[\?\d*u/y, // kitty keyboard flags
  /\x1b\[\??\d+;\d+\$y/y, // mode report (DECRPM)
  /\x1bP>\|[^\x1b]*\x1b\\/y, // terminal name and version (XTVERSION)
  /\x1bP[01]\$r[^\x1b]*\x1b\\/y, // setting report (DECRQSS)
  /\x1b\](?:4;\d+|1\d);rgb:[0-9A-Fa-f]+\/[0-9A-Fa-f]+\/[0-9A-Fa-f]+(?:\x07|\x1b\\)/y, // OSC colour replies
  /\x1b\[[IO]/y // focus in, focus out
];
const SGR_MOUSE = /\x1b\[<(\d+);\d+;\d+[Mm]/y;
const X10_MOUSE = /\x1b\[M([\s\S])[\s\S][\s\S]/y;

// Bit 32 marks motion; 64 marks the wheel (which counts as input).
function isMouseMotion(button) {
  return (button & 32) === 32 && (button & 64) === 0;
}

function matchAt(pattern, text, index) {
  pattern.lastIndex = index;
  return pattern.exec(text);
}

export function isUserInput(data) {
  if (typeof data !== "string" || data.length === 0) return false;
  let index = 0;
  next: while (index < data.length) {
    for (const pattern of AUTOMATIC_REPLIES) {
      const match = matchAt(pattern, data, index);
      if (match) {
        index += match[0].length;
        continue next;
      }
    }
    const sgr = matchAt(SGR_MOUSE, data, index);
    if (sgr && isMouseMotion(Number(sgr[1]))) {
      index += sgr[0].length;
      continue;
    }
    const x10 = matchAt(X10_MOUSE, data, index);
    if (x10 && isMouseMotion(x10[1].charCodeAt(0) - 32)) {
      index += x10[0].length;
      continue;
    }
    return true; // a key, a paste, a click or the wheel
  }
  return false;
}
```

```js
// The wiring S6 does for every session: PTY output into the mirror, the
// mirror's replies back into the PTY.
async function runQueryProbe(dir, { writerAttached, waitMs }) {
  const script = await writeScript(dir, "ask.mjs", QUERY_PROBE);
  const alerts = [];
  let handle = null;
  const mirror = createMirror({
    cols: 80,
    rows: 24,
    onQueryReply: (reply) => handle?.write(reply),
    onAlert: (raw) => alerts.push(raw)
  });
  mirror.setWriterAttached(writerAttached);
  try {
    handle = await spawnPty({
      command: process.execPath,
      args: [script],
      cwd: dir,
      env: ptyEnv(dir, { PROBE_WAIT_MS: String(waitMs) }),
      cols: 80,
      rows: 24
    });
    const out = { text: "" };
    handle.onData((chunk) => {
      out.text += chunk;
      mirror.write(chunk);
    });
    const exit = exitOf(handle);
    const match = await waitFor(() => out.text.match(/GOT ("[^"]*")/), { what: "the probe's report" });
    assert.equal((await exit)?.exitCode, 0);
    await mirror.snapshot(); // everything the probe printed has been read
    return { got: JSON.parse(match[1]), alerts };
  } finally {
    handle?.kill("SIGKILL");
    mirror.dispose();
  }
}
```

#### Notes

1. **One xterm.js build on the server.** `@xterm/addon-serialize` reads xterm.js internals, so `@xterm/headless` and the serialize addon must stay the matching pair W0 pins; never bump one of them alone. The mirror also loads `@xterm/addon-unicode11` (the same build U2 uses), so a line holding an emoji or CJK text has the same width on the server's copy as in the window and a restored screen does not wrap differently. `term.unicode` is a proposed xterm.js API, hence `allowProposedApi: true`.
2. **Alert `raw` format (for SP4).** `"bel"` or `"<osc number>;<payload>"` (for example `"9;Approval requested"`, `"777;notify;Codex;Waiting"`, `"99;i=1:d=0;Hello"`), capped at 4096 characters, so SP4 can tell the three kinds apart. OSC `9;4;…` progress reports some agents send are forwarded too; SP4 decides what they mean.
3. **Modes the serializer leaves out.** The serialized `data` already restores the alternate screen, bracketed paste, focus reporting, cursor keys and mouse tracking. `mouseEncoding` and `kittyFlags` are tracked by the mirror itself, following xterm.js's own rules (kitty flags per screen, a stack of 16). xterm.js supports only the default, SGR (1006) and SGR-pixels (1016) mouse encodings; it logs and ignores 1005 and 1015, and the mirror ignores them too.
4. **Deliberate limits.**
   - Output that arrives before the first `onData` listener is kept up to 1 MB and the rest is dropped. The manager subscribes right after the spawn, so this only covers the program's first moments.
   - A node-pty that does not load stays unavailable until the server restarts; a failed probe (`node -e "process.exit(0)"` in a PTY, which also catches a `spawn-helper` that cannot run in a packaged app) is tried again after 30 s.
   - If xterm.js refuses a write (more than 50 MB waiting to be read), the mirror logs once and its screen copy stays incomplete until the agent redraws. The PTY and the recording are not affected.
   - `pty-host.js` throws plain `Error`s with `code: "pty_unavailable"` or `"spawn_failed"` and does not import `errors.js`: the manager (S6) checks `ptyAvailable()` first and answers a failed spawn with its own `start_failed` `sessionError`.
   - After a resize the agent redraws, which can count as output. The mirror resets its baseline at the resize; S6 also ignores counted output for 1 s after an applied resize.
   - `isUserInput` cannot tell the old keyboard encoding's Ctrl+F3 or Shift+F3 (`CSI 1;<n>R`) from a cursor-position reply, so that key alone does not count as input. With the kitty keyboard on (the default) F3 is sent differently.
   - The tests here start no session (there is no manager yet). They still follow the session tests' rules: `SHELL` is `FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL`, and `PATH` is `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, with the fake folder (all six fake names) first for the fake agent test.

---

### Task S5: recorder (asciicast v2, rotation, 1 GB cap, list/delete)

Every session is recorded: what its terminal showed, output only and never the input stream (spec Security 5). Text the agent echoes on screen, typed prompts and pasted text included, is part of that output and is recorded. This task builds `server/runtime/sessions/recorder.js`, which writes those recordings in the asciicast v2 format, a standard text format that terminal players read: one JSON header line, then one JSON event per line. It writes output events, plus "marker" and "resize" events, and has no way at all to record input.

- Each session keeps at most two segments of 25 MB in `<AGENT_OS_HOME>/sessions/<id>/`: `screen.cast` (newest) and `screen.prev.cast`.
- When `screen.cast` would pass 25 MB, it becomes `screen.prev.cast`, the older segment is deleted (the oldest output goes first), and the new `screen.cast` starts with an "[earlier output removed]" marker.
- A resumed session appends to the same file after a "--- resumed ---" marker, instead of writing a new header.
- A 1 GB cap across all recordings deletes the oldest ended recordings first and never touches a live one.
- All files are 0600.

The module also lists, streams and deletes recordings for the routes (S8).

The recorder throws the same `sessionError` the session manager uses. It imports it, with `SESSION_ID_RE`, from the shared module `server/runtime/sessions/errors.js`, which Task S3 creates and owns (ruling R4). This task only imports from that file and never creates or changes it. The routes (S8) turn each recorder error into its answer with that module's `errorBody(err)`.

**Files:**
- Create: `server/runtime/sessions/recorder.js`
- Test: `test/sessions-recorder.test.js` (new; 13 tests)
- Consumes (S3): `server/runtime/sessions/errors.js` (`SESSION_ID_RE`, `isSessionId`, `sessionError`, `errorBody`). Not changed here.
- No existing file changes.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (S2, `server/runtime/store.js`): `runtimePaths().sessions` (`<root>/sessions`), `ensurePrivateDir(dir)` (mkdir -p, mode 0700, chmod when it already exists), and `readJson(file, fallback)` (exists today).
- Consumes (S3, `server/runtime/sessions/errors.js`, ruling R4):
  - `export const SESSION_ID_RE = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/`
  - `export function isSessionId(value)` → boolean
  - `export function sessionError(status, code, message, extra = {})` → `Error` with `.status`, `.code`, `.message` and `.extra`, and no `.body`.
  - `export function errorBody(err)` → `{ error: err.code, message: err.message, ...err.extra }`.
  - `recorder.js` imports only `SESSION_ID_RE` and `sessionError` and passes no `extra`, so S8 answers every recorder error as exactly `{ error, message }`. The test also pins `isSessionId` and `errorBody`.
- Consumes (meta.json written by S6, read here): the keys `kind` (`"agent"`/`"update"`), `agentId`, `agentLabel`, `folder`, `folderName`, `folderShown`, `status` (`"starting"` while the process runs, `"exited"` after), `startedAt` (ISO 8601 UTC), `endedAt` (ISO 8601 UTC or null). A session counts as live when `status !== "exited"` and `endedAt` is empty, unless the caller passes `isLive`. The manager's `isLive` is `(id) => live.has(id)` (R8), so a session still closing its recording counts as live.
- Produces (`server/runtime/sessions/recorder.js`):
  - Constants: `CAST_FILE = "screen.cast"`, `PREV_CAST_FILE = "screen.prev.cast"`, `SEGMENT_BYTES = 26214400`, `RECORDING_CAP_BYTES = 1073741824`, `ROTATION_MARKER = "[earlier output removed]"`, `RESUME_MARKER = "--- resumed ---"`.
  - `export function createRecorder({ dir, cols, rows, segmentBytes = 26214400, append = false, now = Date.now, onError })` → `{ output(chunk), marker(text), resize(cols, rows), close() }`:
    - `output(chunk)` takes a string (empty or non-string is ignored);
    - `marker(text)` writes an asciicast `"m"` event;
    - `resize(cols, rows)` writes an `"r"` event `"<cols>x<rows>"`;
    - `close()` returns the same Promise every time and resolves when every queued event is on disk.

    Further behaviour:
    - writes happen in order in the background, so the three event methods never block;
    - event times are seconds since the header's `timestamp` (whole Unix seconds), rounded to 6 decimals, and never go backwards within one recorder;
    - `append: true` reads the existing header's `timestamp` and writes `[t, "m", "--- resumed ---"]` then `[t, "r", "<cols>x<rows>"]` instead of a new header (a new header when no recording is left). The recorder writes this marker itself; the manager never does (R8);
    - a recording that cannot be written calls `onError(error)` once (default: one `console.warn`) and then ignores further output. It never throws into the session.
  - `export async function listRecordings({ isLive } = {})` → `[{ sessionId, kind, agentId, agentLabel, folder, folderName, folderShown, startedAt, endedAt, bytes, live }]`, newest `startedAt` first (U1's `RecordingSummary`: `startedAt` is always a string, `endedAt` a string or null). Only sessions with a valid id folder, a readable meta.json that has a `startedAt` text, and at least one cast file are listed. `bytes` is the size of both segments together.
  - `export function enforceRecordingCap({ capBytes = 1073741824, isLive } = {})` → `Promise<{ deleted: string[] }>`. While the total is over the cap, it deletes the cast files of the ended recording with the oldest `endedAt` (falling back to `startedAt`). It never touches a live one, keeps meta.json, and runs one at a time.
  - `export function recordingsRemovedByCap()` → how many recordings the cap removed since the server started (Q38's note).
  - `export async function deleteRecording(sessionId, { isLive } = {})` → `{ ok: true }`. It throws `sessionError`:
    - 404 `unknown_session` "That session doesn't exist anymore." (bad id or no meta.json);
    - 409 `recording_live` "That session is still running. Stop it first, then delete its recording.";
    - 404 `recording_missing` "That recording doesn't exist anymore.".

    It removes only `screen.cast` and `screen.prev.cast`; meta.json, and with it the ended tab and Resume, stays.
  - `export async function openRecording(sessionId)` → `{ lines: AsyncGenerator<string> }`. It implements Q26's stream for `GET /api/sessions/:id/recording`:
    - one header line (the older segment's when it exists), then the older segment's events, then the newer segment's events;
    - it leaves out the newer segment's header and its leading rotation marker, so "[earlier output removed]" appears only at the very start;
    - each line ends with "\n", and a last line still being written is left out;
    - it throws 404 `unknown_session` or `recording_missing` before anything is streamed.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing tests.** Create `test/sessions-recorder.test.js` with exactly this content:

```js
// Session recordings (asciicast v2): output only, never input; two segments of
// 25 MB with the oldest output dropped first; a marker when a resumed session
// continues; a 1 GB cap across all recordings that never touches a live one;
// and listing, streaming and deleting them. Everything is written to a temp
// AGENT_OS_HOME only.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import crypto from "node:crypto";
import { appendFile, mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, realpath, rm, stat, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import test from "node:test";
import { SESSION_ID_RE, errorBody, isSessionId, sessionError } from "../server/runtime/sessions/errors.js";
import {
  CAST_FILE,
  PREV_CAST_FILE,
  RECORDING_CAP_BYTES,
  RESUME_MARKER,
  ROTATION_MARKER,
  SEGMENT_BYTES,
  createRecorder,
  deleteRecording,
  enforceRecordingCap,
  listRecordings,
  openRecording,
  recordingsRemovedByCap
} from "../server/runtime/sessions/recorder.js";

const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";
const START = 1_760_000_000_000; // a whole second, so event times come out exact

function makeClock(start = START) {
  let current = start;
  return {
    now: () => current,
    tick: (ms) => {
      current += ms;
    }
  };
}

async function withTempHome(fn) {
  const home = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-recorder-home-")));
  const previous = process.env.AGENT_OS_HOME;
  process.env.AGENT_OS_HOME = home;
  try {
    return await fn(home);
  } finally {
    if (previous === undefined) delete process.env.AGENT_OS_HOME;
    else process.env.AGENT_OS_HOME = previous;
    await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

function sessionDir(home, id) {
  return path.join(home, "sessions", id);
}

async function exists(file) {
  try {
    await stat(file);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

async function readCast(file) {
  const text = await readFile(file, "utf8");
  assert.ok(text.endsWith("\n"), `${path.basename(file)}: every line ends with a newline`);
  return text
    .slice(0, -1)
    .split("\n")
    .map((line) => JSON.parse(line));
}

async function collectLines(lines) {
  const out = [];
  for await (const line of lines) out.push(line);
  return out;
}

// A session folder the way S6 leaves it: meta.json, and optionally cast files.
async function makeSession(home, { meta = {}, cast = null, prev = null } = {}) {
  const id = crypto.randomUUID();
  const dir = sessionDir(home, id);
  await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
  await writeFile(
    path.join(dir, "meta.json"),
    JSON.stringify({
      id,
      kind: "agent",
      agentId: "claude",
      agentLabel: "Claude Code",
      folder: "/Users/you/projects/app",
      folderName: "app",
      folderShown: true,
      status: "exited",
      startedAt: "2026-10-14T09:00:00.000Z",
      endedAt: "2026-10-14T09:30:00.000Z",
      ...meta
    })
  );
  if (cast !== null) await writeFile(path.join(dir, CAST_FILE), cast);
  if (prev !== null) await writeFile(path.join(dir, PREV_CAST_FILE), prev);
  return id;
}

// 40 numbered chunks of about 330 bytes each into 4 KB segments: three
// rotations, so the first segment is gone and both files start with a marker.
async function recordChunks(dir) {
  const clock = makeClock();
  const recorder = createRecorder({ dir, cols: 80, rows: 24, segmentBytes: 4096, now: clock.now });
  for (let i = 0; i < 40; i += 1) {
    clock.tick(100);
    recorder.output(`chunk-${String(i).padStart(2, "0")} ${"x".repeat(300)}\r\n`);
  }
  await recorder.close();
}

// errors.js is S3's module (ruling R4); this test pins the parts the recorder
// relies on, and the answer the routes build from a recorder error.
test("sessionError (from S3) carries status, code, message and extra, errorBody is its answer, and SESSION_ID_RE accepts only randomUUID ids", () => {
  const error = sessionError(400, "folder_refused", "Your home folder itself can't be used. Pick a folder inside it.", {
    code: "is_home"
  });
  assert.ok(error instanceof Error);
  assert.equal(error.status, 400);
  assert.equal(error.code, "folder_refused");
  assert.equal(error.message, "Your home folder itself can't be used. Pick a folder inside it.");
  assert.deepEqual(error.extra, { code: "is_home" });
  assert.equal("body" in error, false, "one error shape: no .body");
  assert.deepEqual(errorBody(error), {
    error: "folder_refused",
    message: "Your home folder itself can't be used. Pick a folder inside it.",
    code: "is_home"
  });
  // A recorder error passes no extra, so its answer is exactly { error, message }.
  const missing = sessionError(404, "recording_missing", "That recording doesn't exist anymore.");
  assert.ok(missing instanceof Error);
  assert.equal(missing.status, 404);
  assert.equal(missing.code, "recording_missing");
  assert.equal(missing.message, "That recording doesn't exist anymore.");
  assert.deepEqual(errorBody(missing), { error: "recording_missing", message: "That recording doesn't exist anymore." });

  const id = crypto.randomUUID();
  assert.ok(SESSION_ID_RE.test(id));
  assert.equal(isSessionId(id), true);
  for (const bad of [id.toUpperCase(), "../etc/passwd", "", "6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8", `${id}/..`, null, 42]) {
    assert.equal(isSessionId(bad), false, String(bad));
  }
});

test("a recording is asciicast v2 with output, marker and resize events only, in private files", async () => {
  await withTempHome(async (home) => {
    const dir = sessionDir(home, crypto.randomUUID());
    const clock = makeClock();
    const recorder = createRecorder({ dir, cols: 100, rows: 30, now: clock.now });
    assert.equal("input" in recorder, false, "there is no way to record input");
    clock.tick(500);
    recorder.output("hello\r\n");
    clock.tick(250);
    recorder.output("\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m");
    clock.tick(250);
    recorder.resize(90, 25);
    clock.tick(1000);
    recorder.marker("checkpoint");
    await recorder.close();

    const [header, ...events] = await readCast(path.join(dir, CAST_FILE));
    assert.deepEqual(header, { version: 2, width: 100, height: 30, timestamp: 1760000000 });
    assert.deepEqual(events, [
      [0.5, "o", "hello\r\n"],
      [0.75, "o", "\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m"],
      [1, "r", "90x25"],
      [2, "m", "checkpoint"]
    ]);
    if (!isWindows) {
      assert.equal((await stat(dir)).mode & 0o777, 0o700, "the session folder is private");
      assert.equal((await stat(path.join(dir, CAST_FILE))).mode & 0o777, 0o600, "the recording is private");
    }
  });
});

test("output after close is ignored, close returns the same promise, and empty or non-text output is skipped", async () => {
  await withTempHome(async (home) => {
    const dir = sessionDir(home, crypto.randomUUID());
    const clock = makeClock();
    const recorder = createRecorder({ dir, cols: 80, rows: 24, now: clock.now });
    clock.tick(100);
    recorder.output("");
    recorder.output(Buffer.from("not text"));
    recorder.output("kept");
    recorder.marker("   ");
    recorder.resize(0, 24);
    const closing = recorder.close();
    recorder.output("too late");
    assert.equal(recorder.close(), closing);
    await closing;
    const [, ...events] = await readCast(path.join(dir, CAST_FILE));
    assert.deepEqual(events, [[0.1, "o", "kept"]]);
  });
});

test("a recording that cannot be written reports once and never throws into the session", async () => {
  assert.throws(() => createRecorder({ dir: "relative/folder", cols: 80, rows: 24 }), TypeError);
  await withTempHome(async (home) => {
    const notAFolder = path.join(home, "a-file");
    await writeFile(notAFolder, "x");
    const errors = [];
    const recorder = createRecorder({ dir: notAFolder, cols: 80, rows: 24, onError: (error) => errors.push(error) });
    recorder.output("one");
    recorder.output("two");
    recorder.marker("three");
    await recorder.close();
    assert.equal(errors.length, 1);
    assert.ok(errors[0] instanceof Error);
  });
});

test("at the segment size the newer file becomes screen.prev.cast, the oldest output goes first, and each new segment starts with a marker", async () => {
  await withTempHome(async (home) => {
    const dir = sessionDir(home, crypto.randomUUID());
    await recordChunks(dir);
    const castPath = path.join(dir, CAST_FILE);
    const prevPath = path.join(dir, PREV_CAST_FILE);
    for (const file of [castPath, prevPath]) {
      const info = await stat(file);
      assert.ok(info.size <= 4096, `${path.basename(file)} stays within the segment size (${info.size} bytes)`);
      if (!isWindows) assert.equal(info.mode & 0o777, 0o600, `${path.basename(file)} is private`);
    }
    const newer = await readCast(castPath);
    const older = await readCast(prevPath);
    assert.deepEqual(newer[0], { version: 2, width: 80, height: 24, timestamp: 1760000000 });
    assert.deepEqual(older[0], newer[0], "every segment keeps the recording's start time");
    assert.deepEqual(newer[1].slice(1), ["m", ROTATION_MARKER]);
    assert.deepEqual(older[1].slice(1), ["m", ROTATION_MARKER], "after several rotations the older segment also follows removed output");
    assert.equal(ROTATION_MARKER, "[earlier output removed]");
    const all = JSON.stringify([...older, ...newer]);
    assert.equal(all.includes("chunk-00 "), false, "the oldest output was dropped");
    assert.ok(all.includes("chunk-39 "), "the newest output is kept");
  });
});

test("the default segment size is 25 MB, and rotation really happens there", async () => {
  assert.equal(SEGMENT_BYTES, 26214400);
  await withTempHome(async (home) => {
    const dir = sessionDir(home, crypto.randomUUID());
    const clock = makeClock();
    const recorder = createRecorder({ dir, cols: 80, rows: 24, now: clock.now });
    const megabyte = "x".repeat(1024 * 1024);
    for (let i = 0; i < 27; i += 1) {
      clock.tick(10);
      recorder.output(megabyte);
    }
    await recorder.close();
    const older = (await stat(path.join(dir, PREV_CAST_FILE))).size;
    const newer = (await stat(path.join(dir, CAST_FILE))).size;
    assert.ok(older <= SEGMENT_BYTES, `screen.prev.cast is ${older} bytes`);
    assert.ok(older > 20 * 1024 * 1024, "the first segment filled up before it rotated");
    assert.ok(newer < 4 * 1024 * 1024, `screen.cast is ${newer} bytes`);
  });
});

test("a resumed session appends after a marker instead of a new header, on one timeline", async () => {
  await withTempHome(async (home) => {
    const dir = sessionDir(home, crypto.randomUUID());
    const clock = makeClock();
    const first = createRecorder({ dir, cols: 80, rows: 24, now: clock.now });
    clock.tick(1500);
    first.output("before\r\n");
    await first.close();

    clock.tick(60000);
    const second = createRecorder({ dir, cols: 100, rows: 30, append: true, now: clock.now });
    clock.tick(500);
    second.output("after\r\n");
    await second.close();

    const [header, ...events] = await readCast(path.join(dir, CAST_FILE));
    assert.deepEqual(header, { version: 2, width: 80, height: 24, timestamp: 1760000000 });
    assert.deepEqual(events, [
      [1.5, "o", "before\r\n"],
      [61.5, "m", RESUME_MARKER],
      [61.5, "r", "100x30"],
      [62, "o", "after\r\n"]
    ]);
    assert.equal(RESUME_MARKER, "--- resumed ---");
    if (!isWindows) assert.equal((await stat(path.join(dir, CAST_FILE))).mode & 0o777, 0o600);
  });
});

test("openRecording streams one header, the older segment, then the newer one without its rotation marker", async () => {
  await withTempHome(async (home) => {
    const id = crypto.randomUUID();
    await recordChunks(sessionDir(home, id));
    const lines = await collectLines((await openRecording(id)).lines);
    for (const line of lines) assert.ok(line.endsWith("\n"));
    const entries = lines.map((line) => JSON.parse(line));
    assert.deepEqual(entries[0], { version: 2, width: 80, height: 24, timestamp: 1760000000 });
    assert.equal(entries.filter((entry) => !Array.isArray(entry)).length, 1, "one header");
    const events = entries.slice(1);
    assert.deepEqual(events[0].slice(1), ["m", ROTATION_MARKER], "the stream starts by saying earlier output was removed");
    assert.equal(events.filter((event) => event[1] === "m").length, 1, "the newer segment's own marker is left out");
    const numbers = events.filter((event) => event[1] === "o").map((event) => Number(event[2].slice(6, 8)));
    assert.ok(numbers[0] > 0, "the oldest output is gone");
    assert.equal(numbers.at(-1), 39);
    numbers.forEach((number, index) => {
      if (index > 0) assert.equal(number, numbers[index - 1] + 1, "nothing missing or repeated between the segments");
    });
    events.forEach((event, index) => {
      if (index > 0) assert.ok(event[0] >= events[index - 1][0], "times never go back");
    });
  });
});

test("openRecording leaves out a line still being written, and answers 404 for odd ids, unknown sessions and missing recordings", async () => {
  await withTempHome(async (home) => {
    const id = crypto.randomUUID();

    const clock = makeClock();
    const recorder = createRecorder({ dir, cols: 80, rows: 24, now: clock.now });

    recorder.output("whole line\r\n");
    await recorder.close();
    await appendFile(path.join(dir, CAST_FILE), '[9.5,"o","half a li');
    const lines = await collectLines((await openRecording(id)).lines);
    assert.equal(lines.length, 2, "the header and the one complete event");
    assert.deepEqual(JSON.parse(lines[1]), [0.1, "o", "whole line\r\n"]);

    await assert.rejects(
      () => openRecording("../../etc"),
      (error) => error.status === 404 && error.code === "unknown_session"
    );
    await assert.rejects(
      () => openRecording(crypto.randomUUID()),

    );

    await assert.rejects(
      () => openRecording(noFiles),

    );
  });
});

test("the 1 GB cap removes the oldest ended recordings first, never a live one, and one cap run at a time", async () => {
  assert.equal(RECORDING_CAP_BYTES, 1073741824);
  await withTempHome(async (home) => {
    const oldest = await makeSession(home, {
      meta: { startedAt: "2026-10-14T08:00:00.000Z", endedAt: "2026-10-14T08:10:00.000Z" },
      cast: "a".repeat(400)
    });
    const newer = await makeSession(home, {
      meta: { startedAt: "2026-10-14T09:00:00.000Z", endedAt: "2026-10-14T09:10:00.000Z" },
      cast: "b".repeat(300),
      prev: "b".repeat(100)
    });
    const live = await makeSession(home, {
      meta: { status: "live", startedAt: "2026-10-14T07:00:00.000Z", endedAt: null },
      cast: "c".repeat(400)
    });
    const before = recordingsRemovedByCap();

    assert.deepEqual(await enforceRecordingCap(), { deleted: [] }, "1 200 bytes are far under 1 GB");

    const [first, second] = await Promise.all([
      enforceRecordingCap({ capBytes: 900 }),
      enforceRecordingCap({ capBytes: 900 })
    ]);
    assert.deepEqual(first, { deleted: [oldest] });
    assert.deepEqual(second, { deleted: [] }, "the second run sees the first one's result");
    assert.equal(await exists(path.join(sessionDir(home, oldest), CAST_FILE)), false);
    assert.ok(await exists(path.join(sessionDir(home, oldest), "meta.json")), "the session itself stays");

    assert.deepEqual(
      await enforceRecordingCap({ capBytes: 100, isLive: (id) => id === newer || id === live }),
      { deleted: [] },
      "what the manager says is live is never removed"
    );
    assert.deepEqual(await enforceRecordingCap({ capBytes: 100 }), { deleted: [newer] });
    assert.equal(await exists(path.join(sessionDir(home, newer), PREV_CAST_FILE)), false, "both segments go");
    assert.deepEqual(
      (await listRecordings()).map((recording) => recording.sessionId),
      [live],
      "the live recording stays, even over the cap"
    );
    assert.equal(recordingsRemovedByCap() - before, 2);
  });
});

test("deleteRecording removes an ended session's recording files only, and refuses live, unknown and odd ids", async () => {
  await withTempHome(async (home) => {
    const live = await makeSession(home, { meta: { status: "live", endedAt: null }, cast: "x" });
    const ended = await makeSession(home, { cast: "x", prev: "y" });

    await assert.rejects(
      () => deleteRecording("../../etc"),
      (error) => error.status === 404 && error.code === "unknown_session" && error.message === "That session doesn't exist anymore."
    );
    await assert.rejects(
      () => deleteRecording(crypto.randomUUID()),
      (error) => error.status === 404 && error.code === "unknown_session"
    );
    await assert.rejects(
      () => deleteRecording(live),
      (error) =>
        error.status === 409 &&
        error.code === "recording_live" &&
        error.message === "That session is still running. Stop it first, then delete its recording."
    );
    assert.ok(await exists(path.join(sessionDir(home, live), CAST_FILE)), "a live recording is kept");
    await assert.rejects(
      () => deleteRecording(ended, { isLive: (id) => id === ended }),
      (error) => error.status === 409 && error.code === "recording_live"
    );

    assert.deepEqual(await deleteRecording(ended), { ok: true });
    assert.equal(await exists(path.join(sessionDir(home, ended), CAST_FILE)), false);
    assert.equal(await exists(path.join(sessionDir(home, ended), PREV_CAST_FILE)), false);
    assert.ok(await exists(path.join(sessionDir(home, ended), "meta.json")), "the session itself stays (ended tab, Resume)");
    await assert.rejects(
      () => deleteRecording(ended),
      (error) => error.status === 404 && error.code === "recording_missing" && error.message === "That recording doesn't exist anymore."
    );
  });
});
```
