```ts

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Sessions (SP3): an agent's own terminal, kept by server/runtime/sessions/. These mirror manager.js's
// SessionSummary, routes.js's answers and ws.js's frames (spec "SP3 Sessions engine and page"; the SP3
// contract). Frames are read defensively by src/ui/sessionsShared.ts (parseServerFrame).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export type SessionKind = "agent" | "update";

// "waiting" and "held" are never produced in SP3; they arrive with SP4's signals.
export type SessionStatus = "starting" | "live" | "waiting" | "idle" | "held" | "exited";

// "stop" or "quit" when Agent OS ended the session, otherwise null.
export type SessionEndedBy = "stop" | "quit" | null;

export interface SessionSummary {
  id: string;
  kind: SessionKind;
  agentId: string;
  // The short name: "Claude Code", "Codex", "Cursor", "Hermes", "OpenClaw".
  agentLabel: string;
  folder: string;
  folderName: string;
  // false for OpenClaw until spike S5: it picks its own folder, so none is shown or claimed.
  folderShown: boolean;
  branch: string | null;
  status: SessionStatus;
  // When the current status began (ISO time), for "Idle for <time>".
  stateSince: string;
  startedAt: string;
  endedAt: string | null;
  // null when a signal ended the process.
  exitCode: number | null;
  signal: string | null;
  endedBy: SessionEndedBy;
  dismissed: boolean;
  brain: { kind: "plan" | "openrouter" | "local"; label: string } | null;
  resume: { available: boolean; reason: string | null; fallback: boolean };
  // Every session's alerts are "basic" in SP3 (the 20 s rule).
  alerts: "basic";
  recordingBytes: number;
}

export interface SessionListResponse {
  sessions: SessionSummary[];
  // The quiet one-line notice when the login-shell environment could not be read (H2), else null.
  environmentNotice: string | null;
  pty: { ok: boolean; reason: string | null };
  maxLive: number;
}

// POST /api/sessions/:id/stop: the session (unchanged when it had already ended), plus Stop's note: OpenClaw's
// honest "Stopped the terminal. OpenClaw may still be finishing its last step." when only its terminal could be
// stopped, otherwise null.
export interface StopSessionResult extends SessionSummary {
  note: string | null;
}

export interface SessionSettings {
  claudeFullscreen: boolean;
}

export interface SessionFolder {
  path: string;
  name: string;
  lastUsedAt: string;
}

export interface SessionFolderList {
  folders: SessionFolder[];
}

export interface QuitCheckItem {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  // An update session is never resumed, so the quit question promises a resume only when none is listed.
  kind: SessionKind;
}

export interface QuitCheckResponse {
  live: QuitCheckItem[];
}

export interface RecordingSummary {
  sessionId: string;
  // Update rows read "<agent> update" (spec, Session kinds).
  kind: SessionKind;
  agentId: string;
  agentLabel: string;
  folder: string;
  folderName: string;
  // false for OpenClaw until spike S5: its row reads "OpenClaw · Set by OpenClaw", never a folder it may not use.
  folderShown: boolean;
  startedAt: string;
  endedAt: string | null;
  bytes: number;
  live: boolean;
}

export interface RecordingListResponse {
  recordings: RecordingSummary[];
  // How many recordings were removed to stay under 1 GB since the server started (Q38).
  removedByCap: number;
}

// The terminal modes a snapshot carries (mirror.js), put back on reattach (spec, Browser terminal).
export type MouseTrackingMode = "none" | "x10" | "vt200" | "drag" | "any";
export type MouseEncodingMode = "default" | "sgr" | "sgr-pixels";

export interface SessionModes {
  altScreen: boolean;
  bracketedPaste: boolean;
  mouseTracking: MouseTrackingMode;
  mouseEncoding: MouseEncodingMode;
  focusReporting: boolean;
  cursorKeysApp: boolean;
  kittyFlags: number;
}

export interface SessionSnapshot {
  data: string;
  cols: number;
  rows: number;
  modes: SessionModes;
}

export interface SessionStateFrame {
  status: SessionStatus;
  exitCode: number | null;
  signal: string | null;
  endedBy: SessionEndedBy;
  resetAt: string | null;
}

// Server to client, one JSON message per frame (ws.js).
export type SessionServerFrame =
  | ({ t: "snapshot" } & SessionSnapshot)
  | { t: "out"; seq: number; d: string }
  | ({ t: "state" } & SessionStateFrame)
  | { t: "alert"; raw: string };

// Client to server.
export type SessionClientFrame =
  | { t: "focus" }
  | { t: "in"; d: string }
  | { t: "resize"; cols: number; rows: number }
  | { t: "ack"; seq: number };
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the shared rules.** Create `src/ui/sessionsShared.ts`:

```ts
// Sessions (SP3): the words and small rules shared by the Sessions page, Home, Runs, the menu and the quit
// question, plus the pure half of the terminal's WebSocket protocol (frame sizes, acks, reading a frame).
// `import type` only (decision P14): test/sessions-shared.test.js loads this file straight from src/ and
// Node strips the types.
import type {
  MouseEncodingMode,
  MouseTrackingMode,
  QuitCheckItem,
  SessionModes,
  SessionServerFrame,
  SessionStatus,
  SessionSummary
} from "../types";
import type { StatusState } from "./components/StatusWord";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Titles, status words and the side panel's line
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// What every tab, dialog and recording calls a session: "Claude Code · my-app". OpenClaw picks its own
// folder until spike S5, so its sessions read "OpenClaw · Set by OpenClaw". An update session is
// "<agent> update" (spec, Session kinds). "—" stands in for a folder name that is not known.
export function sessionTitle(s: Pick<SessionSummary, "kind" | "agentLabel" | "folderName" | "folderShown">): string {
  if (s.kind === "update") return `${s.agentLabel} update`;
  if (s.folderShown === false) return `${s.agentLabel} · Set by OpenClaw`;
  return `${s.agentLabel} · ${s.folderName || "—"}`;
}

// The kit's status words (planning decision Q18): "Starting" and "Ended" are new labels on existing
// states, not new colours. An unknown status from the server shows "—".
const STATE_WORDS: Record<SessionStatus, { state: StatusState; label: string }> = {
  starting: { state: "idle", label: "Starting" },
  live: { state: "live", label: "Live" },
  waiting: { state: "waiting", label: "Waiting for you" },
  idle: { state: "idle", label: "Idle" },
  held: { state: "held", label: "Held" },
  exited: { state: "stopped", label: "Ended" }
};

function knownStatus(status: unknown): status is SessionStatus {
  return typeof status === "string" && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(STATE_WORDS, status);
}

export function sessionStateWord(s: Pick<SessionSummary, "status">): { state: StatusState; label: string } {
  return knownStatus(s.status) ? STATE_WORDS[s.status] : { state: "unknown", label: "" };
}

// A session whose program is still running: every status but "exited" (an unknown status is not counted).
export function isSessionRunning(s: Pick<SessionSummary, "status">): boolean {
  return knownStatus(s.status) && s.status !== "exited";
}

// The menu's count: running AGENT sessions only; an update session is never shown there (spec, Session kinds).
export function runningSessionCount(sessions: ReadonlyArray<Pick<SessionSummary, "kind" | "status">>): number {
  return sessions.filter((s) => s.kind === "agent" && isSessionRunning(s)).length;
}

// "under 1 m", "26 m", "1 h 05 m" (the same words as Home's elapsedLabel); "—" when not known.
export function sessionDuration(fromIso: string | null | undefined, now: number): string {
  const from = fromIso ? Date.parse(fromIso) : NaN;
  if (!Number.isFinite(from) || now < from) return "—";
  const minutes = Math.floor((now - from) / 60_000);
  if (minutes < 1) return "under 1 m";
  if (minutes < 60) return `${minutes} m`;
  return `${Math.floor(minutes / 60)} h ${String(minutes % 60).padStart(2, "0")} m`;
}

type EndFields = Pick<SessionSummary, "exitCode" | "signal" | "endedBy">;

// How a session ended, in words (spec, the side panel's exited lines). Agent OS's own Stop and quit come
// first, because both end the program with a signal; then a signal, which says more than an exit code
// that comes with it.
export function endedLine(s: EndFields): string {
  if (s.endedBy === "stop") return "Stopped by you.";
  if (s.endedBy === "quit") return "Ended when Agent OS quit.";
  if (typeof s.signal === "string" && s.signal.trim()) return `Ended by signal ${s.signal.trim()}.`;
  if (s.exitCode === 0) return "Ended normally.";
  if (typeof s.exitCode === "number" && Number.isFinite(s.exitCode)) return `Ended with exit code ${s.exitCode}.`;
  return "Ended.";
}

// The side panel's one line for the state, SP3 versions (spec, Session activity states). Before alerts
// exist, live says only "Working."; waiting and held never happen in SP3 but get true words anyway. An
// ended session's recording holds at least its header line, so 0 bytes means the 1 GB cap (Q38) or a
// delete removed it: then Runs has no row for it, and the line does not send the person there.
export function sessionPanelLine(
  s: Pick<SessionSummary, "status" | "agentLabel" | "recordingBytes"> & { stateSince?: string | null } & EndFields,
  now: number
): string {
  switch (s.status) {
    case "starting":
      return `Starting ${s.agentLabel}…`;
    case "live":
      return "Working.";
    case "waiting":
      return "The question is in the terminal. Agent OS never answers for you.";
    case "idle": {
      const time = sessionDuration(s.stateSince, now);
      return time === "—" ? "Idle. Nothing is running." : `Idle for ${time}. Nothing is running.`;
    }
    case "held":
      return "Plan limit reached.";
    case "exited":
      return s.recordingBytes > 0 ? `${endedLine(s)} The recording is in Runs.` : `${endedLine(s)} Its recording was removed.`;
    default:
      return "";
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The Stop dialog and the Resume confirm
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

type DialogFields = Pick<SessionSummary, "kind" | "agentId" | "agentLabel" | "folderName" | "folderShown">;

export interface StopDialogCopy {
  title: string;
  body: string;
  note: string | null;
  cancel: string;
  confirm: string;
}

// The Stop dialog (spec, the prototype's stopDialog()). OpenClaw adds what Stop cannot promise for it
// until spike S5.
export function stopDialogCopy(s: DialogFields): StopDialogCopy {
  return {
    title: `Stop ${sessionTitle(s)}?`,
    body: `This ends ${s.agentLabel} in this tab. The recording stays in Runs.`,
    note: s.agentId === "openclaw" ? "OpenClaw may still finish its last step after the terminal closes." : null,
    cancel: "Keep it running",
    confirm: "Stop session"
  };
}

export interface ResumeConfirmCopy {
  title: string;
  body: string;
  warning: string | null;
  blocked: string | null;
  cancel: string;
  confirm: string;
}

// Resume conversation's confirm (spec, Resume per agent; planning decision Q36). `blocked` is the written
// reason when the rules say no (the button is disabled and shows it); `warning` is a fallback resume's
// honest limit.
export function resumeConfirmCopy(s: DialogFields & Pick<SessionSummary, "resume">): ResumeConfirmCopy {
  const resume = s.resume || { available: false, reason: null, fallback: false };
  return {
    title: `Resume ${sessionTitle(s)}?`,
    body: `This starts ${s.agentLabel} again in the same tab and continues the conversation. The recording continues after a marker.`,
    warning: resume.fallback
      ? `This resumes the most recent ${s.agentLabel} conversation in this folder, which may be one you started outside Agent OS.`
      : null,
    blocked: resume.available ? null : resume.reason || "This session can't be resumed.",
    cancel: "Cancel",
    confirm: "Resume conversation"
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Keys (spec, App shortcuts (precedence))
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export function isMacPlatform(platform: string): boolean {
  return /mac/i.test(platform || "");
}

// The parts of a KeyboardEvent these rules read (a real KeyboardEvent fits).
export interface KeyLike {
  key: string;
  code?: string;
  metaKey: boolean;
  ctrlKey: boolean;
  altKey: boolean;
  shiftKey: boolean;
}

export type AppShortcut = { action: "palette" } | { action: "new-session" } | { action: "switch"; index: number };

// The letter pressed, also on a keyboard layout that types another letter in that place (for example
// Cyrillic): then the key's place (event.code) decides.
function isLetter(event: KeyLike, letter: string): boolean {
  const pressed = (event.key || "").toLowerCase();
  if (pressed === letter) return true;
  return !/^[a-z]$/.test(pressed) && event.code === `Key${letter.toUpperCase()}`;
}

// 1 to 9 on the number row: by the key's place first, because Shift changes the character (Ctrl+Shift+1 types "!").
function rowDigit(event: KeyLike): number | null {
  const byPlace = /^Digit([1-9])$/.exec(event.code || "");
  if (byPlace) return Number(byPlace[1]);
  return /^[1-9]$/.test(event.key || "") ? Number(event.key) : null;
}

// The palette key OUTSIDE a terminal: ⌘K on a Mac, Ctrl+K elsewhere, never both on one computer.
export function isPaletteKey(event: KeyLike, { isMac }: { isMac: boolean }): boolean {
  if (event.altKey || event.shiftKey) return false;
  const held = isMac ? event.metaKey && !event.ctrlKey : event.ctrlKey && !event.metaKey;
  return held && isLetter(event, "k");
}

// The only keys a terminal leaves to Agent OS: ⌘K, ⌘T and ⌘1-9 on a Mac; Ctrl+Shift+K/T/1-9 elsewhere.
// Everything else goes to the agent, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+R included. A browser keeps ⌘T and ⌘1-9 (Ctrl+T,
// Ctrl+1-9, Ctrl+Shift+T) for itself, so in browser mode only the palette key is Agent OS's. ⌘\ (split)
// arrives with SP4 and is not taken yet.
export function isAppShortcut(event: KeyLike, { isMac, desktop }: { isMac: boolean; desktop: boolean }): AppShortcut | null {
  if (event.altKey) return null;
  const held = isMac ? event.metaKey && !event.ctrlKey && !event.shiftKey : event.ctrlKey && event.shiftKey && !event.metaKey;
  if (!held) return null;
  if (isLetter(event, "k")) return { action: "palette" };
  if (!desktop) return null;
  if (isLetter(event, "t")) return { action: "new-session" };
  const digit = rowDigit(event);
  return digit === null ? null : { action: "switch", index: digit - 1 };
}

// The side panel footer's hints: desktop app only, nothing in browser mode (spec, Browser mode).
export function shortcutHints({ isMac, desktop }: { isMac: boolean; desktop: boolean }): Array<{ keys: string; word: string }> {
  if (!desktop) return [];
  return isMac
    ? [{ keys: "⌘T", word: "new" }, { keys: "⌘1-9", word: "switch" }]
    : [{ keys: "Ctrl+Shift+T", word: "new" }, { keys: "Ctrl+Shift+1-9", word: "switch" }];
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The quit question (desktop app; planning decision Q6)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const QUIT_REQUESTED_EVENT = "agentos://quit-requested";
export const QUIT_SHOWN_EVENT = "agentos://quit-shown";
export const QUIT_ANSWER_EVENT = "agentos://quit-answer";
// The shell quits on its own when no window says "quit-shown" within 2 s. A local answer normally takes a
// few milliseconds; when it takes longer than this, the question shows "Checking…" first.
export const QUIT_FAST_MS = 700;
// How much longer the question waits for the list before it says it could not check.
export const QUIT_CHECK_MS = 6000;

export type QuitView = { phase: "checking" } | { phase: "asking"; live: QuitCheckItem[] } | { phase: "unknown" };

// "A", "A and B", "A, B and C", "A, B, C, D and 2 more".
export function joinNames(names: string[], max = 4): string {
  const shown = names.slice(0, max);
  const rest = names.length - shown.length;
  const parts = rest > 0 ? [...shown, `${rest} more`] : shown;
  if (parts.length <= 1) return parts[0] ?? "";
  return `${parts.slice(0, -1).join(", ")} and ${parts[parts.length - 1]}`;
}

// The quit question's words (planning decisions, "Quit question"; ruling R21). An update session is never
// resumed (spec, Session kinds), so the agent sentence, with its resume promise, covers only agent sessions,
// and a running update gets its own sentence. Its title is already "<agent> update" (S6, decision Q27).
export function quitQuestionCopy(view: QuitView): { title: string; body: string; keep: string; quit: string } {
  const base = { title: "Quit Agent OS?", keep: "Keep running", quit: "Quit" };
  if (view.phase === "checking") return { ...base, body: "Checking which sessions are still running…" };
  if (view.phase === "unknown") {
    return { ...base, body: "Agent OS couldn't check which sessions are running. Quitting ends any that are. Their recordings stay in Runs." };
  }
  const agents = view.live.filter((item) => item.kind !== "update").map((item) => item.title);
  const updates = view.live.filter((item) => item.kind === "update").map((item) => `the ${item.title}`);
  const sentences: string[] = [];
  if (agents.length === 1) {
    sentences.push(`${agents[0]} is still running. Quitting ends it. Its recording stays in Runs, and you can resume it later.`);
  } else if (agents.length > 1) {
    sentences.push(
      `These sessions are still running: ${joinNames(agents)}. Quitting ends them. Their recordings stay in Runs, and you can resume them later.`
    );
  }
  if (updates.length > 0) {
    // At most one update runs at a time (S6), so this is nearly always "the Hermes update".
    const names = joinNames(updates);
    sentences.push(
      agents.length > 0
        ? `Quitting also stops ${names}.`
        : `${names.charAt(0).toUpperCase()}${names.slice(1)} ${updates.length === 1 ? "is" : "are"} still running. Quitting stops ${updates.length === 1 ? "it" : "them"}.`
    );
  }
  return { ...base, body: sentences.join(" ") };
}

export interface QuitFlow {
  // POST /api/sessions/quit-check.
  check: () => Promise<{ live: QuitCheckItem[] }>;
  // Draw (or redraw) the question.
  show: (view: QuitView) => void;
  // Tell the shell the question is on screen ("agentos://quit-shown"). Called at most once.
  shown: () => void;
  // Answer without asking (nothing would be lost).
  answer: (quit: boolean) => void;
  // false once the person has answered, so a late check changes nothing.
  isOpen: () => boolean;
}

type Checked = { live: QuitCheckItem[] } | null;

function within<T>(promise: Promise<T>, ms: number, late: T): Promise<T> {
  return new Promise<T>((resolve) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(late), ms);
    void promise.then((value) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve(value);
    });
  });
}

// What the window does when the shell asks to quit: quit at once when nothing runs; otherwise put the
// question on screen inside the shell's 2 s, naming the running sessions as soon as they are known.
export async function runQuitFlow(flow: QuitFlow): Promise<void> {
  const checked: Promise<Checked> = Promise.resolve()
    .then(() => flow.check())
    .then(
      (answer) => (answer && Array.isArray(answer.live) ? { live: answer.live } : null),
      () => null
    );
  const first = await within<Checked | "slow">(checked, QUIT_FAST_MS, "slow");
  if (!flow.isOpen()) return;
  if (first !== "slow") {
    if (first && first.live.length === 0) {
      flow.answer(true);
      return;
    }
    flow.show(first ? { phase: "asking", live: first.live } : { phase: "unknown" });
    flow.shown();
    return;
  }
  flow.show({ phase: "checking" });
  flow.shown();
  const later = await within<Checked>(checked, QUIT_CHECK_MS, null);
  if (!flow.isOpen()) return;
  if (later && later.live.length === 0) {
    flow.answer(true);
    return;
  }
  flow.show(later ? { phase: "asking", live: later.live } : { phase: "unknown" });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The terminal's WebSocket protocol, pure half (spec, WebSocket protocol)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Acknowledge at least every 64 KB received (and processed).
export const ACK_EVERY_BYTES = 64 * 1024;
// An {t:"in"} frame over 64 KB is refused, so every frame (JSON and all) stays at or under it.
export const MAX_IN_FRAME_BYTES = 64 * 1024;
export const RESIZE_DEBOUNCE_MS = 50;
export const MIN_COLS = 2;
export const MAX_COLS = 500;
export const MIN_ROWS = 1;
export const MAX_ROWS = 200;

export function validSize(cols: unknown, rows: unknown): boolean {
  return (
    typeof cols === "number" &&
    typeof rows === "number" &&
    Number.isInteger(cols) &&
    Number.isInteger(rows) &&
    cols >= MIN_COLS &&
    cols <= MAX_COLS &&
    rows >= MIN_ROWS &&
    rows <= MAX_ROWS
  );
}

// Bytes the text takes as UTF-8 (a lone surrogate counts 3, as TextEncoder writes U+FFFD).
export function utf8ByteLength(text: string): number {
  let bytes = 0;
  for (const ch of text) {
    const cp = ch.codePointAt(0) as number;
    bytes += cp < 0x80 ? 1 : cp < 0x800 ? 2 : cp < 0x10000 ? 3 : 4;
  }
  return bytes;
}

// Bytes one character takes inside a JSON string, as UTF-8.
function jsonBytes(cp: number): number {
  if (cp === 0x22 || cp === 0x5c) return 2; // \" and \\
  if (cp === 0x08 || cp === 0x09 || cp === 0x0a || cp === 0x0c || cp === 0x0d) return 2; // \b \t \n \f \r
  if (cp < 0x20) return 6; // \u001b and the other control characters
  if (cp >= 0xd800 && cp <= 0xdfff) return 6; // a lone surrogate is written as \udxxx
  return cp < 0x80 ? 1 : cp < 0x800 ? 2 : cp < 0x10000 ? 3 : 4;
}

const IN_FRAME_OVERHEAD = utf8ByteLength(JSON.stringify({ t: "in", d: "" }));

// Splits typed or pasted text into {t:"in"} frames of at most `maxFrameBytes` each, never inside a
// character (an emoji stays whole).
export function chunkInput(data: string, maxFrameBytes = MAX_IN_FRAME_BYTES): string[] {
  if (!data) return [];
  const budget = maxFrameBytes - IN_FRAME_OVERHEAD;
  const chunks: string[] = [];
  let current = "";
  let used = 0;
  for (const ch of data) {
    const size = jsonBytes(ch.codePointAt(0) as number);
    if (used + size > budget && current) {
      chunks.push(current);
      current = "";
      used = 0;
    }
    current += ch;
    used += size;
  }
  if (current) chunks.push(current);
  return chunks;
}

// Counts output that is on screen and says when to acknowledge it: once 64 KB more than the last ack.
export function createAckCounter(every = ACK_EVERY_BYTES) {
  let processed = 0;
  let acked = 0;
  return {
    // Output up to `seq` (cumulative UTF-8 bytes since the snapshot) is on screen. Returns the seq to
    // acknowledge now, or null.
    processed(seq: number): number | null {
      if (!Number.isFinite(seq) || seq <= processed) return null;
      processed = seq;
      if (processed - acked < every) return null;
      acked = processed;
      return processed;
    },
    // A fresh snapshot starts the count again at 0 (seq counts from 0 after each snapshot).
    reset() {
      processed = 0;
      acked = 0;
    }
  };
}

const MOUSE_TRACKING: readonly MouseTrackingMode[] = ["none", "x10", "vt200", "drag", "any"];
const MOUSE_ENCODING: readonly MouseEncodingMode[] = ["default", "sgr", "sgr-pixels"];

function oneOf<T extends string>(value: unknown, allowed: readonly T[], fallback: T): T {
  return (allowed as readonly unknown[]).includes(value) ? (value as T) : fallback;
}

// The snapshot's modes, every value checked; anything not allowed is off.
export function readModes(raw: unknown): SessionModes {
  const m = raw && typeof raw === "object" ? (raw as Record<string, unknown>) : {};
  const flags = m.kittyFlags;
  return {
    altScreen: m.altScreen === true,
    bracketedPaste: m.bracketedPaste === true,
    mouseTracking: oneOf(m.mouseTracking, MOUSE_TRACKING, "none"),
    mouseEncoding: oneOf(m.mouseEncoding, MOUSE_ENCODING, "default"),
    focusReporting: m.focusReporting === true,
    cursorKeysApp: m.cursorKeysApp === true,
    kittyFlags: typeof flags === "number" && Number.isInteger(flags) && flags >= 0 && flags <= 31 ? flags : 0
  };
}

const numberOrNull = (value: unknown): number | null => (typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value) ? value : null);
const textOrNull = (value: unknown): string | null => (typeof value === "string" && value ? value : null);

// One server frame, or null for anything that is not a well-formed frame (it is then ignored).
export function parseServerFrame(text: string): SessionServerFrame | null {
  let raw: unknown;
  try {
    raw = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object") return null;
  const f = raw as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (f.t === "snapshot") {
    if (typeof f.data !== "string" || !validSize(f.cols, f.rows)) return null;
    return { t: "snapshot", data: f.data, cols: f.cols as number, rows: f.rows as number, modes: readModes(f.modes) };
  }
  if (f.t === "out") {
    if (typeof f.d !== "string" || typeof f.seq !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(f.seq) || f.seq < 0) return null;
    return { t: "out", seq: f.seq, d: f.d };
  }
  if (f.t === "state") {
    if (!knownStatus(f.status)) return null;
    const endedBy = f.endedBy === "stop" || f.endedBy === "quit" ? f.endedBy : null;
    return { t: "state", status: f.status, exitCode: numberOrNull(f.exitCode), signal: textOrNull(f.signal), endedBy, resetAt: textOrNull(f.resetAt) };
  }
  if (f.t === "alert") return typeof f.raw === "string" ? { t: "alert", raw: f.raw } : null;
  return null;
}

// What a window does after the server closed its socket. S9's CLOSE_CODES give each reason word a number
// (too_far_behind 4000, session_ended 4001, attach_failed 4004), and the close reason text is that word.
// The word decides, never the number, so a changed number cannot make a window attach to an ended session.
// 1009 is ws's own close for a message over 1 MB and carries no word of Agent OS's: the one number read.
//   "reattach": attach again for a fresh snapshot (too far behind, a dropped connection, Agent OS restarting);
//   "ended":    the session ended; keep the last screen and never attach again;
//   "wait":     this window could not attach, or sent too much; do not try again at once.
export type SessionCloseAdvice = "reattach" | "ended" | "wait";

export function sessionCloseAdvice({ code, reason }: { code: number; reason: string }): SessionCloseAdvice {
  if (reason === "session_ended") return "ended";
  if (reason === "too_far_behind") return "reattach";
  if (reason === "attach_failed" || code === 1009) return "wait";
  return "reattach";
}
```

```ts
// Sessions (SP3): every request the shell and the pages make about sessions, each one with a time limit
// (withTimeout, planning decision Q31), and the WebSocket client for one session's terminal (spec,
// WebSocket protocol). The pure rules (frame sizes, acks, reading a frame) live in
// src/ui/sessionsShared.ts, where test/sessions-shared.test.js checks them.
import { ApiError, request } from "./api";
import type {
  QuitCheckResponse,
  RecordingListResponse,
  SessionClientFrame,
  SessionFolderList,
  SessionListResponse,
  SessionSettings,
  SessionSnapshot,
  SessionStateFrame,
  SessionSummary,
  StopSessionResult
} from "./types";
import { withTimeout } from "./ui/homeShared";
import { chunkInput, createAckCounter, parseServerFrame, RESIZE_DEBOUNCE_MS, sessionCloseAdvice, validSize } from "./ui/sessionsShared";
import type { SessionCloseAdvice } from "./ui/sessionsShared";

// How long each request may take before the page says Agent OS did not answer.
export const SESSION_LIMITS_MS = {
  list: 8000,
  // The server waits for the login-shell environment (up to 10 s, H2) before it starts the agent.
  create: 30000,
  // The soft stop (2 s) and the kill grace (3 s), with room to spare.
  stop: 15000,
  resume: 30000,
  dismiss: 10000,
  settings: 10000,
  folders: 10000,
  quitCheck: 8000,
  recordings: 10000,
  signedIn: 5000
} as const;

const TIMEOUT_WORDS = "Agent OS did not answer in time.";
const UNREADABLE = "Agent OS gave an answer that could not be read.";

const sessionPath = (sessionId: string, tail = "") => `/api/sessions/${encodeURIComponent(sessionId)}${tail}`;
const postJson = (body: unknown = {}): RequestInit => ({ method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body) });

export async function listSessions(): Promise<SessionListResponse> {
  const body = await withTimeout(request<SessionListResponse>("/api/sessions"), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.list);
  if (!body || !Array.isArray(body.sessions)) throw new Error(UNREADABLE);
  return body;
}

// `folder` is null for OpenClaw, which picks its own folder until spike S5. The server checks the folder
// (planning decision Q14) and answers 400 folder_refused with a sentence when it is not allowed.
export function createSession({ agentId, folder }: { agentId: string; folder: string | null }): Promise<SessionSummary> {
  return withTimeout(request<SessionSummary>("/api/sessions", postJson({ agentId, folder })), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.create);
}

export function stopSession(sessionId: string): Promise<StopSessionResult> {
  return withTimeout(request<StopSessionResult>(sessionPath(sessionId, "/stop"), postJson()), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.stop);
}

export function resumeSession(sessionId: string): Promise<SessionSummary> {
  return withTimeout(request<SessionSummary>(sessionPath(sessionId, "/resume"), postJson()), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.resume);
}

export function dismissSession(sessionId: string): Promise<SessionSummary> {
  return withTimeout(request<SessionSummary>(sessionPath(sessionId, "/dismiss"), postJson()), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.dismiss);
}

export function getSessionSettings(): Promise<SessionSettings> {
  return withTimeout(request<SessionSettings>("/api/sessions/settings"), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.settings);
}

export function putSessionSettings(patch: Partial<SessionSettings>): Promise<SessionSettings> {
  return withTimeout(
    request<SessionSettings>("/api/sessions/settings", { method: "PUT", body: JSON.stringify(patch) }),
    SESSION_LIMITS_MS.settings
  );
}

export function listSessionFolders(): Promise<SessionFolderList> {
  return withTimeout(request<SessionFolderList>("/api/sessions/folders"), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.folders);
}

// Every live session of both kinds, with its title, for the quit question (planning decision Q27).
export function quitCheck(): Promise<QuitCheckResponse> {
  return withTimeout(request<QuitCheckResponse>("/api/sessions/quit-check", postJson()), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.quitCheck);
}

export function listRecordings(): Promise<RecordingListResponse> {
  return withTimeout(request<RecordingListResponse>("/api/recordings"), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.recordings);
}

export function deleteRecording(sessionId: string): Promise<{ ok: true }> {
  return withTimeout(request<{ ok: true }>(sessionPath(sessionId, "/recording"), { method: "DELETE" }), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.recordings);
}

// Words for a refused or failed request: the server's own sentence when it sent one (Q14, Q15, Q25),
// otherwise a plain fallback.
export function sessionProblem(error: unknown): string {
  if (error instanceof ApiError) return error.detail || "Agent OS couldn't do that. Try again.";
  if (error instanceof Error && error.message === TIMEOUT_WORDS) return TIMEOUT_WORDS;
  return "Couldn't reach Agent OS.";
}

// True when a request got no answer at all (time limit or network): it may still have happened, so a page
// never says "nothing was changed" then, and reads the list again instead (Q31).
export function sessionGotNoAnswer(error: unknown): boolean {
  return !(error instanceof ApiError);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The WebSocket client for one session's terminal
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface SessionSocketClose {
  // 4000 too_far_behind, 4001 session_ended, 4004 attach_failed (S9's CLOSE_CODES), ws's 1009, or the
  // browser's own (1006 for a dropped connection). For logs; `advice` is what to act on.
  code: number;
  // The server's reason word: "too_far_behind", "session_ended" or "attach_failed" (empty when none came).
  reason: string;
  // false when the socket closed before its snapshot arrived (refused, or the server went away).
  hadSnapshot: boolean;
  // Decided by the reason word (sessionCloseAdvice): "reattach" (attach again for a fresh snapshot),
  // "ended" (never attach again) or "wait" (attach_failed or 1009: do not try again at once). A refused
  // upgrade (an ended or unknown session gets a bare 403) arrives as 1006 with no word, so "reattach" here
  // is only advice: the terminal (U2) attaches again only while the session list still says the session is
  // live (ruling R12).
  advice: SessionCloseAdvice;
}

export interface SessionSocketHandlers {
  // The first frame. A returned promise holds every later frame until it settles, so output never lands
  // before the restored screen.
  onSnapshot: (snapshot: SessionSnapshot) => void | Promise<void>;
  // A returned promise means "not on screen yet": the bytes count as processed (for acks) when it settles.
  onOut: (data: string) => void | Promise<void>;
  onState: (state: SessionStateFrame) => void;
  // SP3: the raw OSC 9 / 99 / 777 payload, or "bel".
  onAlert: (raw: string) => void;
  // Not called after close() from this side.
  onClose: (info: SessionSocketClose) => void;
}

export interface SessionSocket {
  // This terminal has the keys: it becomes the writer, and its size follows at once.
  focus(): void;
  // Keystrokes, paste and the terminal's own replies to terminal queries.
  input(data: string): void;
  resize(cols: number, rows: number): void;
  close(): void;
}

// Same host as the page; no query string and no token in the address (the session cookie goes with the
// upgrade; Security 1, planning decision Q40).
export function sessionSocketUrl(sessionId: string): string {
  const scheme = window.location.protocol === "https:" ? "wss:" : "ws:";
  return `${scheme}//${window.location.host}${sessionPath(sessionId, "/attach")}`;
}

// A socket that closes before its snapshot may mean the person is signed out: check, the way useRunStream does.
async function checkStillSignedIn(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const session = await withTimeout(request<{ authenticated?: boolean }>("/api/session"), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.signedIn);
    if (session && session.authenticated === false) window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("agentos:locked"));
  } catch {
    // A network hiccup here is not a sign-out.
  }
}

export function openSessionSocket(sessionId: string, handlers: SessionSocketHandlers): SessionSocket {
  const ws = new WebSocket(sessionSocketUrl(sessionId));
  const acks = createAckCounter();
  let closedHere = false;
  let hadSnapshot = false;
  // Settles once the snapshot is on screen; every later frame waits for it, in arrival order.
  let ready: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();
  let size: { cols: number; rows: number } | null = null;
  let sent: { cols: number; rows: number } | null = null;
  let resizeTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
  let focusWhenOpen = false;

  const send = (frame: SessionClientFrame): boolean => {
    if (ws.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return false;
    ws.send(JSON.stringify(frame));
    return true;
  };
  const cancelResize = () => {
    if (resizeTimer !== null) clearTimeout(resizeTimer);
    resizeTimer = null;
  };
  const sendSize = () => {
    cancelResize();
    if (size && send({ t: "resize", cols: size.cols, rows: size.rows })) sent = { ...size };
  };
  // {t:"focus"} makes this window the writer; its size follows right after it (spec).
  const takeKeys = () => {
    send({ t: "focus" });
    sendSize();
  };

  ws.onopen = () => {
    if (focusWhenOpen) {
      focusWhenOpen = false;
      takeKeys();
    }
  };

  ws.onmessage = (event: MessageEvent) => {
    if (closedHere || typeof event.data !== "string") return;
    const frame = parseServerFrame(event.data);
    if (!frame) return;
    if (frame.t === "snapshot") {
      // One snapshot per socket; a fresh one comes with a new socket.
      if (hadSnapshot) return;
      hadSnapshot = true;
      acks.reset();
      const snapshot: SessionSnapshot = { data: frame.data, cols: frame.cols, rows: frame.rows, modes: frame.modes };
      ready = Promise.resolve()
        .then(() => handlers.onSnapshot(snapshot))
        .then(
          () => undefined,
          () => undefined
        );
      return;
    }
    // The snapshot always comes first; anything earlier has no screen to land on.
    if (!hadSnapshot) return;
    if (frame.t === "out") {
      const seq = frame.seq;
      const data = frame.d;
      void ready
        .then(() => (closedHere ? undefined : handlers.onOut(data)))
        .then(() => {
          const ack = acks.processed(seq);
          if (ack !== null) send({ t: "ack", seq: ack });
        })
        .catch(() => undefined);
      return;
    }
    if (frame.t === "state") {
      const state: SessionStateFrame = { status: frame.status, exitCode: frame.exitCode, signal: frame.signal, endedBy: frame.endedBy, resetAt: frame.resetAt };
      void ready.then(() => {
        if (!closedHere) handlers.onState(state);
      });
      return;
    }
    const raw = frame.raw;
    void ready.then(() => {
      if (!closedHere) handlers.onAlert(raw);
    });
  };

  ws.onclose = (event: CloseEvent) => {
    cancelResize();
    if (closedHere) return;
    if (!hadSnapshot) void checkStillSignedIn();
    const reason = event.reason || "";
    handlers.onClose({ code: event.code, reason, hadSnapshot, advice: sessionCloseAdvice({ code: event.code, reason }) });
  };

  return {
    focus() {
      if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) takeKeys();
      else if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.CONNECTING) focusWhenOpen = true;
    },
    input(data: string) {
      for (const d of chunkInput(data)) send({ t: "in", d });
    },
    resize(cols: number, rows: number) {
      if (!validSize(cols, rows)) return;
      size = { cols, rows };
      cancelResize();
      if (sent && sent.cols === cols && sent.rows === rows) return;
      resizeTimer = setTimeout(() => {
        resizeTimer = null;
        sendSize();
      }, RESIZE_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    },
    close() {
      closedHere = true;
      cancelResize();
      try {
        ws.close(1000, "closed");
      } catch {
        // Already closed.
      }
    }
  };
}
```

export function queryParam(name: string) {
  return new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get(name) || "";
}

export function navigateTo(page: string, extra: Record<string, string> = {}) {
  const next = new URL(window.location.href);
  next.searchParams.set("page", page);
  // `step` picks a Setup step (check, plan, install, brain, signin, ready) and
  // `example` asks the Runs page to open the New run dialog with the safe example typed in.
  // `session` picks a Sessions tab, `tab` a page's own tab (Runs: "recordings") and `highlight` the row
  // to mark there ("Open recording" lands on its session's row).
  for (const key of ["file", "folder", "filter", "agent", "run", "room", "step", "example", "session", "tab", "highlight"]) {
    if (extra[key]) next.searchParams.set(key, extra[key]);
    else next.searchParams.delete(key);
  }
  window.history.replaceState({}, "", next);
  window.dispatchEvent(new Event("aos-navigate"));
}

- [ ] **Step 8: One shared sessions poll (Q30).** Create `src/ui/useSessionsList.ts` (a `.ts` file, so the provider uses `createElement` rather than JSX; the path and the `{ source, available, refresh }` shape are what Task U3 consumes):

```ts
// One shared read of GET /api/sessions for the whole shell (planning decision Q30): the menu's sessions
// count, Home and the Sessions page all read this one list, so they never disagree for longer than a poll.
// It asks every 5 s (paused while the window is hidden, useInterval), one read at a time with the newest
// answer winning (latestRead.ts), and every read has a time limit (sessionsApi.ts). After a good read, a
// failed one keeps the last good list marked stale (homeShared.ts Source), so a page can show it under a
// warn note instead of wiping it. Where sessions do not exist (the public demo, the public mode), the server
// answers 404 not_available and `available` turns false, so a page says so instead of "Can't reach Agent OS".
import { createContext, createElement, useCallback, useContext, useEffect, useMemo, useState } from "react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { ApiError } from "../api";
import { listSessions, sessionProblem } from "../sessionsApi";
import type { SessionListResponse } from "../types";
import { useInterval } from "./components/useInterval";
import { failedLoad, loaded } from "./homeShared";
import type { Source } from "./homeShared";
import { createLatestRead } from "./latestRead";
import { runningSessionCount } from "./sessionsShared";

export const SESSIONS_POLL_MS = 5000;
const NOT_AVAILABLE = "Sessions are not available here.";

export interface SessionsList {
  source: Source<SessionListResponse>;
  // false where sessions do not exist (the server answered 404 not_available, or the public demo).
  available: boolean;
  // Read again now (after Start, Stop, Resume or Dismiss). The same function on every render; a read still
  // waiting no longer counts.
  refresh: () => void;
}

const OFF: SessionsList = { source: { state: "error", message: NOT_AVAILABLE }, available: false, refresh: () => undefined };

const SessionsListContext = createContext<SessionsList>(OFF);

export function useSessionsList(): SessionsList {
  return useContext(SessionsListContext);
}

// How many agent sessions are running, for the menu. null while that is not known: still loading, or the
// last read failed (a stale number is never shown).
export function useLiveSessionCount(): number | null {
  const { source } = useSessionsList();
  if (source.state !== "ok" || source.stale) return null;
  return runningSessionCount(source.data.sessions);
}

function isNotAvailable(error: unknown): boolean {
  return error instanceof ApiError && error.status === 404 && error.message === "not_available";
}

export function SessionsListProvider({ enabled, children }: { enabled: boolean; children: ReactNode }) {
  const [source, setSource] = useState<Source<SessionListResponse>>({ state: "loading" });
  const [available, setAvailable] = useState(true);
  const [reads] = useState(createLatestRead);

  const load = useCallback(
    (fresh: boolean) => {
      if (!enabled) return;
      if (fresh) reads.cancel();
      void reads.run(
        () => listSessions(),
        (outcome) => {
          if (outcome.ok) {
            setAvailable(true);
            setSource(loaded(outcome.value));
            return;
          }
          if (isNotAvailable(outcome.error)) {
            setAvailable(false);
            setSource({ state: "error", message: NOT_AVAILABLE });
            return;
          }
          setSource((prev) => failedLoad(prev, sessionProblem(outcome.error)));
        }
      );
    },
    [enabled, reads]
  );

  useEffect(() => {
    load(true);
    // A read still waiting when the shell goes away must not update it.
    return () => reads.cancel();
  }, [load, reads]);
  useInterval(() => load(false), enabled ? SESSIONS_POLL_MS : null);

  const refresh = useCallback(() => load(true), [load]);
  const value = useMemo<SessionsList>(() => (enabled ? { source, available, refresh } : OFF), [enabled, source, available, refresh]);
  return createElement(SessionsListContext.Provider, { value }, children);
}
```

Create `src/ui/components/QuitQuestion.tsx`:

```tsx
// The quit question (desktop app only; spec "Quitting Agent OS", planning decision Q6). Instead of quitting
// at once, the Rust shell tells this window "agentos://quit-requested". The window asks Agent OS which
// sessions are running (both kinds) and either answers "quit" straight away, when nothing would be lost, or
// shows this question, tells the shell "agentos://quit-shown", and then sends the person's answer as
// "agentos://quit-answer" { quit }. If no window says quit-shown within 2 s, the shell quits on its own.
// The Tauri event module is imported lazily, so a browser tab never loads it.
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { quitCheck } from "../../sessionsApi";
import { isDesktopApp } from "../desktop";
import { QUIT_ANSWER_EVENT, QUIT_REQUESTED_EVENT, QUIT_SHOWN_EVENT, quitQuestionCopy, runQuitFlow } from "../sessionsShared";
import type { QuitView } from "../sessionsShared";
import AgentConfirmModal from "./AgentConfirmModal";

async function tellShell(event: string, payload?: unknown): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const { emit } = await import("@tauri-apps/api/event");
    await emit(event, payload);
  } catch {
    // Not inside the desktop shell after all (a browser tab with ?desktop=1): there is nobody to tell.
  }
}

export interface DesktopQuit {
  view: QuitView | null;
  keepRunning: () => void;
  quit: () => void;
}

export function useDesktopQuit(): DesktopQuit {
  const [view, setView] = useState<QuitView | null>(null);
  // True from the shell's request until an answer is sent; a second request in between changes nothing.
  const open = useRef(false);

  const answer = useCallback((quit: boolean) => {
    open.current = false;
    setView(null);
    void tellShell(QUIT_ANSWER_EVENT, { quit });
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isDesktopApp()) return undefined;
    let unlisten: (() => void) | null = null;
    let gone = false;
    function onQuitRequested() {
      if (open.current) return;
      open.current = true;
      void runQuitFlow({
        check: () => quitCheck(),
        show: (next) => {
          if (open.current) setView(next);
        },
        shown: () => void tellShell(QUIT_SHOWN_EVENT),
        answer,
        isOpen: () => open.current
      });
    }
    import("@tauri-apps/api/event")
      .then(({ listen }) => listen(QUIT_REQUESTED_EVENT, onQuitRequested))
      .then((stop) => {
        if (gone) stop();
        else unlisten = stop;
      })
      .catch(() => {
        // Not inside the desktop shell after all: nothing will ask.
      });
    return () => {
      gone = true;
      unlisten?.();
    };
  }, [answer]);

  return { view, keepRunning: () => answer(false), quit: () => answer(true) };
}

// `quitLabel` names the button that ends the sessions: "Quit" by default, "Install & restart" from the update
// banner (its restart quits Agent OS too, and the shell cannot ask on that path; see UpdateBanner.tsx).
export default function QuitQuestion({
  view,
  onKeepRunning,
  onQuit,
  quitLabel
}: {
  view: QuitView;
  onKeepRunning: () => void;
  onQuit: () => void;
  quitLabel?: string;
}) {
  const copy = quitQuestionCopy(view);
  // Focus starts on Keep running (the first button), so Enter never quits by accident; Escape keeps running.
  return (
    <AgentConfirmModal
      title={copy.title}
      cancelLabel={copy.keep}
      confirmLabel={quitLabel ?? copy.quit}
      onConfirm={onQuit}
      onClose={onKeepRunning}
      danger
      closeOnBackdrop={false}
    >
      <p aria-live="polite">{copy.body}</p>
    </AgentConfirmModal>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 11: Ask before an update restarts Agent OS.** The banner's "Install & restart" calls `downloadAndInstall()` and then `relaunch()`. That restart quits Agent OS and ends every running session, and the shell cannot ask on that path: it leaves with `RESTART_EXIT_CODE`, which `prevent_exit()` ignores (decision Q5b). So the banner asks first, with the quit question (ruling R19, decision D-U1-9). Replace the whole of `src/ui/components/UpdateBanner.tsx` with:

```tsx
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { ArrowUpCircle } from "lucide-react";
import type { Update } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-updater";
import { quitCheck } from "../../sessionsApi";
import type { QuitView } from "../sessionsShared";
import QuitQuestion from "./QuitQuestion";
import "../updateBanner.css";

// Only the desktop app has an updater. The Rust shell opens the window with
// ?desktop=1; window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__ is the fallback marker.
function isDesktopApp(): boolean {
  if (typeof window === "undefined") return false;
  if (new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("desktop") === "1") return true;
  return "__TAURI_INTERNALS__" in window;
}

const CHECK_EVERY_MS = 4 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
const LOG_PREFIX = "[agent-os updater]";

// "checking": asking Agent OS which sessions run, before anything is downloaded.
type Phase = "ready" | "checking" | "installing" | "failed";

// A slim notice that appears only when a newer desktop build exists. It never
// installs or restarts on its own: running agents may be mid-task, so the
// user has to click "Install & restart". That restart quits Agent OS and ends
// every session, and the shell cannot ask first on this path (an approved
// restart leaves with RESTART_EXIT_CODE, which the shell's quit question cannot
// hold; see desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs). So the banner asks first, with the
// same quit question, whenever a session runs or Agent OS does not answer.
export default function UpdateBanner() {
  const desktop = isDesktopApp();
  const [update, setUpdate] = useState<Update | null>(null);
  const [phase, setPhase] = useState<Phase>("ready");
  const [notesOpen, setNotesOpen] = useState(false);
  // The quit question while it asks before the restart, otherwise null.
  const [ask, setAsk] = useState<QuitView | null>(null);
  const installingRef = useRef(false);

  const checkForUpdate = useCallback(async () => {
    if (installingRef.current) return;
    try {
      // Lazy import: the plain browser build never loads the Tauri packages.
      const { check } = await import("@tauri-apps/plugin-updater");
      const found = await check();
      if (found) setUpdate(found);
    } catch (error) {
      // Expected until the app has a signing key and an update feed; kept
      // out of the UI so it never nags, but visible in the console.
      console.warn(`${LOG_PREFIX} update check failed:`, error);
    }
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!desktop) return undefined;
    void checkForUpdate();
    const timer = window.setInterval(() => void checkForUpdate(), CHECK_EVERY_MS);
    return () => window.clearInterval(timer);
  }, [desktop, checkForUpdate]);

  // Downloads, installs and relaunches. Reached only when nothing runs, or from the question's "Install & restart".
  async function installNow() {
    if (!update) return;
    setAsk(null);
    setPhase("installing");
    try {
      await update.downloadAndInstall();
      const { relaunch } = await import("@tauri-apps/plugin-process");
      await relaunch();
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`${LOG_PREFIX} install failed:`, error);
      installingRef.current = false;
      setPhase("failed");
    }
  }

  async function install() {
    if (!update || installingRef.current) return;
    installingRef.current = true;
    setPhase("checking");
    // Every live session of both kinds, with its title (POST /api/sessions/quit-check, with its time limit).
    const check = await quitCheck().catch(() => null);
    if (!check || !Array.isArray(check.live)) {
      // No answer: say so plainly and let the person choose.
      setPhase("ready");
      setAsk({ phase: "unknown" });
      return;
    }
    if (check.live.length > 0) {
      setPhase("ready");
      setAsk({ phase: "asking", live: check.live });
      return;
    }
    // Nothing running, so nothing would be lost: install at once, as before.
    await installNow();
  }

  // Keep running: nothing was downloaded or restarted, and the banner is back as it was.
  function keepRunning() {
    setAsk(null);
    installingRef.current = false;
    setPhase("ready");
  }

  if (!desktop || !update) return null;
  const notes = (update.body || "").trim();

  return (
    <>
      <div className="os-update" role="status" aria-live="polite">
        <div className="os-update__bar">
          <ArrowUpCircle size={16} className="os-update__icon" aria-hidden="true" />
          <span className="os-update__text">
            {phase === "failed"
              ? "The update didn't install. Nothing was changed; you can try again."
              : `Agent OS ${update.version} is ready to install`}
          </span>
          {notes ? (
            <button className="os-update__link" onClick={() => setNotesOpen((open) => !open)} aria-expanded={notesOpen}>
              What&apos;s new
            </button>
          ) : null}
          <button
            className="os-btn os-btn--primary os-update__action"
            onClick={() => void install()}
            disabled={phase === "checking" || phase === "installing" || ask !== null}
          >
            {phase === "checking" ? "Checking…" : phase === "installing" ? "Installing…" : phase === "failed" ? "Try again" : "Install & restart"}
          </button>
        </div>
        {notesOpen && notes ? <pre className="os-update__notes">{notes}</pre> : null}
      </div>
      {/* Outside .os-update: that wrapper ignores the pointer and is its own layer (updateBanner.css), so a
          dialog inside it could not be clicked or sit above the page. */}
      {ask ? <QuitQuestion view={ask} quitLabel="Install & restart" onKeepRunning={keepRunning} onQuit={() => void installNow()} /> : null}
    </>
  );
}
```

What changes for the person: with no session running, "Install & restart" works exactly as before (after a check that usually takes a few milliseconds). With sessions running, the quit question names them first, and only its "Install & restart" downloads and restarts; "Keep running" (or Escape) leaves everything as it was. If Agent OS does not answer the check, the question says it couldn't check, and the person chooses.
